_Last updated: 2026-08-24 — **Office Inventory Management, Workstream 7 — Stocktaking: shipped.** Built exactly to the frozen plan (`docs/OFFICE_INVENTORY_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` §7.8, §28, §29, Owner Decision 14, §47, §50) — **no W8 ESS/Department-Head UX exists yet; no new backend authority beyond what this workstream itself needed. Office Inventory not enabled for WWM or any organization, production untouched.** **Core principle preserved:** a physical count is never substituted for system stock — every non-zero variance requires an explicit resolution, live-proven end-to-end via a single comprehensive 6-item stocktake session covering every required scenario in one internally-consistent narrative (snapshot capture, post-snapshot issue and receipt correctly explained away as zero variance, a true shortage and a true surplus each resolved via adjustment, a recount resolving a variance to zero with no ledger effect, a shortage resolved via the store-side "missing" path, incomplete-count and unresolved-variance rejections at the right moments, and a clean successful finalization). **Stocktake model (§7.8):** two new tables, `office_inventory_stocktakes` (header: store, reference, `draft|counting|finalized`, started/finalized actor+timestamp, notes) and `office_inventory_stocktake_lines` (one row per in-scope item: `expectedQuantitySnapshot`, `countedQuantity`, `variance`, `resolutionType` `recount|adjustment|missing`, `resolutionMovementId`). **Disclosed interpretation:** the frozen schema's own three-status lifecycle (rather than two) is read as a genuine `draft` (store chosen, nothing snapshotted) preceding a separate, explicit `start` action that both populates every in-scope line AND captures the snapshot atomically — not creation-equals-start. **Stocktake lines:** one row per item with ANY movement history in the store (not merely a currently non-zero balance), so a fully-issued, zero-balance item required for control is never silently excluded; a unique `(stocktakeId, itemId)` index prevents duplicate lines. **Snapshot-at-start:** `expectedQuantitySnapshot` is captured, once, the instant a stocktake transitions draft→counting, and is never rewritten by any later movement — live-proven (the original 100/50 snapshot values for two items remained byte-identical after a subsequent issue and receipt against those same items). **Post-snapshot movement reconciliation:** `reconciledExpectedQuantity = expectedQuantitySnapshot + movementsSinceSnapshot`, where `movementsSinceSnapshot` is a fresh, live, batched SQL sum over every ledger row for that item/store strictly after the stocktake's own `startedAt` — a legitimate issue or receipt occurring during an open count is therefore correctly explained away rather than surfacing as unexplained variance, live-proven for BOTH an outbound (issue, -10) and an inbound (receipt, +5) case in the same session. **Expected vs counted model:** the physical count is always compared against the reconciled (movement-adjusted) expected quantity, never the raw snapshot directly. **Variance model:** `variance = countedQuantity − reconciledExpectedQuantity`, computed via the same BigInt/minor-units arithmetic used throughout this module (zero native floating-point). **Zero variance:** finalizable without any resolution record at all — no artificial adjustment is ever required, live-proven for two items whose counts matched their reconciled expectation exactly. **Recount:** a plain re-submission of `countedQuantity`; when it brings a previously non-zero variance to exactly zero, `resolutionType` is set to `recount` automatically — no separate action, no stock movement, live-proven (store balance byte-identical before and after). **Adjustment resolution:** a thin, direct pass-through to Workstream 6's own existing `adjustStore` (direction/quantity derived from the freshly-recomputed variance's own sign/magnitude, never trusted from an earlier read) — live-proven for both a shortage (-3, `adjustment_out`) and a surplus (+3, `adjustment_in`) in the same session, each correctly reflected in the store balance and each line's `resolutionMovementId`. **Missing resolution — the single most architecturally significant decision this workstream made:** the frozen schema's own `resolutionMovementId` field (a ledger movement id, NOT an incident id) settled a genuine ambiguity in favor of activating the STORE-side `missing` movement type — already present in Workstream 2's own original direction table but never produced by any code path until now — via a new, W6-file-owned `markStoreMissing` function mirroring `adjustStore`'s exact shape, rather than routing through Workstream 6's HOLDER-scoped incident/mark-missing pipeline (which has no store concept at all and could not represent a store-level physical-count discrepancy). Disclosed explicitly as a reuse of W6's own movement type/semantics/shape, not a second missing-item engine. Live-proven: a -5 shortage resolved as `missing` produced a genuine store-decreasing `missing` ledger row referencing the stocktake line via `sourceReferenceType='stocktake_line'`. **Finalization rules:** requires every line counted AND every fresh, live-recomputed non-zero variance resolved — rejected with the exact list of blocking lines (and their reason: `not_counted` or `unresolved_variance`) otherwise, live-proven at both checkpoints (0-of-6 counted; then 4-of-6 still blocking after two of six were deliberately left unresolved). A line's stored `resolutionType` is cleared back to null the instant a fresh recompute shows a reopened non-zero variance, so a stale resolution can never quietly cover for a newer discrepancy. Finalization itself never appends a ledger row — every stock effect a stocktake ever causes already happened through an explicit adjustment/missing action, strictly before finalization succeeds. **Finalization immutability:** live-proven — count, resolve, start, and re-finalize are all rejected once a stocktake is finalized; a subsequent ordinary movement against the same store/item changes current stock normally while the finalized stocktake's own historical snapshot/count/variance remain byte-identical. **Concurrent store operations:** normal receiving/issue/return/transfer/adjustment are never blocked by an open stocktake, exactly as frozen — `startStocktake` acquires the same advisory-lock domain an ordinary movement would (§28's own explicit requirement), serializing only the brief snapshot-read moment, never a store-wide freeze. **Finalization concurrency:** a finalize-vs-issue and a finalize-vs-receipt race were both live-proven coherent (the concurrent movement always succeeds; finalize either succeeds and the movement becomes an ordinary post-finalization event, or is correctly rejected as newly-incomplete — never an uncaught error either way); a genuine double-finalization race resolved to exactly one winner with exactly one audit event. **Count concurrency:** two genuinely simultaneous count submissions for the same line both succeed (recount is an ordinary, expected operation, serialized — not rejected — by the line's own row lock), with the final persisted value always exactly one of the two submitted counts, never a corrupted hybrid. **Permissions:** zero new keys — the single frozen `office_inventory.stocktake` key gates every stocktake action, including the internal adjustment/missing resolution calls (a Stocktake operator needs no separate `.adjust`/`.writeoff` grant to resolve their own session's variances). **Authorization:** every route composes `requireAuth → requireMembership → requireModuleEnabled → requirePermission`. **Audit:** `office_inventory_stocktake.created`/`.started`/`.finalized`, `office_inventory_stocktake_line.counted`/`.resolved` — all live-proven to fire correctly, with no duplicate Workstream 6 adjustment/write-off audit event suppressed (both domains legitimately fire their own). **Database/migration:** migration `0054` — exactly two new tables, `office_inventory_stocktakes`/`_stocktake_lines` (both RLS-enabled, zero policies, confirmed via direct query); every other schema element this workstream needed (the `missing` store-decreasing enum value, `sourceReferenceType='stocktake_line'`) already existed since earlier workstreams. Organization config gained one new, purely additive `stocktakeNumber` series (explicitly named in the frozen plan's own §40 enumeration). **API/OpenAPI/codegen:** 7 new endpoints; codegen run twice, byte-identical, zero duplicate operationIds; no generic status-PATCH, no generic ledger writer — re-confirmed by a permanent architectural test. **Frontend:** one new "Stocktakes" tab (status-filterable queue, a Create Stocktake dialog, and a per-stocktake detail panel showing snapshot/movements-since/reconciled-expected/counted/variance per line with inline count-entry, Start, adjustment/missing resolution, and Finalize actions) — operational-first surface, not the full ESS/Department-Head experience or any dashboard/reporting surface reserved for later workstreams. **Automated tests:** 30 new focused backend tests across 2 files (an architectural no-generic-write-route proof and an HTTP-boundary authorization suite covering all 7 routes) — full backend regression 120/120 files, 2214/2214 tests; frontend regression 64/64 files, 714/714 tests; full workspace typecheck clean; all 3 production builds clean; OpenAPI codegen deterministic across two independent runs; zero schema drift beyond migration `0054` itself. **Live development QA (disposable fixtures, WWM never touched):** 59/59 checks passed against the real development database via the actual lib functions, across two scripts — 38/38 (the complete single-session narrative above: snapshot correctness, post-snapshot issue/receipt reconciliation, incomplete-count and unresolved-variance rejection, true shortage/surplus, recount, adjustment resolution for both directions, missing resolution, successful finalization, and full finalization immutability plus a correctly-unaffected post-finalization movement) and 21/21 (all four mandated concurrency races, cross-org isolation across all four mutating actions, every expected audit event, the WWM boundary, and a structural no-Procurement-table verification). **Issues found:** one Category A product defect, caught by this workstream's own live QA — the reconciliation cutoff (`startedAt`) was captured using the APPLICATION server's clock (`new Date()`) while every ledger row's own `occurredAt` default is computed by the DATABASE server's clock (Postgres `now()`); this environment's own Node process and Postgres host were confirmed to differ by a genuine ~9.5-second skew, which meant a receipt that had already happened, in true wall-clock time, seconds before a stocktake was started could still appear to have occurred AFTER the snapshot cutoff — silently pulling an already-snapshotted quantity back into "movements since snapshot" and corrupting the reconciled expected value (a receive-100-then-issue-10 scenario showed a movements-since figure of +90, the sum of BOTH events, instead of the correct -10). **Fixed** by capturing `startedAt` via SQL `now()` inside the same transaction that captures the snapshot, so the cutoff and every `occurredAt` value are always drawn from the identical clock regardless of any app/DB skew; re-verified live (the full 38-check business script re-run clean afterward, including the exact post-snapshot reconciliation figures) and the full backend suite re-confirmed clean (120/120, 2214/2214). **RLS/security (freshly queried, not copied from W6):** 121 public tables (119 + the two new stocktake tables), 100% RLS-enabled, zero policies anywhere. **Documentation:** this `PROJECT_STATUS.md` entry only; `ROADMAP.md`/`MODULES.md` not edited — Office Inventory is not marked complete. **WWM boundary:** independently re-verified live — no WWM `office_inventory` module override, zero WWM stocktake rows, zero WWM stocktake-linked movement rows. **Production:** untouched throughout. **Office Inventory status:** W1 complete, W2 complete, W3 complete, W4 complete, W5 complete, W6 complete, W7 — Stocktaking — complete. Live-proven both ways: authorized by the receiving Head succeeds; attempted by a non-Head/non-delegate is rejected; attempted by the *sending* department's own Head (the wrong Head) is also correctly rejected. **Store transfer model (§23):** a single atomic paired `transferred_out`/`transferred_in` movement — both movement types already existed in Workstream 2's own store direction table (unused until now), so no direction-table change was needed for transfers at all. Live-proven against the frozen plan's own exact numeric example: Store A=100, Store B=20, transfer 30 → Store A=70, Store B=50, organization total unchanged at 120. **Transfer lock ordering (§16):** a new `acquireOrderedStoreLocks` sorts the two store keys before acquiring, so a transfer A→B can never deadlock against a concurrent transfer B→A; a matching `acquireOrderedHolderLocks` does the same for handovers, and a new `acquireStoreThenHolderLock` gives returns the identical store-then-holder lock order Workstream 4's own issue functions already use by construction — without this, a return (which touches both a store and a holder domain, like issue does) could deadlock against a concurrent issue for the same item under real contention (§17's own Issue-vs-Return race requirement). **Consumable boundary (§24):** return and handover of a `consumable`-classified item are both strictly rejected — issuing a consumable is itself its consumption (Owner Decision 10), never reversible or transferable; live-proven for both actions. **Custody derivation:** `getHolderBalance`/`listCurrentCustody` correctly aggregate across issue → partial return → full return → handover chains of arbitrary length, live-proven via the full accountability-chain scenario above. **Overdue (§20):** extended `listCurrentCustody`'s response shape (additively — a Workstream-4-compatible, non-breaking change) with live-derived `overdue`/`expectedReturnDate` fields, computed via a batched (no N+1) `SELECT DISTINCT ON` over the most recent holder-increasing row per item — a handover's own destination row is itself such a row, so a handover correctly becomes the new "most recent" and supersedes whatever due date the previous holder was tracking, live-proven; overdue remains true after a partial return while outstanding quantity remains, and clears entirely (the item no longer appears in the custody listing at all) once the full outstanding quantity is returned. **Request-history immutability (§27):** live-proven — a request line's `approvedQuantity`/`quantityIssuedSoFar` and the header's `fulfilled` status are completely unaffected by a later return; _Last updated: 2026-08-23 — **Office Inventory Management, Workstream 3 — Requests, Department Approval & Delegation: shipped.** Built exactly to the frozen plan (`docs/OFFICE_INVENTORY_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` §5.3, §6, §7.4, §10, §11, §14, §15, §47, §50) — **no issue/fulfilment exists yet (Workstream 4's own scope); approval never touches the stock ledger, proven both architecturally (a permanent test asserts `officeInventoryRequests.ts`/`officeInventoryDelegations.ts` import nothing from the ledger/receiving modules) and live (movement count byte-identical before/after a full request→approval cycle). Office Inventory not enabled for WWM or any organization, production untouched.** **Request model:** `office_inventory_requests` + `office_inventory_request_lines` — employee requests resolve `forEmployeeId` exclusively via `resolveOwnEmployeeId` (never client-supplied) and `forDepartmentId` from the employee's own current department (an employee with no department cannot submit one — a controlled 400, never a silent fallback); department requests require the submitter to themselves belong to the target department (a disclosed interpretation — the frozen plan does not explicitly restrict this, but leaving it fully open would be an undisclosed authorization gap). Header `status` is recomputed after every line decision from a disclosed derivation rule (all-pending → pending; all-approved → approved; all-rejected → rejected; any mix → partially_approved) — never manually set. Cancellation (present in the frozen schema's own `cancelled`/`cancelledAt`/`cancelledByMembershipId` fields) is implemented as requester-only, pending-only, per a disclosed reasonable interpretation absent explicit frozen prose. **Department Head authority:** every approval action re-resolves authority live via `resolveApprovalAuthority` — either the department's actual current Head (via W1's own `getCurrentDepartmentHead`) or a currently-valid delegate — permission alone is never sufficient, matching the frozen instruction exactly; a vacant department (no current Head) permanently blocks approval with no HR/org_admin fallback, live-proven. **Self-approval is permanently valid** — a Head submitting and approving their own request is ordinary, audited normally, `actedAsDelegate: false`, live-proven. **Delegation:** `office_inventory_approval_delegations`, half-open interval, only the department's current Head may create/revoke/view (enforced, not merely permission-gated); the load-bearing §5.3 rule — a delegation surviving its delegating Head's own replacement becomes functionally inert for NEW approvals while the row itself remains open and fully historically queryable — is live-proven, including the specific historical-authority scenario (a pre-replacement delegated approval remains permanently attributed to the original delegate). **Approval authority snapshot:** every line decision permanently records `approvedByMembershipId`/`actedAsDelegate`/`delegatorHeadMembershipId`/`delegationId`, never rewritten by a later Head/delegation change. **Full/partial approval and rejection:** approved quantity must be `> 0` and `<= quantityRequested`; multi-line requests support fully independent per-line outcomes (live-proven: 4-of-10 approved alongside a separate rejected line on the same request). **Repeat-request warning:** query-time only (never a stored flag), truthfully derived only from recent request history (no fabricated issue/custody data — Workstream 4's own concern, added later without a breaking API change), non-blocking (an approver can and did approve despite an active warning). **Permissions:** zero new keys — reuses exactly 3 of the frozen 23 (`office_inventory.request`, `office_inventory.approve`, `office_inventory.delegate.manage`). **Authorization:** every route composes `requireAuth → requireMembership → requireModuleEnabled → requirePermission`, with the Head-or-delegate relationship additionally enforced server-side wherever the frozen plan requires it (never assumed from the permission grant alone) — live-proven, including that a non-Head/non-delegate holding `.approve` still cannot approve someone else's department's request. **Audit:** `office_inventory_request.submitted`/`.cancelled`, `office_inventory_request_line.approved`/`.rejected`, `office_inventory_delegation.created`/`.revoked` — all live-proven to fire correctly. **Database/migration:** migration `0052` (3 tables — `office_inventory_requests`, `office_inventory_request_lines`, `office_inventory_approval_delegations` — all RLS-enabled with zero policies), applied to the development database only; zero schema drift confirmed before and after. **API/OpenAPI/codegen:** 11 new endpoints; codegen run twice, byte-identical, zero duplicate operationIds; no generic status-PATCH endpoint anywhere — every state change is a dedicated action route. **Frontend:** two new tabs on `/office-inventory` — "My Requests" (create employee/department request, list, detail/cancel) and "Approvals" (department picker, approval queue, full approval-context screen showing store availability and the repeat-request warning, approve/partial/reject actions, delegation management) — no issue/fulfilment/confirmation/return/handover/incident/stocktake surface exists. **Automated tests:** 41 new focused backend tests across 3 files (header-status derivation, the architectural no-ledger-import proof, delegation authority resolution including the load-bearing Head-replacement-inertness rule, and an HTTP-boundary authorization suite) — full backend regression 112/112 files, 2100/2100 tests; frontend regression 64/64 files, 714/714 tests; full workspace typecheck clean; all 3 production builds clean. **Live development QA (disposable fixtures, WWM never touched):** 32/32 checks passed against the real development database via the actual lib functions, covering the frozen plan's own full 24-item checklist (§37) — employee/department requests, unauthorized-approval denial, Head approval, Head self-approval, partial approval, rejection, delegate creation/approval/revocation, Head replacement with the old delegate correctly denied for new approvals while the historical approval remains intact, the repeat-request warning shown-but-non-blocking, live store availability in the approval context, zero ledger effect, cross-org isolation (both employee/item and department), every expected audit event, two genuine concurrency races, and the WWM boundary. **Concurrency:** a 3-way simultaneous approve/approve/reject race on one line (exactly one winner, via the frozen `FOR UPDATE` row-lock pattern) and a Head-vs-delegate race approving two DIFFERENT lines of the same request (both succeed independently, no false conflict) — both executed as genuinely simultaneous requests, not sequential simulation. **Issues found:** one Category A product defect, caught by this workstream's own live concurrency QA (not by the mocked test suite, which never happened to construct the triggering fixture) — `resolveApprovalAuthority` queried for "any open delegation row for this delegate" and could non-deterministically return a stale, inert row from a FORMER Head instead of the genuinely valid row from the CURRENT Head, since the frozen schema's own unique constraint is per-delegating-Head, not per-delegate, so the same delegate can legitimately hold two simultaneously-open rows after a Head replacement. **Fixed** by filtering directly on `delegatingHeadMembershipId = currentHead.headMembershipId` in the query itself rather than checking after the fact; a permanent regression test reproducing the exact dual-open-row scenario was added; the fix was independently re-verified live (32/32, including the specific race that first caught it) and the full backend suite re-confirmed clean (112/112, 2100/2100) afterward. **RLS/security (freshly queried):** 118 public tables, 100% RLS-enabled, zero policies anywhere. **Documentation:** this `PROJECT_STATUS.md` entry only; _Last updated: 2026-08-23 — **Office Inventory Management, Workstream 2 — Stock Ledger & Receiving: shipped.** Built exactly to the frozen plan (`docs/OFFICE_INVENTORY_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` §7.3, §8, §9, §40, §47, §50) — the authoritative append-only stock ledger, the advisory-lock-based balance/custody derivation engine, and receiving. **No requests/approval/issue exist yet — receiving is the only movement type any code path can produce. Office Inventory not enabled for WWM or any organization, production untouched.** **Ledger:** `office_inventory_stock_movements` — append-only (no application code anywhere UPDATEs or DELETEs a row; enforced by this file being the sole write-owner and exposing no such function, disclosed consistently with the platform's established app-layer-invariant convention rather than a DB trigger). Current store balance is derived LIVE via SQL `SUM` over a signed-quantity `CASE` expression keyed on a single, centrally-defined movement-direction table (increasing: `received`/`transferred_in`/`adjustment_in`/`returned`/`recovered`; decreasing: `issued`/`transferred_out`/`adjustment_out`/`written_off`/`missing`/`asset_handoff`) — never a persisted balance column. Workstream 2 populates only `received` rows; every other enum value exists in the schema now so later workstreams need no redesign. **Concurrency:** every store-balance-affecting append acquires `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('org:item:store'))` — reusing the exact mechanism `payrollRuns.ts`/`payrollPeriods.ts` already prove for period/run-creation races — before resolving the live balance and before inserting, all inside one transaction. **Negative-stock invariant:** application-layer only (disclosed, not a DB CHECK, since balance is never stored) — re-validated live via a dedicated `InsufficientStockError` rejection path; structurally untriggerable by W2 itself (receiving is always store-increasing) but proven correct via its own dedicated tests/live smoke check. **Receiving:** NOT Procurement — no purchase requisition/RFQ/PO/approval workflow exists; `source`/`deliveryReference` are plain descriptive text. A submission may cover multiple items sharing one generated reference (`office_inventory_receipt` sequence key, reusing `numbering.ts`'s exact primitive, a new `receiptNumber` sub-config mirroring W1's own `itemNumber` shape), committed atomically — an invalid line rolls back the entire submission with zero rows written. There is no separate "receipts" header table — a receipt is simply the set of ledger rows sharing one `referenceNumber`, assembled on read. **Idempotency:** an optional client-supplied key is derived per-line (`key#lineIndex`) against the ledger's own `(organizationId, idempotencyKey)` partial unique index; a repeat submission is detected via a `pg_advisory_xact_lock` keyed on `(organizationId, idempotencyKey)` acquired before the existence check inside the same transaction — this serializes genuinely concurrent duplicate submissions so the loser observes the winner's committed rows and returns them (`replay: true`) rather than double-inserting; the DB unique index remains a defense-in-depth backstop. **Permissions:** zero new keys — reuses exactly two of the frozen 23 (`office_inventory.receive` for creating receipts, `office_inventory.custody.read` for every read route). The custody.read mapping for stock/movement reads is a disclosed interpretation, not literal frozen-plan text (the frozen plan names no dedicated "stock read" permission) — flagged for confirmation, matching this session's own established practice of surfacing rather than silently resolving genuine ambiguity. **Authorization:** every route composes `requireAuth → requireMembership → requireModuleEnabled("office_inventory") → requirePermission`; IDOR-tested live (a cross-org store or item ID is rejected even for an otherwise fully-authorized actor). **No generic ledger-write API exists** — the only way to append a movement row through this API is `POST .../receiving`, which always hard-codes `movementType: "received"`; a client can never specify `movementType` or any other ledger field directly — verified by a permanent test that introspects the Express router's own registered routes and asserts only GET/POST exist, with POST limited to exactly one path. **Audit:** `office_inventory_receipt.created`, fired exactly once per non-replay receipt (never on idempotency replay, mirroring Payroll's own established export-repeat-call precedent). **Cost boundary:** optional `unitCost`/`currency` captured at receiving only, reference-only — no FIFO/LIFO/weighted-average/GL posting/valuation engine; quantity and cost arithmetic reuses Payroll's own `payrollMoney.ts` BigInt/minor-units helpers directly (disclosed cross-module reuse of a genuinely generic decimal-safe primitive) — zero native floating-point arithmetic anywhere in the balance or idempotency-comparison path. **Database/migration:** migration `0051` (`office_inventory_stock_movements` — 1 table, 24 columns, RLS-enabled with zero policies), applied to the development database only; zero schema drift confirmed via `drizzle-kit generate` both immediately after applying and again after all subsequent work. **API/OpenAPI/codegen:** 5 new endpoints (create/list/get receiving, stock balance, movement history); orval codegen run twice, byte-identical output confirmed via MD5, zero duplicate operationIds. **Frontend:** two new tabs on the existing `/office-inventory` page — Receiving (multi-line Receive Stock dialog, history table, per-receipt detail view) and Stock (per-item balance with a per-store breakdown) — no request/approval/issue/return/handover/incident/stocktake/ESS/reporting surfaces exist. **Automated tests:** 33 new focused backend tests across 4 files — pure movement-direction-table and append-only-enforcement coverage (the SQL-computed balance math and real-Postgres concurrency are deliberately NOT re-implemented against a mocked db, consistent with this codebase's own established precedent that genuine row-locking/SQL behavior is proven live, not simulated — see `employeeNumbering.test.ts`'s own header), receiving orchestration (one item, multi-item atomicity, cross-org item/store rejection, invalid/zero/negative quantity rejection, idempotency replay vs. genuinely new submissions), and an HTTP-boundary authorization suite (401/403/module-disabled/cross-org IDOR/success, plus the no-generic-write-route architectural test) — one real Category A bug was caught and fixed during this workstream's own test-writing (see Issues Found). Full backend regression 109/109 files, 2057/2057 tests; frontend regression 64/64 files, 714/714 tests; full workspace typecheck clean; all 3 production builds clean. **Live development QA (disposable fixtures, WWM never touched):** 28/28 checks passed against the real development database via the actual lib functions — scenarios A–M from the frozen plan's own mandate, including: receive 100 into Store 1 (balance 100), receive another 50 (balance 150), receive into Store 2 with both stores' balances and the organization-wide total independently correct, an atomic multi-item receipt, a deliberately invalid multi-item receipt (zero lines committed), same idempotency key submitted twice (stock changes once, second call replays), a genuinely concurrent 3-way duplicate submission (exactly one reference number wins, the other two replay, stock increases by exactly one receipt's worth), cross-org item/store rejection, the module-disabled state confirmed live, ledger history reconciling exactly to the derived balance, the expected audit events present, and the WWM boundary. **Additionally, the frozen plan's own explicitly-named W2 concurrency test — 5 simultaneous receiving submissions for the same item/store — was executed live: all 5 succeeded with 5 distinct reference numbers and zero lost updates** (balance increased by exactly 5× the submitted quantity). The frozen plan document itself (`docs/PAYROLL_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`) was never edited to relabel this sequence.

**Scope delivered, end-to-end:** module foundation (`payroll`, `status: hidden`, `defaultEnabled: false`, category `financial-operations`) · an org-scoped `"payroll"` config namespace · 16 narrow `payroll.*` permissions, none granted to any role by default · an effective-dated, maker-checker-approved statutory-rule engine (PAYE bands, pension/SSNIT rates, pension earnings ceiling, each independently versionable) · employee compensation with as-of historical resolution · banking details and statutory identifiers, both narrowly gated and read-audited · payroll periods and draft runs · explicit, date-driven employee inclusion (never staff-number-driven) · explicit one-off payroll inputs (never inferred from Attendance/Leave) · the calculation engine (gross → pensionable earnings → employee pension → taxable income → PAYE → other deductions → net pay → employer contributions) · a BigInt/pesewa fixed-point money engine (zero native floating-point in the authoritative path) · calculation snapshots (`payroll_run_lines`/`payroll_run_line_components`) as the sole downstream financial authority · a recalculation boundary that closes the instant a run is approved · distinct-actor approval and locking · append-only corrections · payslips (HR + ESS) · Payroll Register, PAYE Schedule, and Pension/SSNIT Schedule, each with CSV export · payment-batch preparation and a generic CSV export · audit coverage across every mutating/sensitive-read surface · tenant isolation throughout · and historical reproducibility, proven live and repeatedly across every workstream from W3 onward.

**Statutory architecture:** PAYE bands, pension/SSNIT rates, and the pension earnings ceiling are stored, effective-dated, maker-checker-approved DATA (`payroll_statutory_rule_versions` + three rule-type child tables) — never hard-coded permanent constants in application code. A future GRA/SSNIT change is entered as a new effective-dated version through the existing draft → validate → approve workflow, superseding the prior version automatically and non-retroactively at the moment its own `effectiveFrom` arrives, without touching the calculation engine itself, PROVIDED the change fits the already-supported rule shapes (graduated PAYE bands with an open-ended final band; a flat employee/employer pension split with independent Tier 1/Tier 2 allocation percentages and an independent earnings ceiling). **No automatic statutory scraping, notification, or activation exists or is claimed** — every version is entered and approved by a human, from a disclosed source, through the controlled workflow; this was an explicit, deliberate boundary from the very first Payroll planning document and remains unchanged.

**Calculation authority / historical integrity:** the calculation order above is authoritative and immutable per run once locked; every payslip, register row, statutory-schedule row, and payment-batch line is read exclusively from the stored calculation snapshot — never recalculated from live data — proven architecturally (no reporting or payment-batch code path imports the calculation engine) and live, repeatedly, across W5, W8, and W9. A later compensation change, a later-approved statutory-rule version, a banking-details change, an employee's separation, and a staff-number release/reuse **do not rewrite any historical locked Payroll artifact** — each was independently live-proven, most recently and most completely in W9's own historical-reproducibility master scenario. `employees.id` remains the sole technical Payroll identity throughout; `employeeNumber`/staff-number values are always historically snapshotted at the moment they matter (calculation time for run lines, batch-creation time for banking) and are never resolved live for a historical artifact.

**Staff-number reuse compatibility:** proven live, repeatedly (W3, W5, W8, W9) — after an employee separates, releases a staff number, and a different employee later receives that exact number, every one of the original employee's historical Payroll artifacts (run line, payslip, Payroll Register row, PAYE/pension schedule row, payment-batch line, correction) remains attached to the original employee's `employees.id` and displays the original employee's historically-snapshotted number — never the new holder's identity or number.

**Payroll lifecycle (final state machine):** `draft → calculated → approved → locked`, with `payroll_corrections` as the only sanctioned path to adjust a locked run's result — append-only, referencing the original locked line directly, never overwriting it, with at most one open draft correction per line and unlimited sequential approved corrections. A run may only be cancelled while `draft`/`calculated`, never once `approved`. Payment batches sit strictly downstream of `locked` and are themselves `draft → exported`, with `exported` being terminal/immutable — batches never feed back into or mutate the run.

**Maker-checker:** enforced server-side at three independent points — statutory-rule approval (creator may never self-approve), payroll-run approval and locking (both require an actor distinct from the run's own preparer), and correction approval (approver must differ from the correction's own creator) — each independently live-proven, including the specific business-logic-layer 409 (not merely a permission-layer 403) that makes the check a genuine maker-checker enforcement rather than incidental role separation.

**Payslip / ESS boundary:** an employee reaches only their own payslip(s) through `payroll.payslip.read.own`, with identity resolved server-side from the caller's own `employee_user_links` — never a client-supplied employeeId or line ID — live-proven to match the HR-authorized view of the same line exactly, and live-proven that a second ESS-linked employee resolves only their own distinct figures.

**Payment Batch boundary — stated explicitly and without qualification:** Payment Batches PREPARE a generic, neutral payment-instruction export. **The system does not execute bank payments, does not integrate with any bank or mobile-money rail, and an exported batch must never be read or represented as meaning employees have been paid.** The lifecycle is `draft → exported` only; there is no "paid" state anywhere in the schema, API, or frontend, and none is implied by any UI copy.

**Sensitive-data boundary:** banking details and statutory identifiers remain behind their own narrow `payroll.banking.*`/`payroll.statutory_identifiers.*` permissions, distinct from general compensation/report access; reads of both are audit-logged (a deliberate, disclosed exception to the platform's general read-silence convention); full bank-account numbers surface only in the authorized payment-batch CSV export, masked everywhere else.

**Permissions (final count, verified live in W9, not re-queried in this documentation-only pass):** exactly 16 `payroll.*` keys, matching the frozen plan's own §14 list exactly. `org_admin`, `hr_manager`, and `employee` hold zero by default; `super_admin` holds all 16 (the platform's own existing blanket-grant convention, not a Payroll-specific decision). Zero org-scoped custom roles exist anywhere on the platform. **WWM's own membership holds zero `payroll.*` permissions** as of the W9 verification and this reconciliation found nothing to contradict that.

**Module configuration:** Payroll remains organization-configurable and disabled by default (`defaultEnabled: false`, `status: hidden`) exactly as every prior workstream shipped it. This report enables nothing for any organization.

**Database / schema (verified from the repository directly, not assumed):** Payroll's migration footprint is exactly `0045` through `0049` — `0045`/`0046`/`0047` (Foundation/Compensation/Calculation Engine schema), `0048` (Corrections + run-status lifecycle extension), `0049` (Payment Batches). No `0050` was created by this report; none was needed. The Payroll-related table set (statutory rule versions + 3 rule-type child tables, employee compensation/banking/statutory-identifier tables, periods, runs, run lines, run line components, input references, corrections, correction components, payment batches, payment batch lines — 16 tables total) all carry RLS enabled with zero policies, per the platform's own deny-by-default, application-layer-authorization convention.

**RLS/security:** W9's own fresh audit stands as the authority — 111 public tables, 100% RLS-enabled, zero policies, zero permissive policies anywhere, all 16 Payroll tables individually confirmed. Not re-queried in this documentation-only pass, per the explicit instruction not to reproduce W9.

HR uploads evidence during `hr_review`; real `hr_review → finalized` transition with a `92.50` override — the manager's own `80.00` score preserved and independently readable, the override stored and displayed as a genuinely distinct value, never conflated with the manager's own result; a repeat finalize attempt correctly 409'd; a post-finalization evidence upload attempt correctly denied (409, confirming evidence really is part of the durable historical record); HR reopened the review to `manager_review` with a reason — `revisionNumber` incremented from 1 to 2, `computedOverallScore` and the override both cleared, `selfAssessmentSubmittedAt` correctly preserved (not blanked), and **all 3 evidence items survived the reopen untouched, never deleted**; the manager then made a genuinely different competency rating (5 instead of 3) and resubmitted for real, producing a **genuinely different** recomputed score (`100.00` — proving real recalculation against the new input, not a stale cached value); HR finalized again without supplying any override — confirming no prior override silently carries across a reopen, and that `revisionNumber` correctly stayed at 2 (only reopen itself increments it, not a second finalize). The W80 internal HR workspace, W78's own team-reviews route, the W81 dashboard (zero-filled lifecycle buckets, with the reopened-then-refinalized review counting only under its final live `finalized` status — never double-counted under any prior state — and, confirmed again, no forbidden average-score or completion-percentage tile anywhere), all 3 currently-implemented reports (correct rows, the manager/override/effective scores kept correctly distinct, CSV export working end-to-end), and the still-correctly-unregistered `performance_rating_distribution` report key (404, confirming the W81 deferral remains intact and was not casually "fixed" here) were all exercised against the real running server. _Last updated: 2026-08-20 — **Phase 3C, W82 — Evidence/Attachments shipped in development.** Wires up W73's own `performance_review_evidence` join table (§8.9: "a lightweight join table only... no new file-storage layer") to the platform's EXISTING `employee_documents` storage system (Phase 2A, `lib/employeeDocuments.ts`/`lib/fileStorage.ts`/`lib/documentValidation.ts`) — **no schema change, still migration `0038`**, and deliberately no second storage provider, no second upload-directory architecture, no cloud-storage abstraction: every byte is written/read through the exact same `writeOrgFile`/`readOrgFile`/`validateDocumentUpload` primitives every other document upload on this platform already uses, keeping the codebase equally deployable on shared hosting, a VPS, or any other provider. **Ownership**: because a plain employee or a manager (reviewer-of-record) holds neither of the existing HR-only `employee.write`/`employee.read` keys the pre-existing `/employees/:employeeId/documents` routes require, this workstream owns its own combined "create the employee_documents row + attach it to the review" action (`addEvidence` in the new `lib/performanceReviewEvidence.ts`), authorized entirely through Performance's own existing permission keys — no new key anywhere. The created `employee_documents` row is always filed under the review's own `employeeId` (the reviewee), regardless of which authorized actor uploaded it, matching how it would read in that employee's own personnel file. **Stage gating — a disclosed interpretation, not frozen-literal**: §8.9 specifies only the schema, no stage rule for evidence anywhere in the frozen plan. Absent one, this workstream applies §10.2's own "each actor may act only during their own active stage" discipline symmetrically to evidence: employee upload requires `performance.write.own` + own review + status `self_assessment`; the reviewer of record requires `performance.review.write` + status `manager_review`; HR requires `performance.manage` (the plan's own established org-wide signal used everywhere else in Performance reporting/reopen — deliberately not `performance.finalize`, which is scoped narrowly to the finalize/override action only) + status `hr_review`. Once a review reaches `finalized`/`acknowledged`, no actor can add evidence through any route — durable historical record, satisfied structurally by this same gate rather than a separate rule. **View/download are never stage-gated** — evidence remains visible to the same own/reviewer-of-record/organization-wide tier at every stage, including after finalization. Reopening (W79) never touches this table at all — only review-row timestamp/decision columns are cleared — so existing evidence is always preserved across a reopen, and upload eligibility re-opens automatically the moment status returns to a stage some actor is authorized for. **No delete route** — §8.9/§22/§27 are all silent on removal, so none was invented, per the master brief's own "if frozen plan contains no delete behavior, do not invent a DELETE route" instruction. **Download is authorization-checked before any storage read**: authenticate → membership → module → resolve the review → prove the caller's own/reviewer/organization-wide visibility → confirm the evidence row genuinely belongs to this exact review and organization → only then read the file from disk. No public or signed URL is ever generated; the file streams through this one authenticated route on every single request, mirroring `backgroundChecks.ts`'s own existing "authenticated evidence download" precedent (`Content-Type`/`Content-Disposition: attachment`/`Cache-Control: private, no-store`) — the only other place on this platform that already serves a document this way. **Consistency, designed and tested**: the file is written to storage first; the `employee_documents` insert and the `performance_review_evidence` join-row insert then run together inside one `db.transaction`; if that transaction fails for any reason, the already-written file is deleted (compensating cleanup) so storage and the database can never disagree — verified by a fixture-based unit test that force-fails the transaction and confirms zero orphaned rows and zero orphaned files result. **Audit — two events, neither purely invented, since §22 names no evidence event at all**: reuses the real, already-frozen `employee_document.uploaded` event (Phase 2A — a genuine document row really is created) for the document-creation half, and adds one new event for the genuinely-new "attached to a review" half, `performance_review.evidence_attached` — modeled directly on this exact codebase's own sibling precedent for the identical concept, `background_check.evidence_attached` (`lib/backgroundChecks.ts`), rather than invented from nothing. A new `document_category` Master Data code, `performance_evidence`, registered as a system-wide default item (§8.9/§35's own literal instruction: "a new document_category Master Data code registered") via the existing idempotent `seed:master-data` script's `SYSTEM_ITEMS` map — additive seed data, not a migration. **3 new routes**, all under the existing `performance.write.own`/`performance.review.write`/`performance.manage` coarse-permission union (mirroring `performanceReviewGoals.ts`'s own established "coarse gate + fine-grained check" precedent): `POST/GET .../performance/reviews/:id/evidence` and `GET .../performance/reviews/:id/evidence/:evidenceId/download`. **New shared `PerformanceEvidenceSection` component**, embedded — never a second, standalone file manager — on all three frozen surfaces named by §19/§28: My Performance (ESS `/self-service`, employee upload), My Team Reviews (`/performance-team`, manager upload), and the internal HR review detail (`/performance-reviews`, HR view + upload during `hr_review`); each host page computes its own `canUpload` from the review's current status and the viewer's own relationship to it, while the backend remains the sole authority on whether an upload attempt actually succeeds. No new table, no new permission key, no migration `0039` (still `0038`, 39 migration files, confirmed unchanged) — the one Master Data item is additive seed data only. 24 new backend tests (`performanceReviewEvidence.test.ts`) + 7 new frontend tests (`performance-evidence.test.tsx`), plus the 3 existing page test suites (My Performance/My Team Reviews/the HR review workspace) updated with inert evidence-hook stubs so their own suites keep passing unchanged — full suite: 1163 backend (+24) / 362 frontend (+7) tests pass, typecheck clean across all four workspace packages, OpenAPI/codegen byte-identical across two runs, zero migration drift, all three production builds succeed (`mockup-sandbox`, `api-server`, `hrms`). **Lint: NOT AVAILABLE** — pre-existing repository tooling gap, unchanged. **A real bug found live and fixed, not merely reported**: multer's own `LIMIT_FILE_SIZE` error for an oversized upload was, before this fix, surfacing as a raw, unhandled Express 500 rather than a typed 400 — violating the master brief's own explicit "no raw filesystem/storage errors" and "typed 4xx" requirements. _Last updated: 2026-08-20 — **Phase 3C, W81 — Performance Dashboard & Reporting shipped in development.** Read-only, server-computed aggregation over W73–W80's existing `performance_reviews`/`performance_review_goals` data, exactly per §20/§21/§27 of the frozen plan — **no schema change, still migration `0038`**. **Explicitly not a second scoring engine, no persisted dashboard/report table, nothing mutated by any function here.** New dedicated route `routes/performanceReporting.ts` (`GET .../performance/dashboard`, `GET .../performance/reports/:reportKey`), mirroring `attendanceReporting.ts`'s/`recruitmentReporting.ts`'s own established dedicated-scope-route precedent — the generic `GET .../reports/:reportKey/run` runner takes only an `organizationId` and cannot express Performance's own/reviewer-of-record/organization-wide visibility tiers, so it safely 404s "Unknown report" for every Performance key, matching the identical established pattern for `recruitment_*`/`attendance_*` keys. Both new routes gated `performance.reports.read` only — §27's own literal permission for each — with scope resolved in the service layer exactly as line 142 of the frozen permission table itself specifies: `performance.manage` holders get organization-wide reach; everyone else (including a plain `employee`-role holder, who is granted `performance.reports.read` too, per the seeded permission table) sees only reviews where they are the review's own employee or its snapshotted `reviewerEmployeeId` — the identical own/reviewer/organization-wide three-tier model `performanceAuthorization.ts` already establishes, resolved here at the review-SET level via a genuine `or(employeeId = own, reviewerEmployeeId = own)` condition rather than per single review. **Dashboard (§20) — plain, zero-filled tile counts only, per its own explicit "no invented rate/KPI" instruction**: `activeCycleCount` (organization-wide — cycle existence isn't sensitive review data — regardless of the caller's own scope), `employeesAssignedCount`, a full 6-status `statusBreakdown` (`draft`/`self_assessment`/`manager_review`/`hr_review`/`finalized`/`acknowledged`, zero-filled, fixed order — a review's live status column decides its bucket, so a reopened review counts only under its current status, never a prior one, and no historical double-counting is possible since nothing here reads `audit_events`), plus the two named pending-vs-submitted tiles (self-assessment, manager review) and a `proposedGoalsAwaitingDecisionCount` tile, all derived from that one status-grouped count pass rather than separate queries — avoiding the N+1 the master brief's own "Performance / Query Strategy" section warns against. Optional `?cycleId=` narrows every review-scoped tile to one cycle; `activeCycleCount` stays organization-wide regardless of it. **No completion-percentage or average-score tile exists anywhere in this dashboard** — §20's own text explicitly forbids both ("no fabricated 'average score' tile"), and none was invented despite the master brief's own "potential concepts" list naming both as things to consider; the frozen plan controls where the two disagree. **3 of the 4 frozen report keys implemented and registered** in the existing Reporting Foundation registry (`lib/db/src/seed/report-definitions.ts` — additive seed data via the existing idempotent `seed:reports` script, not a migration): `performance_review_status` (employee/cycle/status/reviewer/department snapshot/position snapshot/revision/four submission-and-finalization timestamps — no unrelated employee-sensitive fields), `performance_scores` (employee/cycle/manager score/HR override/effective score/status/revision — **manager score, HR override, and effective score always three distinct columns, read directly from each review's own already-persisted W78/W79 columns, never recalculated here** — an override is never presented as if it were the manager's own result), and `performance_goal_results` (only `approvalStatus = 'accepted'` goals — §21's own "official accepted goals only" scope; rejected/still-proposed goals are never included; `originType`/`approvalStatus` exposed per §21's own literal amendment, for HR visibility into employee-proposed-vs-manager-created acceptance outcomes). CSV export (`?format=csv`) reuses the platform's established `toCsv` convention verbatim, as a local copy matching `attendanceReporting.ts`'s own precedent exactly (its row type is nullable, unlike the generic `lib/reporting.ts` version's, so a fresh local copy — not an import — is the established pattern here too). **A genuine, disclosed omission, not a guess**: the 4th frozen key, `performance_rating_distribution`, and its matching "rating distribution (score bands)" dashboard tile, are **deliberately NOT implemented or registered this workstream**. §20/§21 name the concept but define no actual band/bin boundaries anywhere for the normalized 0-100 score, and a full search of this codebase's own established reporting precedent (every `recruitment_*`/`attendance_*` report, including `attendance_monthly_summary`'s own explicit "no rate/percentage column... none is invented here" comment) found zero prior use of numeric banding to reuse as a pattern either. _Last updated: 2026-08-20 — **Phase 3C, W74 — Rating Scales & Review Templates (HR Configuration) shipped in development.** CRUD + level/competency management over W73's schema, exactly per the frozen plan's own W74 scope (`docs/PHASE_3C_PERFORMANCE_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` §27) — **no schema change, still migration `0038`**. **10 new routes** under `.../performance/rating-scales` (list/create broad-read+manage-write, read/update, replace-levels) and `.../performance/templates` (list/create, read/update, replace-competencies) — GET is "read broad" (`performance.read.own`, seeded to every role, per §27's own explicit line); every mutating route requires `performance.manage`. **Rating scale immutability**: a scale's *level set* becomes structurally locked (409) once any `performance_reviews` row references it — derived live via a query, never a stored counter; the scale's own name/description remain always editable and status can always move to/from `archived` regardless of lock state, since only the level set (values/labels/ordering/count) could alter a historical review's meaning. The new `GET .../rating-scales/:id` response carries a `levelsLocked` boolean so the frontend can show this proactively, not only after a failed save. **Templates carry no usage lock at all** — a review snapshots competencies at *creation* time (a later workstream), so a template edit can never rewrite review history; editing is instead blocked only while the template's own `status` is `archived` (a W74-local business-rule choice, not itself frozen, chosen for consistency with every other "archived means retired" resource on this platform — reactivating first is required to keep editing). Template creation/update validates `ratingScaleId` belongs to the same organization (`orgScopedRefs.ts`'s `assertBelongsToOrganization`, extended with one new table reference) and that `goalsWeight + competenciesWeight` sum to exactly 100 (§11.5); the competency-set PATCH validates weights sum to 100 when `competenciesWeight > 0`, and must be empty when `competenciesWeight === 0` — a deliberate, documented consistency rule beyond the frozen document's own literal text, defense-in-depth matching this codebase's established "validate at save time and again downstream" discipline. **Audit** follows §22's own exhaustive list literally, including its asymmetry: rating scales get only `.created`/`.archived` (no `.updated` event exists for scales in the frozen list — name/description/level edits are deliberately unaudited, flagged rather than silently invented); templates get `.created`/`.updated`/`.archived` (competency-set replacement also emits `.updated`, since no separate competency-specific event name exists). **Phase 3H, W114 — Foundation, Numbering & Identifier History — Done (2026-08-23).** Delivered exactly the frozen W114 scope: the organization-level numbering-format engine (new `numbering` config namespace — prefix/suffix/separator/sequenceLength/startingSequence/branch+department+year+month tokens/resetPolicy/reuseEnabled — reusing the existing `organizationConfig` engine and `organization.update` permission, zero new permission for configuration itself); two new tables, migration `0041` (additive, applied to development) — `numbering_sequences` (concurrency-safe counter, `SELECT ... This report does not claim more than that frozen scope satisfies — Manager Portal was never elaborated beyond a bare bullet, so "satisfying the roadmap item" means delivering the frozen V1, not some larger, unwritten ambition.

### Shipped Architecture

**Hybrid Manager Portal** — one consolidated read/orchestration surface (`/manager`: Overview, My Team, Pending Actions) plus module-aware deep-links into each module's own existing, unmodified manager page (Leave Approvals, Performance Team Reviews, My Team Training). **No duplicate cross-module business-rules engine** — every tile and every Pending Actions item is computed by calling that module's own existing service function unchanged (`listPendingApprovals`, `listTeamReviews`, `listTeamEnrollments`, `listTeamAssetAssignments`, `getAttendanceRegisterForEmployees`), never a reimplementation. **No inline mutation engine** — zero `POST`/`PATCH`/`DELETE` route exists anywhere in the Manager Portal backend; every action a manager takes happens on the existing, authoritative module page. This is frozen as a **permanent V1 invariant**, not merely a launch-day simplification — any future workstream that wants to add inline mutation requires its own explicit Owner approval, not an assumed extension of Phase 3G.

### Module

`manager_portal` — registry status **active** (flipped from the pre-existing `hidden` row, never a newly-created module key), `defaultEnabled: false`. **Zero organizations auto-enabled** — confirmed live throughout W109–W113: 0 `organization_modules` rows for `manager_portal` at rest. No alternate module key was ever created. No production enablement of any kind.

### Permissions / Role Model

**Zero new Manager Portal permissions** — no `manager_portal.read`, `manager.read`, `manager.read.team`, or any `*.read.team` variant exists anywhere in the permission registry, reconfirmed live in W112 and again in this closure. **No formal manager role** — the role registry is unchanged: `employee`, `hr_manager`, `org_admin`, `super_admin`. Manager eligibility for Manager Portal purposes is a pure live relational fact: whether the caller's employee record is currently referenced as `reportingManagerId` by ≥1 current employee.

### Manager Eligibility

Server-derived caller employee identity on every route (`resolveManagerPortalActorEmployeeId`, wrapping the existing `resolveOwnEmployeeId` — never a second "which employee is me" mechanism). Live `reportingManagerId`, direct reports only — no recursive hierarchy, no indirect reports, no dotted-line management, no historical manager privilege of any kind. If a manager loses their final direct report, every relationship-derived count/item/team-row disappears immediately on the next call — proven live in both W112's and this report's own reconciliation via the relationship-change test.

### Team Overview

`GET .../manager-portal/team` returns exactly the frozen narrow field set (actual field names, `lib/managerPortal.ts`): `id`, `employeeNumber`, `firstName`, `lastName`, `positionId`/`positionName`, `departmentId`/`departmentName`, `branchId`/`branchName`, `employmentStatus`, `hasProfilePicture` (a **boolean only** — no image, no storage key, no URL). Direct-reports-only, **including for HR/admin** — Team Overview never returns an organization-wide employee list, by design (Decision 27/A). Deterministic ordering (lastName, firstName, id). Terminated employees (`employmentStatus = "terminated"`) are excluded from the live direct-report set — the one deliberate, disclosed narrowing beyond the 7 pre-existing direct-report query implementations elsewhere in the codebase, none of which were touched. Zero sensitive fields of any kind — no address, no personal contact info, no banking, no compensation, no payroll, no emergency contacts, no documents, no medical or disciplinary data, no Career Profile details. Read-only (zero mutation route exists), audit-silent (confirmed live, `audit_events` unchanged across every QA session this phase).

### HR / Admin Behavior

`hr_manager`/`org_admin`/`super_admin` may open the Manager Portal for operational visibility, per the frozen access model — but this access does **not** create manager-of-record, reviewer-of-record, or instructor-of-record authority. Team Overview remains **their own direct reports only**, even for HR/admin — Employee Management (`/employees`) already serves the organization-wide browsing need, and Manager Portal was deliberately not built as a second one. Underlying modules preserve exactly their own existing HR/admin capabilities, no more. **The one explicit, frozen exception**: Leave's Pending Leave Actions tile/items go organization-wide for a caller who separately holds `leave_request.manage` (reusing Leave's own existing `listPendingApprovals` org-wide branch unchanged) — this exception is scoped to Leave alone and does **not** generalize to Attendance, Performance, Learning, or Assets, each of which stays strictly direct-report/snapshot-scoped regardless of what other permissions the caller holds.

### Dashboard

Exactly six frozen metrics, backend-authoritative, zero client-side recalculation:
1. **Direct Reports** — count of live direct reports (`listLiveDirectReports`).
2. **Attendance — Absent or Late Today** — live direct-report scope, counts only `absent`/`late` statuses for the organization's own resolved civil "today."
3. **Pending Leave Actions** — direct-reports-only, or organization-wide for `leave_request.manage` holders.
4. **Pending Performance Actions** — strictly `reviewerEmployeeId`-snapshot at `status="manager_review"`.
5. **Pending Learning Actions** — strictly `managerEmployeeIdSnapshot`-snapshot at `approvalStatus="pending"`; instructor-of-record never counted.
6. **Team Assets In Custody** — live direct-report scope, current custody only.

Each of the five module-backed tiles is `null` — never a genuine `0` — when its own module is disabled, the caller lacks that module's own existing permission, or (Attendance only) the organization's timezone isn't configured yet for a safe calculation. A real number, including `0`, means the module is enabled, the caller is authorized, and the query genuinely found nothing. The frontend renders `null` as a deliberately generic "Unavailable" state, never as `0` — verified by a dedicated mixed-response test (positive integer + real zero + two nulls, all rendered correctly in the same view).

### Attendance

Live direct-report scope (shared with Team Overview's own `listLiveDirectReports`), reuses `getAttendanceRegisterForEmployees`/`resolveOrganizationTodayCivilDate` unchanged — no second Attendance date/timezone engine. Returns `null` (not `0`, not an error) when the organization's timezone configuration prevents a safe "late" calculation, mirroring Attendance's own existing hard-error-on-missing-timezone design. Zero Attendance mutation exists anywhere inside Manager Portal.

### Leave

Manager/workflow authority fully preserved — Manager Portal never redefines who may act on a leave request. Plain-manager scope matches Leave's own existing `listPendingApprovals` direct-report branch exactly; the `leave_request.manage` organization-wide carve-out is Leave's own pre-existing behavior, reused unchanged. Pending count and Pending Actions item list are both derived from the same underlying query, confirmed to agree exactly in live QA. All approvals/rejections continue to occur exclusively on the existing Leave Approvals page — Manager Portal only deep-links there.

### Performance

Reviewer-of-record snapshot authority (`reviewerEmployeeId`) is the sole source of Performance pending-action authority — never the live `reportingManagerId`. A relationship change does **not** move an existing Performance action to the new manager; it stays with the original snapshotted reviewer. This was proven live, not merely asserted, in both W112 and this report's own reconciliation: reassigning a direct report's manager left their pending Performance review with the original reviewer, and the new manager's own Pending Performance count/items remained at zero for that review. Deep-links to the existing Performance Team Reviews page for all review actions.

### Learning

`managerEmployeeIdSnapshot` is the sole source of general Manager Portal Learning pending-action authority. Instructor-of-record (`instructorEmployeeId`, keyed to a session, not an enrollment) is kept structurally separate — Manager Portal's own aggregation code never queries `instructorEmployeeId` at all, so instructor-only work can never inflate the general manager pending count, confirmed with a real instructor-of-record fixture in W112's own live QA. Deep-links to the existing My Team Training page for all enrollment actions.

### Asset Management

Live current-direct-report scope (shared with Team Overview/Attendance), active current custody only — reuses `listTeamAssetAssignments` unchanged. Read-only Manager Portal metric; no historical custody widening; zero Asset mutation inside the portal. Deep-links to the existing Team Assets page, which remains the sole authoritative surface for any asset-related manager action.

### Live vs. Snapshot Authority (Final Architectural Property)

**Live**: Team Overview, Attendance, Assets — all three share the same `listLiveDirectReports` helper and re-evaluate the `reportingManagerId` relationship on every call. **Workflow/Snapshot**: Performance (`reviewerEmployeeId`) and Learning (`managerEmployeeIdSnapshot`) — both resolve their own authoritative relationship independently of `listLiveDirectReports`, by construction (their own actor-resolvers, `resolvePerformanceActorEmployeeId`/`resolveLearningActorEmployeeId`, are never called with the live direct-report list). **Leave** uses its own existing workflow/permission semantics (direct-report or `leave_request.manage`-gated organization-wide), a model distinct from both the pure-live and pure-snapshot categories. Manager Portal deliberately has **no single universal manager-authorization model** — this is a permanent property, not a simplification pending later unification. W112's integrated live relationship-change test, and this report's own independent reconciliation, both proved all of these simultaneously and correctly in one real-data scenario.

### Pending Actions

Exactly three source modules — **Leave, Performance, Learning**. No Attendance action items, no Assets action items, no Recruitment, no Workforce, no Documents, no Career Profile — confirmed by direct code inspection (the aggregation file imports only Leave/Performance/Learning service functions) and by every live QA run across W110/W112/W113. Computed live on every call, read-only, non-persistent (no task table, no notification engine, no task-completion endpoint anywhere in the codebase). Each item carries only the frozen safe/narrow DTO: source module, the underlying entity's own id, employee id + raw first/last name, current authoritative status, a concise safe title, `createdAt`.

### Inline Mutation Boundary

**Zero Manager Portal mutation routes** — confirmed via `grep` for `router.post|patch|put|delete` across every Manager Portal backend file, zero matches, reconfirmed in this closure. **Zero cross-module mutation hooks or buttons in the frontend** — confirmed via direct inspection of `manager-portal.tsx`'s own import list and a dedicated frontend test asserting no approve/reject/complete/submit/assign/return/correct/lifecycle control exists anywhere on the page. The portal reads and routes; underlying module pages perform every action and produce their own, unmodified audit events.

### Module Gating

Two-tier: the shell is gated by `manager_portal`; each dashboard tile and each Pending Actions source is additionally gated by its own underlying module's own enabled state and the caller's own existing permission for that module. Mixed-module organizations are fully supported — W112's own mixed-module test (Learning disabled mid-session) proved only Learning's own tile/items disappeared, with every other section remaining fully functional; this report's own reconciliation re-confirmed the code path is unchanged since.

### Zero-Direct-Report Behavior

A linked employee with zero current direct reports receives a valid, explicit empty Team Overview (`linked: true, directReports: []`) and zero-filled relationship-derived dashboard metrics/Pending Actions — never an error, never historical-report authority, never an organization-wide fallback. The frontend renders the frozen "You currently have no direct reports" empty state rather than a false error, distinct from the separate `linked: false` "not linked to an employee record" state.

### Frontend

Route `/manager`, nav label "Manager Portal" (unconditional visibility, mirroring Leave Approvals' own established precedent — the one pre-existing nav item with no `isHrCapable` role gate). Three sections as Tabs: Overview, My Team, Pending Actions. Generated React Query hooks only — zero manual `fetch()`, zero direct Supabase access, confirmed by direct grep. Zero cross-module business logic of any kind — every rendered value is the server's own value, verbatim. Null vs. zero preserved exactly, as documented above. Deep-links to existing, unmodified authoritative module pages only. Responsive (existing grid/card/table patterns, no separate mobile implementation); accessible semantic tab structure, text status labels (never color-only), keyboard-operable throughout. **No browser-driving/screenshot tooling was used anywhere in Phase 3G** — this environment has no Playwright/e2e setup and none was installed, per the explicit "do not install unrelated browser infrastructure" instruction; verification relied on RTL/component tests (78 new across W109–W111) plus direct code inspection plus real-HTTP live QA, stated accurately, not overstated.

### Deep Links

Exact real destinations, verified against the actual route table:
- **Leave** → `/leave-approvals` (existing Leave Approvals page)
- **Performance** → `/performance-team` (existing Performance Team Reviews page)
- **Learning** → `/learning-team-training` (existing My Team Training page)

No invented routes, no unsupported query-parameter assumptions — each destination page already renders its own full pending list without needing an id passed through the URL.

### API

Exactly three Manager Portal routes, all `GET`, confirmed by direct code inspection:
- `GET /organizations/:organizationId/manager-portal/team` (W109)
- `GET /organizations/:organizationId/manager-portal/dashboard` (W110)
- `GET /organizations/:organizationId/manager-portal/pending-actions` (W110)

Each: `requireAuth` → `requireMembership` → `requireModuleEnabled("manager_portal")` → server-derived actor identity → module-specific authority resolved inside the lib layer (never a Manager Portal permission key). Audit-silent. Narrow DTOs (`ManagerPortalTeamOverview`/`ManagerPortalDashboard`/`ManagerPortalPendingActions`). OpenAPI updated across W109/W110; codegen re-run repeatedly across every workstream including this closure, byte-identical every time; zero duplicate `operationId`s.

### Database

Zero new tables, zero schema changes, migration remains `0040` (no `0041`), zero drift — confirmed via `drizzle-kit generate` in every one of W109/W110/W112 and re-confirmed in this closure.

### Authorization / Tenant Isolation

Authenticated membership required; `manager_portal` module required; caller employee identity always server-derived, never client-suppliable; live direct-report scope where the module's own authority model calls for it; each underlying module's own workflow authority fully preserved; no cross-org widening anywhere. W112 verified WWM ↔ Acme isolation both directions across every portal surface and every module-derived summary, including a 403 for an out-of-membership organization id — this report does not claim isolation testing beyond that already-verified matrix.

### Sensitive Data Boundary

Manager Portal does not expose banking, compensation, payroll, private addresses, emergency contacts, documents, medical information, disciplinary information, or Career Profile details anywhere — it uses purpose-built narrow DTOs throughout, never the full Employee shape and never `SelfServiceEmployeeProfile`. The broad `employee.read` exposure discovered during Phase 3G's own discovery pass remains a separate, pre-existing hardening item — Manager Portal was built specifically to avoid depending on it (confirmed: no Manager Portal route or frontend file consumes the broad `employee.read`-gated profile-picture route or any other broad-DTO endpoint).

### Pre-Existing Hardening Items

Two items were discovered during Phase 3G's own discovery pass, before any implementation began, and were deliberately **not** fixed by this phase:
1. **Broad `employee.read` authorization exposure** — the flat `employee.read` permission (held by the default `employee` role) exposes an employee's full profile organization-wide with no manager-vs-stranger narrowing. Pre-existing, unrelated to Manager Portal's own introduction.
2. **`reportingManagerId` changes are unaudited** — no `audit_events` row is ever emitted when an employee's manager changes via the existing `PATCH /employees/:employeeId` route. Pre-existing, unrelated to Manager Portal's own introduction.

Both remain genuinely open, disclosed, separate platform hardening items — **not** described as Manager Portal defects, and **not** silently fixed in passing at any point across W109–W113.

### Audit

Every Manager Portal `GET` route is audit-silent — Team, Dashboard, and Pending Actions reads alike. The portal itself emits zero mutation events (it performs zero mutations). Deep-linked actions retain their own underlying module's existing, unmodified audit events — no duplicate audit-event layer exists anywhere. Confirmed via a direct `audit_events` count taken before and after every live QA session across W109/W110/W112 and this closure's own reconciliation — zero new rows in every case.

### Security

W112's independently-verified baseline, reconfirmed unchanged in this closure: **89 public tables, 89 RLS enabled, 0 disabled, 0 permissive policies**; Supabase security advisor **89/89 findings INFO-level** (`rls_enabled_no_policy`), **0 ERROR-level**. No direct frontend Supabase access anywhere in Manager Portal. Zero new permissions, zero new roles. Zero sensitive DTO leakage, confirmed by direct grep across every Manager Portal backend and frontend file. Production untouched throughout all five workstreams.

**Result: PASS.** Focused: 78 tests. Backend: **1697/1697**. Frontend: **632/632**. Integrated live QA: **58/58**. All 3 production builds pass. Typecheck clean. Codegen deterministic. Migration drift: none. Browser automation: unavailable (disclosed, not claimed). Lint: **NOT AVAILABLE — pre-existing repository tooling gap**, unchanged, not addressed by this phase. Product defects: zero. This closure (W113) did not rerun the full 58-assertion live lifecycle, per the frozen plan's own lightweight-closure allowance (no code changed since W112) — instead independently re-confirmed HEAD, module state, migration state, route inventory, and permission/role registry live, and relied on W112's own already-completed regression/live-QA results for everything else.

### Approved Deferrals (V1 Boundaries, Not Defects)

Per the frozen plan's own explicit scope, all deliberately not built and not represented as built: Recruitment; Workforce/Scheduling (does not exist in this codebase at all); recursive/multi-level org hierarchy; indirect reports; dotted-line managers; secondary managers; manager delegation; a persistent task/notification inbox engine; inline cross-module mutations; bulk cross-module actions; Manager Portal reports; CSV export; Career Profile exposure through the portal; employee documents; compensation; banking; payroll; disciplinary/private HR information; succession planning; talent calibration; org-chart redesign. The two pre-existing hardening items (§ above) are recorded separately from this deferral list — they are not approved V1 boundaries, they are disclosed, open, pre-existing platform issues Phase 3G deliberately did not touch.

Zero product defects across all five workstreams. Zero fixes made in this closure — `git status` confirms only `PROJECT_STATUS.md` changed.
