### Original Deferred Scope

Phase 3F traces directly back to Phase 2B's own W39 ("Employee Self-Service, narrowed scope"), which explicitly deferred two items, unchanged through Phase 3A–3E:

> "W39 — employment-history aggregation into Employee Self-Service (W25–W27's `employment_periods`, via `listEmploymentPeriods`) — deferred, not completed."
> "W39 — skills/qualifications/certifications aggregation into Employee Self-Service (W24's `employee_skills`/`employee_qualifications`/`employee_certifications`) — deferred, not completed."

Both are now **CLOSED**, delivered exactly as frozen — see the two `~~struck-through~~` Outstanding Items entries earlier in this file, each annotated with its resolving workstream.

### Executive Summary

Phase 3F delivered the long-deferred Employee Self-Service aggregation gap end to end: a read-only "Career Profile" tab inside the existing `/self-service` page, giving employees visibility into their own internal employment history, skills, qualifications, and external/HR-maintained certifications — all read-only, all server-identity-scoped, all reusing existing Phase 2A tables and service functions verbatim, with zero new tables, zero new permissions, and zero new modules. A genuine pre-existing authorization gap discovered during discovery (the 3 skills/qualifications/certifications HR GET routes were reachable by any employee-role user for any coworker's records) was fixed as part of the phase, not merely disclosed and deferred. Two workstreams (W105, W106) shipped independently reviewed, tested, and live-QA'd; W107 verified the phase as one integrated system — including two checks beyond either workstream's own prior QA (live cross-surface HR-read-vs-own-read consistency, and a live audit-silence measurement) — and found zero product defects; W108 (this report) formally closes the phase.

### Shipped Career Profile

`/self-service` now has exactly 10 tabs (9 pre-existing + 1 new), verified directly against the shipped frontend code. The tenth, **Career Profile**, is ungated by any additional module (same precedent as My Profile/My Documents) and contains exactly four read-only sections:

1. **Employment History** — sourced from `employment_periods` (Phase 2A, W22) exactly as stored; internal organizational movement only (transfer/promotion/confirmation); no external prior-employer history model exists or was invented. `GET /me/employment-history` (own-scoped, zero permission) plus a new HR-side `GET .../employees/:employeeId/employment-history` (`employee.write`) display card in `employee-detail.tsx` — the first time this data has ever been rendered anywhere in the product. Transfer/Promote/Confirm remain the sole, unmodified authoritative writers.
2. **Skills** — sourced from `employee_skills` (Phase 2A, W24) via a new `GET /me/skills` (own-scoped, zero permission). HR administration (`employee-detail.tsx`) remains the sole writer. No employee mutation, no Learning-derived skill synchronization, no new proficiency framework.
3. **Qualifications** — sourced from `employee_qualifications` via a new `GET /me/qualifications` (own-scoped, zero permission). HR remains authoritative. No evidence/document attachment was added.
4. **Certifications** — sourced from `employee_certifications` **only** via a new `GET /me/certifications` (own-scoped, zero permission). Expired certifications remain visible; expiry status is derived live, client-side, mirroring My Learning's own established `isCertificateExpired` pattern exactly — never a value the API itself returns, never a new database column. No renewal workflow, no evidence attachment.

Employee identity is server-derived on every one of the four routes (never a client-supplied `employeeId`/`organizationId`, verified live under real tampering attempts in both W106 and W107). **No employee Career Profile mutation API exists at all** — zero `POST`/`PATCH`/`DELETE` route for any of the four resources, verified both by code inspection and by direct live HTTP attempt (all four rejected). Every state (loading/error/empty/populated) is covered per section, with text-labeled status (never color-only).

### Learning Certificate Boundary

`employee_certifications` (HR-maintained/external credentials) and `learning_certificates` (Phase 3D, system-issued) remain architecturally separate, exactly as Learning's own frozen Owner Decision 3 requires — neither table was altered, merged, or synchronized. Career Profile's Certifications section reads `employee_certifications` exclusively; My Learning remains the sole employee surface for `learning_certificates`. Verified twice, independently: by direct code inspection (zero references to `learning_certificates` anywhere in the Career Profile backend or frontend code, confirmed via grep) and live in both W106 and W107 (a real, disposably-staged Learning certificate appeared through My Learning's own existing path but never through Career Profile).

### Authorization Hardening

Discovery found a genuine pre-existing gap: the 3 GET routes in `employeeSkillsQualifications.ts` (skills, qualifications, certifications — exactly 3, not 4; an earlier draft miscounted and was corrected) required only `employee.read`, which the ordinary `employee` role holds, with no own-scope narrowing — any employee-role user could read any coworker's records through these HR-administration routes. Fixed by changing those 3 routes to `employee.write`, matching the 8 mutating routes on the same three resources that already required it. **Zero new permission definitions, zero role-mapping changes** — the fix reused an existing permission already scoped correctly for HR-administrative access. Ordinary employees now use the separate, correctly-scoped `/me/*` own-read routes; the generic HR routes remain HR-authoritative, org-wide, exactly as before for `org_admin`/`hr_manager`. W107 independently re-verified live: coworker attacks denied on all 3 hardened routes (plus the new HR employment-history route), legitimate HR access unaffected.

### Permissions & Modules

**Zero new permissions** anywhere in Phase 3F — no `employee.read.own`, no `.read.team`, no manager-specific Career Profile permission. Own-scoped ESS reads follow the existing `/me/employee` zero-permission precedent (module gate + server-derived identity only) exactly. **Zero new modules** — Career Profile belongs entirely to the existing `employee_self_service` experience; every independently-gated module tab (Attendance/Performance/Learning/Assets/Leave/Recruitment) remains independently gated, unaffected — W107 live-verified specifically that disabling Learning has no effect on Career Profile availability.

### Manager Boundary

Phase 3F did **not** implement Manager Portal, and did not implement any manager Career Profile, team Career Profile, manager career-record mutation, or manager career reporting of any kind. Existing manager capabilities remain exactly where they already were, distributed across separate, already-shipped, per-module surfaces (Team Assets, My Team Training, Performance manager review, the Attendance Register's own team scope) — these do not constitute a consolidated Manager Portal, and this report does not claim they do.

### Database

Zero new tables, zero schema changes, migration remains `0040` (no `0041`), zero drift — confirmed via `drizzle-kit generate` throughout W105, W106, and W107.

### API

New routes (all GET-only, own-scoped, server-derived identity, tenant-isolated, audit-silent — verified live in W107 via a direct before/after `audit_events` count):
- `GET /me/employment-history` (W105)
- `GET /me/skills`, `GET /me/qualifications`, `GET /me/certifications` (W106)

Plus one new HR-side route (W105): `GET .../employees/:employeeId/employment-history` (`employee.write`).

Existing routes changed (permission only, no path/method/response shape change): the 3 skills/qualifications/certifications GET routes in `employeeSkillsQualifications.ts` (`employee.read` → `employee.write`).

OpenAPI updated across both workstreams; codegen run repeatedly, byte-identical (SHA-256 hash match) every time; zero duplicate `operationId`s.

### Frontend

`/self-service` has exactly 10 tabs, verified directly against the shipped code in W107 — all 9 pre-existing tabs intact, exactly one new Career Profile tab, exactly four sections within it. Loading/error/empty/populated states covered for every section; expired certifications shown with a text status label; Learning certificates never rendered in Career Profile. **No browser-driving/screenshot tooling was used anywhere in Phase 3F** — verification relied on RTL/component tests (41 new frontend tests across W105/W106) plus real-HTTP live QA; stated accurately, not overstated.

### Security

RLS baseline unchanged throughout Phase 3F, re-verified live in W107: **89/89 tables RLS-enabled, 0 disabled, 0 permissive policies**; Supabase security advisor re-run, **89/89 findings all INFO-level** `rls_enabled_no_policy`, **zero ERROR-level** findings anywhere. Tenant isolation (WWM ↔ Acme) verified live in both directions across every new own-scoped route and every hardened HR route, in both W106 and W107.

### Verification (W107, final)

**Result: PASS.** Backend **1650/1650**. Frontend **601/601**. Integrated live QA **49/49** assertions on the corrected run. All 3 production builds succeed. Schema drift: none. Codegen: deterministic. Browser automation: unavailable in this environment (disclosed accurately, not claimed). Lint: **NOT AVAILABLE — pre-existing repository tooling gap**, unchanged, not addressed by this phase. **Zero product defects** in W107 — the one issue found was a wrong column name (`created_at` vs. the real `occurred_at`) in disposable QA tooling only, corrected in that tooling alone; `git status` confirmed zero source files touched.

### Approved Deferrals (V1 Boundaries, not defects)

Per the frozen plan's own explicit scope, all of the following were deliberately not built and are not represented as built:
- External previous-employer history (`employment_periods` models only internal organizational movement).
- Employee create/edit/delete/submission workflow for any Career Profile record.
- Evidence/document attachment for employment history, skills, qualifications, or certifications.
- Learning certificate merging, synchronization, or duplication into `employee_certifications`.
- Learning-to-skill synchronization of any kind.
- A manager Career Profile view of any kind.
- A consolidated Manager Portal.

### Issues Found / Fixes Made

One QA-tooling defect only (W107, disposable script, wrong `audit_events` column name) — corrected in the disposable script, never in the repository. Zero product defects across all four workstreams.

### Executive Summary

Phase 3E delivered a complete, tenant-isolated Asset Management module end to end: module activation → an organization-owned asset register with a 5-state lifecycle → assignment/custody/return with server-derived snapshots and employee acknowledgement → employee self-service ("My Assets") and a read-only manager "Team Assets" view (current-custody-only, live relationship, no historical reach, no mutation authority) → employee report-only incident reporting → HR-side incident review/dismiss (structurally independent of asset-state mutation) → loss/recovery/condition-update/retirement as separate authoritative HR actions → simple maintenance history with live, non-caller-suppliable post-maintenance status derivation → evidence attachment reusing the platform's existing document/storage layer → an internal org-wide operational workspace built with zero new backend logic → a dashboard and 3 CSV-exportable reports — on top of the completed Foundation, Phase 2A, Phase 2B, Phase 3A Recruitment, Phase 3B Attendance, Phase 3C Performance, and Phase 3D Learning. Ten workstreams (W95–W104) each shipped independently reviewed, tested, and live-QA'd against the real development database; W103 verified the phase as one integrated system (not isolated per-workstream re-runs) and found zero product defects; W104 (this report) formally closes the phase.

**One genuine cross-workstream event, disclosed transparently rather than hidden:** an earlier prompt mislabeled Dashboard & Reporting as "W101," causing it to be implemented and committed before the actual W101 (Internal Asset Workspace). This was caught during mandatory post-workstream reconciliation, raised explicitly via `AskUserQuestion` rather than silently guessed or silently renumbered, and resolved by building the described scope under its correct frozen label (W102), then filling the real W101 in a later workstream. The frozen plan's own §24 numbering was never altered. See the **Execution-Order Note** below.

### Module & Permissions (Final)

**Module:** `asset_management` — registry status **`active`**, `defaultEnabled: false`. No organization is auto-enabled; re-confirmed live at W104 closure (0 organizations currently hold an `organization_modules` row for this module).

**Permissions, exactly 4, confirmed live:**
- `asset_management.read.own`
- `asset_management.write.own`
- `asset_management.manage`
- `asset_management.reports.read`

No `asset_management.read.team`. No `assets.*` namespace anywhere.

**Role mapping (re-confirmed live at W104):** `employee` → `read.own`, `write.own`, `reports.read` (not `manage`); `hr_manager` / `org_admin` / `super_admin` → all 4. Manager scope is relationship-derived (current `reportingManagerId`, resolved live on every request), never a static permission tier.

**Permanent `write.own` boundary:** this permission authorizes exactly two frozen employee-own actions — acknowledging one's own assignment, and reporting an issue on an asset currently in one's own custody. It never grants any Asset state or custody mutation; every mutating register/assignment/incident-review/maintenance route requires `asset_management.manage`.

### Data Model (Final)

Exactly 5 tables, migration `0040` (no `0041`, zero drift re-confirmed via `drizzle-kit generate` at W104 closure): `assets`, `asset_assignments`, `asset_maintenance`, `asset_evidence`, `asset_incidents`.

**W95's approved foundation change**, carried permanently: `employee_documents.employeeId` was made nullable so organization-owned Asset evidence (not naturally owned by any one employee) can reuse the platform's existing document/storage system without a fabricated employee owner. This was raised via `AskUserQuestion` before any code was written, approved explicitly, and verified to leave every pre-existing consumer (Core HR documents, Performance W82 evidence, Learning W90 evidence) unaffected. This is a permanent, intentional part of the shipped data model — not an outstanding issue.

**Security:** 89 public tables, 89 RLS-enabled, 0 disabled, 0 permissive policies — re-confirmed live at W104 closure.

### Asset Lifecycle & Register

Status enum: `available` → `assigned` → `maintenance` → `lost` → `retired`, with `retired` permanently terminal (no `disposed` status, no reactivation). Condition (`new`/`good`/`fair`/`poor`/`damaged`) is deliberately independent of status. Every lifecycle transition is a dedicated, mandatory-reason action (retire/mark-lost/recover/condition-update) implemented as an atomic conditional `UPDATE` — the generic `PATCH .../assets/:id` route never smuggles a status change; it is confined to non-lifecycle fields only. `assetTag` is server-generated and sequential per organization; `serialNumber` is partial-uniquely constrained per organization when present.

### Assignment / Custody

`asset_assignments` is the sole custody source of truth — no mutable `assets.employeeId` pointer. A database-level partial unique index guarantees at most one active assignment per asset. Assignment/return are each one atomic transaction; a transfer always closes the old row and opens a new one, preserving full snapshot history (assetTag/name/category/department/position, captured server-side at issue time, verified immutable under a later live asset rename). Concurrency verified both by dedicated unit tests (W97) and a real concurrent-HTTP double-assign/double-return race (W103) — exactly one winner every time.

### Acknowledgement

Own employee only, server-derived identity, server timestamp, atomic conditional guard (repeat/concurrent call → controlled `409`, verified under a real race in W103). Acknowledgement survives a later return — nothing clears it once set. ESS wording is receipt-only ("I confirm I received this item"), never liability acceptance.

### Employee Self-Service

"My Assets" lives inside the existing `/self-service` page, independently module-gated. Shows current custody, full historical assignments, the acknowledgement control, and Report an Issue. No HR/admin controls, no manager controls, no direct maintenance/retirement/lost/recover mutation, no direct Supabase access.

### Manager Team Assets

`/team-assets` — current direct reports only, current custody only, resolved live from `reportingManagerId` on every call (re-verified live in both W98 and W103 via a real relationship change: visibility dropped to zero and restored immediately, no caching). Read-only: no assign/return/condition-update/mark-lost/recover/retire/incident-review/maintenance authority. No `asset_management.read.team` permission exists.

### Incidents & HR Review

Employee report-issue creates exactly one `asset_incidents` row (`open`), scoped to the caller's own active custody, and is structurally report-only — verified by code inspection and live that it never touches asset status, condition, custody, or maintenance. HR/Asset-Officer review (`open → reviewed`) and dismiss (`open → dismissed`) are both terminal, `asset_management.manage`-only (a manager with Team Assets visibility is still denied), and never themselves mutate asset state — loss/condition-update/retirement remain separate, authoritative W96 actions HR issues independently.

### Loss / Recovery / Condition / Retirement

Mark-lost and recover are explicit HR-only actions with mandatory reasons; mark-lost correctly closes any active custody. Condition update is a separate action from status, also mandatory-reason. Retirement is blocked while assigned (custody must close first), permanently terminal once applied, with no `disposed` status and no reactivation path (verified live).

### Maintenance

Simple history only — no scheduling engine, no vendor-management platform, no work-order/SLA system. The frozen 3-state-plus-scheduled lifecycle (`scheduled → in_progress → completed | cancelled`) is dispatched through one `PATCH` route via a closed `action` enum, never a raw status field. Completion/cancel derive the asset's post-maintenance status live, inside the same transaction, from a freshly-queried active assignment (never caller-supplied): active custody → `assigned`, none → `available`. A genuine race — an asset marked lost mid-maintenance — is protected by an atomic `WHERE status='maintenance'` guard, verified to roll back to a controlled `409` rather than silently overwriting the lost status, both by code inspection and live (W100 and W103).

### Evidence

`asset_evidence` joins into the existing `employee_documents`/`fileStorage` system verbatim; `employeeId` is always `null` for Asset-owned evidence (no fabricated owner). Upload validation matches the platform's existing rigor (file-signature-checked, 10MB cap, PDF/JPEG/PNG/DOCX/XLSX allowlist). Download is authenticated-only, checked before any storage read, with no public URL ever generated. A failed database transaction triggers compensating physical-file deletion, verified live. No delete route exists. No malware scanning is performed or claimed. **Operational note carried forward:** a database cascade cannot delete a file on local disk — physical evidence cleanup must always be handled explicitly during QA/operations, a discipline this phase's own QA scripts (W100, W103) applied and independently re-verified via correctly repo-root-relative filesystem scans.

### Internal Asset Workspace

`/asset-workspace` — four frozen operational sections (Register, Outstanding Returns, Open Incidents, Lost/Retired History), `asset_management.manage`-only, zero new backend logic (every action reuses an existing W96–W99 route verbatim, confirmed via `git diff` showing no backend file touched by W101). Maintenance and evidence deliberately remain nested under `/assets` only, not duplicated here, per §19's own literal scope enumeration. No dashboard/report duplication.

### Dashboard

`GET .../assets/dashboard` — exactly 5 deterministic tiles: `totalAssetCount`, a zero-filled `statusBreakdown` (all 5 statuses always present), `employeesWithAssignedAssetsCount`, `overdueReturnCount`, `openIncidentCount`. Scope-aware (own/manager-current/organization-wide), zero-filled rather than falling back to org-wide for an actor with no scope. No financial, depreciation, or utilization/rate KPI of any kind was added.

### Reports

Exactly 3, via a dedicated scope-aware `lib/assetReporting.ts`/`routes/assetReporting.ts` route (double-guarded against the shared generic report runner — confirmed to carry zero `asset_*` entries, so no cross-module leakage is possible):
- **`asset_register`** — organization-wide only; every field reads the asset's own current, live value (a current-state report by definition).
- **`asset_unreturned_by_employee`** — own / live-manager-current / organization-wide; every display field reads the assignment's own snapshot columns (§14), never a live join; informational/warning-only, no termination hard block, no `employee_exit_processes` coupling.
- **`asset_maintenance_history`** — organization-wide only; `asset_maintenance` has no snapshot fields at all, so its asset-name/tag display column is a live, batched join — verified live via a mid-QA asset rename that both reports reflected correctly per their respective (snapshot vs. live) model.

CSV and JSON are row/scope-identical (verified live at W102 and W103); every report-specific filter is genuinely honored server-side, with the frontend never rendering a no-op control. The platform-wide CSV formula-injection escaping gap is disclosed below (Known Non-Blocking Items), not silently claimed fixed.

### Historical Integrity

Assignment rows carry their own frozen contextual snapshots (assetTag/name/category/department/position at issue time); later changes to the live asset's name/category or the employee's department/position never rewrite this history — verified live via a real asset rename in both W102 and W103. Manager visibility is the deliberate opposite: always the LIVE `reportingManagerId` relationship, never a snapshot (Owner Decision 3) — re-verified live three times (W98, W102, W103) via an actual relationship change producing an immediate visibility change with no caching.

### Authorization / Tenant Isolation

Every route: `requireAuth` → `requireMembership` → `requireModuleEnabled("asset_management")` → `requirePermission(...)`, plus relationship/scope resolution where applicable. WWM ↔ Acme isolation was verified live, both directions, across assets, assignments, incidents, evidence (including download), dashboard, and reports (W103); the internal workspace inherits the same `/assets`/`/asset-incidents` route-level isolation it reuses, not independently re-tested as a separate surface.

### Concurrency

Verified race protections: double-assign, double-acknowledge, double-return, incident review-vs-dismiss, and competing maintenance transitions each resolve to exactly one winner — proven under real concurrent HTTP requests in both their own originating workstreams (W97, W98/W99, W100) and again as a representative integrated subset in W103. The lost-mid-maintenance status race is protected by the atomic asset-side guard described above (Maintenance). W103 deliberately ran a representative subset rather than re-proving every individual race a second time, consistent with the frozen plan's own verification strategy (§25).

### Audit

Every mutating action emits a named audit event: `asset.created`, `asset.updated`, `asset.retired`, `asset.marked_lost`, `asset.recovered`, `asset.condition_updated`, `asset.assigned`, `asset.returned`, `asset_assignment.acknowledged`, `asset_incident.reported`, `asset_incident.reviewed`, `asset_incident.dismissed`, `asset_maintenance.started`, `asset_maintenance.completed`, `asset_maintenance.cancelled`, `employee_document.uploaded` + `asset_evidence.attached`. Every GET/list/download read is audit-silent, confirmed both by code inspection and empirically (audit-event counts matching exact mutating-call counts across multiple workstreams' own live QA). Incident metadata never carries the free-text description; evidence metadata carries only filename/MIME/size, never file contents.

### Frontend Surfaces

`/assets` (HR/Admin register + full per-asset lifecycle/incident/maintenance/evidence management), "My Assets" in `/self-service` (ESS), `/team-assets` (manager, read-only), `/asset-workspace` (org-wide operational surface), `/assets-dashboard`, `/asset-reports`. **No browser-driving/screenshot tooling is available in this environment** — no Playwright/chromium-cli/`_electron` was used anywhere across all ten workstreams; every frontend surface was verified via RTL/component tests plus real-HTTP backend verification, not an interactive browser walkthrough. This is stated accurately, not glossed over.

### Security (Final)

RLS 89/89 enabled, 0 disabled, 0 permissive policies; Supabase security advisor shows 89/89 INFO-only `rls_enabled_no_policy` findings, 0 ERROR-level, at every re-check across all ten workstreams. No direct frontend Supabase access anywhere in the Assets surfaces. Evidence is authenticated-download-only with no public URL. No new RLS policies were required (the platform's existing deny-by-default architecture covers every Assets table). No secrets committed; no production access at any point in the phase.

### Verification (W103, final)

**Result: PASS.** Backend **1608/1608**. Frontend **583/583**. Integrated live QA **117/117** assertions on the corrected run. Typecheck clean under both the root `tsc --build` project-reference path and the full `pnpm run build`'s own per-package path. All 3 production builds succeed. OpenAPI/codegen deterministic (3 runs, byte-identical). Zero migration drift. RLS 89/89. Browser automation unavailable (disclosed, not glossed over). **Zero product defects** — the first QA run's 7 failures were all independently reclassified as QA-script defects (3 from an incorrect expected HTTP status on the assign/reassign routes — the shipped `201` is correct; 4 cascading from one incorrect test-file MIME type), corrected, and the verification rerun clean. The `express-rate-limit` login-limiter environment finding is recorded accurately as an environment/QA-pacing interaction, never mischaracterized as a product defect.

### Known Non-Blocking Items

1. No repository-local lint tooling — pre-existing platform-wide gap, unchanged, not addressed by this phase.
2. Browser-driving/screenshot automation is unavailable in this environment — disclosed accurately throughout every workstream; all UI verification used RTL/component tests plus real-HTTP backend verification.
3. CSV spreadsheet formula-injection escaping remains a shared platform-wide hardening gap (Assets' own `toCsv()` reuses the identical, already-known-unescaped shape used by Performance/Learning/the generic reporting module) — not fixed here, not unique to Assets.
4. No malware scanning is performed on Asset evidence uploads (signature/MIME/size validation only, matching the platform's existing document-upload rigor everywhere else).
5. Physical evidence-file cleanup must always be explicit — a database cascade does not delete a file on local disk; this discipline was applied and independently verified in every relevant workstream's own QA.
6. Offboarding UI/hard-block integration remains intentionally deferred (Owner Decision 5) — Assets can identify current outstanding custody and the `asset_unreturned_by_employee` report exists for warning/reporting purposes, but there is no termination hard block and no `employee_exit_processes` UI coupling.

### Approved Deferrals / V1 Boundaries

Per the frozen plan's own explicit scope, Phase 3E V1 intentionally excludes: procurement, purchase orders, a vendor-management platform, warehouse/consumables inventory, depreciation and accounting journals, RFID/barcode/GPS tracking, MDM, fleet management, automatic maintenance scheduling, insurance management, reservations, payroll deductions for loss/damage, complex multi-step approval workflows, and a hard offboarding block. None of these were built, and none are represented as built anywhere in this phase's own documentation.

### Execution-Order Note

W102 (Dashboard & Reporting) was implemented and committed **before** W101 (Internal Asset Workspace) in session execution order, because an earlier prompt mislabeled Dashboard & Reporting's own scope as "W101." This was caught during mandatory reconciliation, raised explicitly with the user (`AskUserQuestion`) rather than silently resolved, and the described scope was built and committed under its correct frozen label (W102); the real W101 was then built in a subsequent workstream, filling the gap exactly as frozen. **The frozen plan's own §24 workstream numbering was never renumbered or altered** — `W101 = Internal Asset Workspace`, `W102 = Dashboard & Reporting`, exactly as originally frozen, regardless of the order in which they were actually implemented.

## Phase 3D Completion Report (W94)

All ten workstreams (W85–W94) are complete. Checking against `docs/PHASE_3D_LEARNING_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`'s own §29 workstream table and §30 Definition of Done, item by item:

- **W85** — Learning Foundation & Module Activation. Yes — 5 tables migrated (`0039`), RLS enabled inline, 5 permissions seeded, module `learning` flipped `hidden`→`active`, `lib/learningAuthorization.ts` foundation. Schema + auth primitives only, no routes/frontend, exactly as scoped.
- **W86** — Course Catalog & Sessions. Yes — org-owned course catalog (`draft`/`active`/`archived`), instructor-led session scheduling (`scheduled`/`completed`/`cancelled`, permanently locked once terminal), `/learning-courses` HR/L&D admin page. Zero enrollment logic.
- **W87** — Enrollment, Assignment & Approval. Yes — the two-axis model, three origins, atomic session-capacity protection, full historical snapshotting, mandatory-cancellation rules.
- **W88** — Employee Self-Service: My Learning. Yes — own-scoped catalog/request/progress, no second business-rules engine.
- **W89** — Manager & Instructor Actions. Yes — manager-of-record and instructor-of-record kept independent; the genuine W88 self-completion defect found and fixed; the genuine W89→W90 certificate-timing contradiction found, raised, and resolved through explicit product direction rather than silently decided.
- **W90** — Certificates & Evidence. Yes — the deferred certificate-timing resolution permanently integrated into `completeEnrollment`'s own atomic transaction; evidence reusing `employee_documents`/`fileStorage` verbatim.
- **W91** — Internal HR/L&D Workspace. Yes — zero new backend code, every mutation reuses an existing W87/W89/W90 route.
- **W92** — Learning Dashboard & Reporting. Yes — six W92-specific implementation-time decisions applied exactly as directed, all independently reconciled against the shipped code in W93.
- **W93** — Phase 3D Verification. **PASS WITH FIXES** — one small frontend filter-display defect found and fixed; two suspected audit-coverage gaps investigated and confirmed as false alarms, not defects.

### Executive Summary

Phase 3D delivered a complete, tenant-isolated Learning & Development module end to end: module activation → course/session catalog → enrollment with three origins and manager-of-record/HR approval → employee self-service progression → manager/instructor actions → system-issued certificates integrated into the authoritative completion transaction → evidence attachments → an internal HR/L&D operational workspace → a dashboard and 3 CSV-exportable reports — on top of the completed Foundation, Phase 2A, Phase 2B, Phase 3A Recruitment, Phase 3B Attendance, and Phase 3C Performance. Nine implementation/verification workstreams (W85–W93) each shipped independently reviewed, tested, and live-QA'd against the real development database; W93 verified the phase as one integrated system (not isolated per-workstream re-runs), reconciled W92's own six implementation-time decisions directly against the shipped code, found and fixed one small genuine defect, and closed two suspected-but-unreal audit gaps; W94 (this report) formally closes the phase.

**Two load-bearing cross-workstream resolutions carried into this report:** (1) W89 discovered a genuine contradiction between §10.4 rule 4 (certificate issuance in the same transaction as completion) and W89's own frozen "no certificate logic" boundary — raised explicitly via `AskUserQuestion` rather than silently decided, resolved by deferring issuance entirely to W90; W90 then permanently closed it by nesting issuance inside `completeEnrollment`'s own transaction, verified under a genuine concurrent-request race. (2) W89 also found and fixed a genuine pre-existing defect in W88's own shipped code (`advanceEnrollmentProgress` let an employee self-complete an assessed self-paced enrollment with no assessment result ever recorded) — fixed with a permanent regression test, re-confirmed still holding in W93's own integrated QA.

### Workstreams Completed

- **W85 — Learning Foundation & Module Activation.** Schema (5 tables, migration `0039`), module `learning` `hidden`→`active`, 5 permissions seeded, `lib/learningAuthorization.ts`.
- **W86 — Course Catalog & Sessions.** `lib/learningCourses.ts`, `lib/learningCourseSessions.ts` — course/session lifecycle, `/learning-courses` admin page.
- **W87 — Enrollment, Assignment & Approval.** `lib/learningEnrollments.ts` — the two-axis model, three origins, atomic capacity protection.
- **W88 — Employee Self-Service: My Learning.** New "My Learning" ESS tab, one new route (`PATCH .../progress`), reuses W87's service layer entirely.
- **W89 — Manager & Instructor Actions.** `/learning-team-training` — manager-of-record and instructor-of-record actions, kept independent.
- **W90 — Certificates & Evidence.** `lib/learningCertificates.ts`, `lib/learningEnrollmentEvidence.ts` — system-issued certificates, evidence reusing `employee_documents`.
- **W91 — Internal HR/L&D Workspace.** `/learning-enrollments` — org-wide operational surface, zero new backend code.
- **W92 — Learning Dashboard & Reporting.** `lib/learningReporting.ts`, `/learning`, `/learning-reports` — dashboard tiles + 3 reports.
- **W93 — Phase 3D Verification.** Full integrated verification pass; one small defect fixed, two suspected gaps closed as false alarms.
- **W94 — Phase 3D Completion Report.** This report.

### Shipped Learning Capabilities

**Foundation & configuration:** module activation with 5 permissions (`learning.read.own`/`.write.own`/`.review.write`/`.manage`/`.reports.read`, no `learning.read.team`); course categories via the existing Master Data `training_category` domain (free-text `categoryCode`, no dedicated Learning category table); Learning never auto-enabled for any organization — verified live, repeatedly, throughout every workstream's own QA.

**Course catalog & sessions:** organization-owned courses (`draft → active → archived`, freely PATCH-settable, archived locks further edits until reactivated); `self_paced`/`instructor_led` delivery; assessment-requirement and certificate-eligibility/validity-period configuration; instructor-led session scheduling (`scheduled → completed | cancelled`, one-way, permanently locked once terminal) with same-org `instructorEmployeeId` validation and optional capacity. No quizzes, SCORM, xAPI, video hosting, or content-authoring exists anywhere — the platform has no content-delivery/player infrastructure, and none was built.

**Enrollment model:** two independent axes — `approvalStatus` (`pending`/`approved`/`rejected`/`auto_approved`) and the sole-authoritative `status` (`assigned → in_progress → completed | failed | cancelled`) — never collapsed anywhere in the backend or any of the five frontend surfaces that render them. Every enrollment starts `status = 'assigned'` regardless of approval state (a genuinely frozen, non-obvious rule — approval gates actionability, not row existence). Three origins: `employee_requested` (manager-of-record approval when the course requires it, employee can never self-approve — structurally excluded, not merely convention-gated), `hr_assigned` and `manager_assigned` (both bypass approval entirely — the assigner's own authority is the approval). Full historical snapshot capture at creation (course title/category/delivery-mode/mandatory-at-assignment/assessment-requirement/certificate-eligibility/validity/department/position/manager-of-record) — verified live, repeatedly, immutable to every later course or employee-record edit tested. HR/L&D bulk-assign audience targeting: `all_active`/`department`/`position`/`manual`; a manager may only assign `scope='manual'` to their own current direct reports. Atomic `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` session-capacity protection, hard-blocked (`409`), no waitlist. Mandatory-at-assignment enrollments cannot be employee-cancelled; HR/L&D may cancel or waive with a mandatory reason. No terminal enrollment (`completed`/`failed`/`cancelled`) may ever be reopened or mutated — retraining always creates a new enrollment row; verified live via repeat-transition `409`s throughout W87–W93.

**Employee Self-Service:** "My Learning" tab, independently module-gated from every other ESS tab — active-course discovery, self-enroll/request, own enrollment list showing both axes independently, own self-paced start/progress, own certificates, own evidence. An assessed self-paced enrollment cannot be self-completed without a recorded assessment outcome — a genuine defect in W88's own original code, found and fixed during W89, re-confirmed live in W93's own integrated QA.

**Manager & instructor actions:** "My Team Training" — manager-of-record approval/rejection/direct-report assignment (server-derived `reportingManagerId`, never client-supplied); instructor-of-record attendance marking and completion (server-derived from the session's own live `instructorEmployeeId`, never role/permission/manager-status-inferred) — the two relationships kept conceptually and functionally independent even where both share the single `learning.review.write` permission key, verified with one employee holding both relationships on the same enrollment and each relationship individually denied when the other doesn't apply.

**Certificates:** system-issued automatically, inside `completeEnrollment`'s own atomic transaction, gated on that transaction's own successful completion UPDATE — never for a `failed` or ineligible enrollment. One-certificate-per-enrollment guaranteed without a database unique constraint, by the same atomicity that already prevents double-completion — verified under a genuine concurrent-request race in the backend suite, live QA, and re-confirmed again in W93's own integration pass. Title/eligibility/validity-period all read from the enrollment's own historical snapshot, never the live course — verified live repeatedly via course-rename-after-issuance checks. Expiry computed once at issuance and never recomputed or stored as a lifecycle status — "expired" is always a live computation against `expiresAt`, identically in the API description and every frontend renderer; stored statuses are `active`/`revoked` only. Revocation is `learning.manage`-only, requires a mandatory reason, and is permanently terminal — no un-revoke route exists anywhere. `learning_certificates` remains structurally separate from `employee_certifications` (confirmed untouched, 0 rows, throughout every workstream) — no automatic cross-write exists or was built. **No dedicated certificate-file/PDF-generation route exists** — §21's own frozen route table names none, so `learning_certificates.employeeDocumentId` remains schema-level capability only, always null in this shipped system; this was never claimed as built anywhere in this phase's own record.

**Evidence:** enrollment-level supporting documentation, reusing the existing `employee_documents`/`fileStorage`/`documentValidation.ts` layer verbatim — identical file-type allowlist, 10MB cap, signature validation, authenticated-only streamed download, no public URL. Visibility mirrors the enrollment's own own/manager-of-record/instructor-of-record/organization-wide tier, with no stage/status gate (a disclosed, deliberate divergence from Performance's own non-frozen stage-gating precedent, since Learning's frozen text imposes none). No delete route exists (none is frozen).

**Internal HR/L&D workspace:** `/learning-enrollments` — org-wide paginated/filterable enrollment list, an approval queue, administrative corrections (cancel-with-reason, attendance correction, administrative completion), full-audience bulk-assign, and certificate administration (list + mandatory-reason revocation) — every single mutation reuses an existing W87/W89/W90 route verbatim; zero new backend business logic was ever introduced for this workstream. Course/session administration was not duplicated here — it already shipped inside `/learning-courses` in W86.

**Dashboard & reporting:** a zero-filled tile breakdown (`activeCourseCount`, `enrollmentsAssignedCount`, a 5-status enrollment breakdown, `pendingApprovalCount`, `overdueCount`, `certificatesExpiringSoonCount`) — no invented rate/KPI tile anywhere; `overdueCount` excludes every terminal status (a past-due `dueDate` on a `completed`/`failed`/`cancelled` enrollment is never "overdue" again); `certificatesExpiringSoonCount` uses a fixed 30-day V1 window, no caller-supplied override. Three reports (`learning_enrollment_status` row-level with every dimension read from the enrollment's own snapshot; `learning_completion_summary` per-course aggregate, `completionPercentage = completedCount / denominator` where the denominator excludes pending-approval/rejected/cancelled but includes failed, null-safe on a zero denominator; `learning_certificate_expiry` row-level with `computedStatus` always live-derived `active`/`expired`/`revoked`, never a stored `expired` value), registered in the shared Reporting Foundation registry for catalog discoverability only and executed exclusively through a dedicated, visibility-scoped route — confirmed in W93 to be genuinely unreachable through the generic report runner. Authorization throughout is `learning.reports.read` only, with own/manager-of-record/organization-wide scope identical across the dashboard and all 3 reports — **deliberately no instructor-of-record reporting tier**, narrower than `learning.review.write`'s own action-scope. CSV export scope is always identical to the already-authorized JSON scope for the same request — verified both by unit test and live, twice (once in W92, independently re-confirmed in W93).

**Cross-cutting:** full audit coverage on every meaningful mutation (enrollment requested/assigned/approved/rejected/cancelled/started/completed/failed/attendance-marked; certificate issued/revoked; evidence attached; course created/updated/archived; session created/updated) — re-confirmed directly against the code in W93 after two items were initially and incorrectly suspected missing (a literal-string grep artifact, not a real gap); tenant isolation and RLS deny-by-default on all 5 tables; zero client-side scoring/lifecycle computation anywhere in the frontend; batched/paginated reads throughout, no N+1 in any hot read path including the W92 dashboard/report aggregations.

### Frozen-Plan Reconciliation

Interpretations and reconciliations made during implementation, each already individually documented in this file's own W85–W93 header paragraphs, consolidated here:

- **The W89→W90 certificate-timing contradiction** (§10.4 rule 4 vs. W89's own frozen "no certificate logic" boundary) — a genuine contradiction in the frozen document itself, raised explicitly rather than silently resolved, closed by owner direction (defer to W90) and then permanently integrated by W90 into `completeEnrollment`'s own transaction.
- **The W88 self-completion defect** — not a frozen-plan ambiguity but a genuine pre-existing code defect, found by W89, fixed with a permanent regression test, re-confirmed live in W93.
- **`GET .../learning/enrollments` (org-wide) is `learning.manage`-only**, mirroring Performance's own actual-shipped W80 precedent rather than the frozen planning text's parenthetical "(scoped)" alternative — the identical reconciliation Performance itself already made.
- **No `/learning-sessions` route was built** — session administration already shipped inside `/learning-courses`'s own course-detail dialog in W86, exactly the "if not already built there" case §29's own W91 line anticipates.
- **Evidence carries no stage/status visibility gate**, a disclosed, deliberate divergence from Performance's own W82 (non-frozen) stage-gating precedent, since Learning's own frozen §21 text imposes none.
- **W92's six implementation-time decisions** (scope model; overdue definition excluding terminal statuses; a fixed 30-day certificate-expiry window; no instructor-of-record reporting tier; the completion-summary denominator's exact exclusion/inclusion rules; the dashboard tile set) — all independently reconciled directly against the shipped code in W93, not merely trusted from W92's own prose.
- **The W93 report-filter defect** — `/learning-reports` rendered Course/Department/Position filters unconditionally, but `learning_certificate_expiry`'s own backend runner only ever honors `employeeId`/`status`; fixed by hiding those controls specifically for that report key, with a permanent regression test. Recorded here as **fixed**, not as an outstanding issue.
- **Two suspected audit-coverage gaps, resolved as false alarms** — `learning_enrollment.approved`/`.rejected` and `learning_course.updated`/`.archived` are both genuinely emitted; a literal-string grep during W93's own discovery pass had simply missed two computed-ternary `eventType` expressions. No code change was needed.
- **CSV formula-injection escaping remains absent** — a pre-existing, shared platform gap (also present in every other module's own CSV export route), not introduced by Learning and not fixed here.
- **No malware scanning on evidence uploads** — extension/MIME/file-signature validation exists (reused from Phase 2A's `documentValidation.ts`), but no scanning engine; a future storage-security enhancement, not claimed as built.

None of the above are presented as defects except the one genuinely fixed in W93 (recorded as fixed) and the one genuinely fixed in W89 (recorded as fixed) — every other item is either the frozen plan's own explicit exclusion, an Owner Decision's own approved answer actually taken, a reconciliation between the frozen document's general prose and its own more specific controlling statement, or (in the certificate-timing case) a genuine contradiction in the frozen document itself, found and resolved through explicit product direction rather than silently decided.

### Known Non-Blocking Items

1. **No repository-local ESLint configuration/script** — pre-existing tooling gap (predates Phase 3D entirely), not fixed here.
2. **No browser automation tooling available on this host** — environment limitation, stated explicitly throughout the phase; RTL + live HTTP QA substituted throughout.
3. **CSV formula-injection escaping absent** — platform-wide hardening item, predates Learning, not fixed here.
4. **No malware scanning for evidence uploads** — future storage-security enhancement, not built.
5. **No dedicated certificate-file/PDF-generation route** — intentionally outside frozen V1 scope; `employeeDocumentId` remains schema-level capability only.
6. **A physical evidence file left on disk after a QA script's own DB-level cleanup, once, during W93** — the `employee_documents` row itself cascaded away correctly when the underlying employee record was deleted (verified: `employeeId` carries `onDelete: cascade`), but a Postgres row cascade cannot delete a file on disk; caught by the same "verify physical files independently, not just DB rows" discipline W90 already established, and the disposable file was found and deleted by hand. This is an operational QA-cleanup consideration for any future disposable-data script that deletes an employee record with attached evidence, not a Learning business-function defect — the application's own normal business flows never delete an employee (or a certificate's underlying enrollment) as a matter of course, so this pattern was never exercised by real application logic, only by a QA script's own aggressive teardown order.

None of the above are classified as defects or blockers — items 1–2 are tooling/environment gaps outside this phase's control; items 3–5 are frozen-scope exclusions or explicitly out-of-scope hardening items, already carried forward unchanged from Performance's own identical items; item 6 is an accurately-disclosed QA-operational note, not a product defect, and was fully remediated (the one file found was deleted) the moment it was discovered.

### Approved Deferrals (V1)

Confirmed still deferred, and never accidentally built anywhere in the shipped code (independently grep-verified against the full `lib/learning*.ts`/`routes/learning*.ts` surface for this report): quizzes/rich assessment engine, SCORM, xAPI, video hosting, course content authoring, gamification, badges, a CPD engine, automatic renewal/recurring-assignment scheduling (renewal or retraining is always a new enrollment row — no background-job infrastructure exists on this platform), session waitlists (capacity is hard-blocked, `409`, no waitlist), formal reopening of a terminal enrollment (retraining is always a new enrollment row; every historical outcome is permanently immutable once terminal), Performance competency coupling, and `employee_skills` coupling. `learning_certificates` also remains structurally separate from `employee_certifications`, with zero automatic cross-write, confirmed untouched throughout the entire phase.

**PRODUCTION UNTOUCHED**, throughout the entirety of Phase 3D (W85–W94) and this report. No connection was made to any production environment; migration `0039` was never applied there; Learning was never enabled there; no Learning data of any kind (courses, sessions, enrollments, certificates, evidence) exists there; no production domain, session, or security configuration was changed. Production rollout — for Learning — remains a separate, explicitly-gated decision requiring its own preflight, review, and approval.

Yes — `hr_review → finalized` with optional override (`hrOverrideScore` always distinct from `computedOverallScore`, mandatory reason), controlled reopen (`performance.manage`, mandatory reason, target-stage allow-list, `revisionNumber` increment, audit) — and, as of W83A, genuinely exercised from a real `acknowledged` source for the first time, confirmed correct with no code change needed.
- **W80** — Internal HR/Manager Review List. Yes — paginated, filterable org-wide HR workspace at `/performance-reviews`, distinct from W78's own manager-scoped `/performance-team`.
- **W81** — Performance Dashboard & Reporting. Yes — zero-filled lifecycle tile breakdown, no invented rate/KPI tiles.
- **W82** — Evidence/Attachments. Yes — `performance_review_evidence` join table over the existing `employee_documents`/`fileStorage` architecture, no second storage provider.
- **W83** — Phase 3C Verification. **PASS WITH FIXES** — one small display defect found and fixed (acknowledgement inferred from a timestamp instead of `status`); one gap found and correctly *reported, not silently implemented* (employee acknowledgement approved and fully specified but never assigned to any W73–W82 workstream).
- **W83A** — Employee Acknowledgement Gap Closure. **COMPLETE** — implemented exactly the one missing `finalized → acknowledged` transition W83 flagged, nothing more.
- **W84** (this report) — declares completion status accurately below, records both W83's verification evidence and W83A's closure, and does not claim any of §9's explicitly-excluded scope as built.

### Executive Summary

Phase 3C delivered a complete, tenant-isolated Performance Management module end to end: module activation → rating scales/templates → cycles/assignment → goal proposals with manager accept/reject → employee self-assessment → manager review with deterministic scoring → HR finalization with optional override → controlled reopen → **employee acknowledgement** → an internal HR review workspace → a manager team-reviews list → a dashboard → 3 CSV-exportable reports → evidence/attachments — on top of the completed Foundation, Phase 2A, Phase 2B, Phase 3A Recruitment, and Phase 3B Attendance. Ten workstreams (W73–W82) each shipped independently reviewed, tested, and live-QA'd against the real development database; W83 verified the phase as a whole and found one small defect (fixed) plus one genuine scope gap (acknowledgement, correctly reported rather than silently patched in a verification-only workstream); W83A closed exactly that gap with a narrowly-scoped corrective workstream; W84 (this report) formally closes the phase.

**A load-bearing point carried forward from W83/W83A into this report:** the frozen plan's own §0 states all six Owner Decisions "have been reconciled" into every downstream section including §35's workstream table — but Owner Decision 2 (acknowledgement) was in fact never assigned there. This was a genuine gap in the frozen document itself, not an implementation shortcut by any of W73–W82; each of those workstreams correctly built exactly what its own §35 scope line specified, and none of their own lines mentioned acknowledgement. W83's verification-only charter meant it could report but not fix this; W83A was the correct, minimal, dedicated mechanism to close it before this completion report could honestly declare the phase done.

### Shipped Performance Capabilities

**Foundation & configuration:** module activation with 6 permissions; org-owned rating scales with configurable, ordered levels (structurally locked once any review uses the scale); review templates with `goalsWeight`/`competenciesWeight` and weighted template competencies.

**Cycles & assignment:** Performance cycles (`draft → open → closed → archived`); `all_active`/`department`/`position`/`manual` eligibility resolution; atomic review generation, one review per employee per cycle, reviewer resolved from `reportingManagerId`; every review starts directly in `self_assessment` (no observable `draft` review state — the cycle's own `open` action, performed by `generate-reviews` itself, is what was `draft` before); full historical snapshotting at creation (department, position, reviewer, template competencies/weights, scoring precision, acknowledgement requirement).

**Goals:** employee-proposed (`employee_proposed`/`proposed`, pending manager decision) and manager-created (`manager`/`accepted` immediately) goals; manager accept/reject on proposals; `actualResult` is manager-owned; `proposed`/`rejected` goals structurally excluded from scoring; qualitative goals carry zero scoring weight by design.

**Self-assessment:** ESS "My Performance" tab — own-review-only, competency self-ratings from the review's own configured scale, goal comments, goal proposals, atomic `self_assessment → manager_review` submission with full readiness validation, post-submit employee lock.

**Manager review:** reviewer-of-record authorization via the snapshotted `reviewerEmployeeId` (never a live re-check); "My Team Reviews"; manager competency ratings and per-goal `actualResult`/comments; N/A marking with required reason and weight redistribution; deterministic `computedOverallScore`, computed and persisted at manager submission (not at HR finalization, per W79's own documented reconciliation of a genuine internal inconsistency in the frozen text); atomic `manager_review → hr_review`.

**HR review, finalization & reopen:** HR finalization with an always-optional, always-distinct override (`hrOverrideScore` + mandatory `hrOverrideReason`, `computedOverallScore` never overwritten); controlled reopen (`performance.manage`, mandatory reason, target-stage allow-list of `self_assessment`/`manager_review`/`hr_review`, `revisionNumber` increment, full audit, downstream-field clearing that preserves upstream content) — now genuinely reachable from a real `acknowledged` source, not merely written for forward compatibility.

**Employee acknowledgement (W83A):** `finalized → acknowledged`, own-review-only, "seen," never "agreed," optional final comment, zero score mutation.

**Internal/manager workspaces:** a paginated, filterable HR-wide review list (W80); a manager-scoped team-reviews list (W78) — kept structurally distinct, never merged.

**Dashboard & reporting:** a zero-filled lifecycle tile breakdown (W81); 3 implemented, CSV-exportable report keys (`performance_review_status`, `performance_scores`, `performance_goal_results`); the 4th candidate key (`performance_rating_distribution`) correctly left unregistered — no frozen band/bin semantics exist to build against.

**Evidence/attachments:** file evidence per review/goal, reusing the existing `employee_documents`/`fileStorage` architecture with a lightweight join table — no second storage provider, no new upload/download infrastructure.

**Cross-cutting:** full audit coverage on every mutating transition; tenant isolation and RLS deny-by-default on all 9 tables; zero client-side scoring anywhere in the frontend; batched/paginated reads throughout, no N+1 in any hot read path.

### Frozen-Plan Reconciliation

Interpretations and reconciliations made during implementation, each already individually documented in this file's own W73–W83A header paragraphs, consolidated here:

- **`computedOverallScore` is computed at `manager_review → hr_review` (manager submission), not at `hr_review → finalized`** — §10.1 row 4 and §16 both literally say the latter, but three independent pieces of evidence outweigh that phrase: the per-goal `computedScore` column's own schema comment says "computed at manager-submit time"; §10.4's own reopen-to-`manager_review` worked example lists `computedOverallScore` among fields *cleared* when reopening from `hr_review`/`finalized` back to `manager_review` (only possible if it was already set before reaching `hr_review`); and the master brief's own override-QA framing treats it as already-known before any override is applied.
- **`acknowledgementRequiredSnapshot` is not a server-side gate on the acknowledgement route** — §10.1 row 5's own text ("if false, acknowledgement is optional but still permitted") describes ESS-UI framing, not an authorization precondition; inventing a second gate on top of `status` would itself violate the phase's own "status is the sole authoritative field" rule. Verified live: a review with the snapshot `false` acknowledges successfully.
- **Employee acknowledgement was approved (Owner Decision 2) and fully specified (§10.1 row 5, §17) but never assigned to any W73–W82 workstream** — a genuine gap in the frozen document's own §35 table, not an implementation shortcut; found by W83, closed by W83A, described in full above.
- **`performance_rating_distribution` remains deferred** — no band/bin semantics are defined anywhere in the frozen document; inventing one would violate this session's "no invented rate/KPI" discipline, consistent with Attendance's own identical precedent.
- **No completion-percentage or average-score dashboard tile** — the frozen plan's own "no invented rate/KPI" scope; the W81 master prompt's own "potential concepts" suggested them, but neither is frozen anywhere, so neither was built.
- **CSV formula-injection escaping remains absent** — a pre-existing, shared platform gap (also present in Attendance's and Recruitment's own dedicated CSV export routes and the generic `lib/reporting.ts` `toCsv` helper), not introduced by Performance and not fixed here — classified as a platform-wide hardening item, not a Phase 3C blocker.
- **No malware scanning on evidence/document uploads** — extension/MIME/file-signature validation exists (reused from Phase 2A's `documentValidation.ts`), but no scanning engine; a future storage-security enhancement, not claimed as built.
- **The competency-rating route (`PATCH .../competencies/:competencyId`) is dual-purpose, not two routes** — §27 named no such route at all; W77 added it for the employee's own self-rating path, and W78 extended the same route to also serve the reviewer's manager-rating path (dispatched server-side by caller identity), rather than inventing a second, near-duplicate endpoint.
- **No formal appeal/dispute workflow** — Owner Decision 3, approved V1 deferral; an optional `employeeFinalComment` at acknowledgement is the only outlet for employee disagreement, and never blocks or reverses finalization.
- **No Performance Improvement Plan (PIP)** — out of frozen V1 scope, not attempted.
- **No custom template question types beyond the frozen competency/goal model** — out of frozen V1 scope.
- **Employee self-rating does not contribute numerically to any score** — Owner Decision 1, an explicit approved design choice, not a limitation.

None of the above are presented as defects — each is either the frozen plan's own explicit exclusion, an Owner Decision's own approved answer actually taken, a reconciliation between the frozen document's general prose and its own more specific, controlling statement, or (in acknowledgement's case) a genuine gap in the frozen document's own workstream assignment, found and closed within the phase itself rather than silently carried forward.
