### Permissions

**Exactly 6 permissions, seeded per §7's frozen matrix — no permission was ever added beyond W73, including by W83A:**

- **`performance.read.own`** — own/reviewer-of-record read; the coarse gate for `my-reviews`, review detail, dashboard, reports.
- **`performance.write.own`** — own self-assessment (goals, self-ratings, comments, proposals), and **acknowledge a finalized review**.
- **`performance.review.write`** — reviewer-of-record: manager competency ratings, goal decisions, manager-review submission, team-reviews.
- **`performance.manage`** — organization-wide configuration/administration: scales, templates, cycles, assignment, reopen.
- **`performance.finalize`** — HR finalize + override, deliberately distinct from `performance.manage`.
- **`performance.reports.read`** — dashboard + reports.

**No `performance.read.team` exists** — reviewer-of-record visibility is resolved entirely in the service layer via the review's own snapshotted `reviewerEmployeeId`, never a permission grant. **No acknowledgement-specific permission was added** — acknowledgement reuses the already-existing `performance.write.own`, per §10.1 row 5's own explicit assignment.

**Seeded role mapping:** `employee` holds `read.own`/`write.own`/`review.write`/`reports.read` only (no `manage`, no `finalize` — no over-granting); `hr_manager`/`org_admin`/`super_admin` hold all 6.

### Module Gating

`performance` — seeded `hidden` at Foundation time, flipped `active` by W73; no organization auto-enabled by module availability alone (WWM and Acme both confirmed disabled at every checkpoint outside each workstream's own bracketed, restored-afterward live QA window, most recently re-confirmed after W83A's own cleanup: an empty `organization_modules` query result, byte-identical to the pre-QA baseline). Every route composes `requireModuleEnabled("performance")` paired with a specific permission check — never a substitute for authorization. Every frontend route wraps in the platform's module-gating pattern; the ESS "My Performance" tab checks `performance` accessibility independently within the ESS page, degrading to a controlled message (the identical My Attendance/My Leave/Internal Vacancies pattern).

### Authorization Matrix

- **Employee:** own self-assessment, own goal proposals, own competency self-ratings, own acknowledgement. Cannot rate as a manager, decide goal proposals, finalize, override, or reopen; cannot target another employee's review (server-derived identity on every write); cannot reach the organization-wide list/dashboard/reports beyond own/reviewer scope.
- **Manager (reviewer of record):** the review's own snapshotted `reviewerEmployeeId` only — never a live `reportingManagerId` re-check — manager competency ratings, goal `actualResult`/decisions, manager-review submission, team-reviews list. Cannot finalize, override, or reopen.
- **HR (`performance.finalize`/`performance.manage`):** finalize + override, cycle/template/scale administration, reopen, organization-wide list/dashboard/reports.
- **Org Admin / Super Admin:** inherit the full HR-equivalent permission set via the seeded role matrix; the platform's own established hostname-binding/tenant-consistency behavior is unaffected by anything Performance-specific.
- **Module disabled:** denied independently of role or permission — confirmed live throughout W73–W83A.
- **No membership:** denied — confirmed live repeatedly (WWM↔Acme cross-org tokens, unauthenticated requests, both directions, throughout every workstream including W83A's own live QA).

### Lifecycle & Scoring

**Review lifecycle (the fully reachable chain, as of W83A):**

```
draft → self_assessment → manager_review → hr_review → finalized → acknowledged
```

`draft` is never observed in practice — `generate-reviews` creates reviews directly in `self_assessment` as part of the same atomic transaction that opens the cycle. `status` is the sole authoritative workflow field throughout — no route or service function anywhere infers stage from a nullable timestamp instead (enforced at the function-signature level from W76 onward, explicitly re-verified by direct code inspection in W83, and preserved by the one frontend defect W83 found and fixed).

**Cycle lifecycle (independent):** `draft → open → closed → archived`. `open` (performed by `generate-reviews`) is the only action that mutates data.

**Scoring model (final, as implemented):** manager scores are the sole official input — employee self-ratings are informational/comparative and structurally excluded from every formula (Owner Decision 1). Numeric/percentage/currency/rating goal types compute a normalized 0–100 item score against their target; boolean goals score 100/0; qualitative goals carry zero weight and never enter the numeric formula. Competency scoring normalizes the manager's rating against the review's own configured rating-scale range. N/A marking (goal or competency, with a required reason) redistributes that item's weight across the remaining applicable items in its own section; a whole section with zero applicable items redistributes its entire section weight to the other section; both sections empty blocks submission entirely. `scoringPrecisionSnapshot` (copied from organization settings at review creation, never re-read afterward) controls display rounding; round-half-up is used throughout. `computedOverallScore` is computed and persisted at manager-review submission (§79's own reconciliation, above) — never recomputed at finalize, never recomputed by acknowledgement or by anything else downstream.

### HR Override / Effective Score

`computedOverallScore` (manager-generated) and `hrOverrideScore` (optional HR final override, mandatory reason when supplied) are always stored and displayed as two distinct values — an override never overwrites or erases the manager's own score. The **effective score** is `hrOverrideScore ?? computedOverallScore` throughout every surface that displays or reports it (internal workspace, dashboard, reports). Live-verified in both W83 and W83A: a manager score of `88.00` with a `92.50` override remains `88.00`/`92.50` distinctly — through finalization, through acknowledgement, and again through a reopen-then-refinalize cycle, with no accidental carryover of a prior override across a reopen.

### Finalization & Reopen

**Finalization:** `hr_review → finalized`, `performance.finalize`, an atomic conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE status = 'hr_review'` (repeat/concurrent finalization → controlled `409`, never a silent double-transition), setting `hrFinalizedAt`, optionally applying an override in the same call. Ordinary employee/manager/HR mutation locks resume immediately.

**Reopen:** `performance.manage`, valid only from `manager_review`/`hr_review`/`finalized`/`acknowledged` (the last now genuinely reachable, verified live for the first time in W83A), mandatory `reopenReason`, target stage one of `self_assessment`/`manager_review`/`hr_review` (never forward, never into `draft`/`acknowledged`), atomic conditional update, `revisionNumber` increments by exactly 1, full `beforeState`/`afterState` audit. Reopen clears only the timestamp/decision fields strictly downstream of the target stage (e.g., reopening to `manager_review` clears `managerReviewSubmittedAt`/`hrFinalizedAt`/`acknowledgedAt`/`computedOverallScore`/`hrOverrideScore`/`hrOverrideReason`) — it never blanks the underlying goal/competency/self-assessment content, and never erases prior history (every submission's own audit event already permanently captured its own `beforeState`/`afterState` at the time it happened).

### Acknowledgement (W83A)

Acknowledgement means **"I have seen this review"** — explicitly, deliberately, and by design, it does **not** mean "I agree with this review." Route: `POST /organizations/:organizationId/performance/reviews/:id/acknowledge`. Authorization: `performance.write.own` + server-derived own-employee identity (never a client-supplied `employeeId`). Prerequisite: the review's own `status = 'finalized'`. Transition: `finalized → acknowledged`, atomic, server sets `acknowledgedAt`; an optional `employeeFinalComment` may be recorded in the same call, informational only, never blocking, never a formal appeal, never mutating any score or manager/HR field. Repeat or concurrent acknowledgement returns a controlled `409` — proven under a genuine concurrent race in the test suite, not just a sequential simulation. **`acknowledgementRequiredSnapshot` implemented semantics, stated precisely and without exaggeration:** the endpoint does **not** check this flag as a precondition — a finalized own review may be acknowledged through the endpoint regardless of whether its `acknowledgementRequiredSnapshot` is `true` or `false`; the flag's role is display/expectation framing for the ESS UI (whether the surface presents acknowledgement as expected of the employee), not an authorization gate. This was verified live in W83A: a review with the snapshot explicitly `false` acknowledged successfully through the real endpoint.

### Goals

Employee-created goals begin `employee_proposed`/`proposed`; the manager (reviewer of record) may accept or reject them, each direction independently authorized and audited. Manager-created goals are `accepted` immediately per the frozen implementation — no manager self-approval step exists because the manager is already the authorizing party for that path. An employee can never make their own proposal official; only the reviewer of record can. `proposed` and `rejected` goals are structurally excluded from scoring — enforced in the scoring function itself, not merely by UI convention. `actualResult` is manager-owned; the employee never writes it. Qualitative goals remain zero-weight/non-numeric, per the frozen design — they carry a comment/assessment but never enter the score formula.

### Self-Assessment

ESS "My Performance" tab, own-review only. The employee may propose new goals, comment on goals, self-rate competencies against the review's own configured rating scale (a value must match one of that scale's configured levels — never an arbitrary number), and submit. Self-rating is contextual/comparative only — it never contributes numerically to any score (Owner Decision 1). Submission readiness is validated at the atomic `self_assessment → manager_review` transition (every problem listed at once, never just the first); post-submit, every employee-writable field locks — enforced both by the stage check and by the write route's own Zod schema never accepting manager-only fields regardless of stage (defense in depth).

### Manager Review

Reviewer-of-record authorization is entirely server-derived from the review's own snapshotted `reviewerEmployeeId` — never a live `reportingManagerId` comparison, since a later manager change must never reassign an in-flight or historical review. "My Team Reviews" lists exactly the manager's own reviewer-of-record set. The manager records `actualResult`/comments per goal and a competency rating per competency, decides any `proposed` goals, marks N/A with a required reason where applicable, and submits — an atomic `manager_review → hr_review` transition that computes and persists `computedOverallScore`. Post-submit, every manager-writable field locks identically to how self-assessment locks after employee submission.

### Historical Integrity

Every review permanently snapshots, at creation: department, position, and reviewer (fixed even if the employee's own current department/position/manager later changes); the template's competency set and weights (a later template edit never rewrites existing review criteria); `goalsWeight`/`competenciesWeight`; `scoringPrecisionSnapshot`; `acknowledgementRequiredSnapshot` (a later organization-wide settings change never retroactively alters an in-flight or historical review). The rating scale itself is kept as a live reference, made safe only because it is structurally immutable once any review uses it (editing is blocked once `usageCount > 0`) — the platform's own "don't duplicate for identity/history concepts unnecessarily" discipline applied deliberately here rather than snapshotting every level row into every review. Goal definitions are inherently review-owned records from creation, never a separate library that could diverge. Finalized (and acknowledged) reviews are durable historical business records, mutated afterward only by the explicit, fully-audited HR reopen action — never silently.

### Rating Scales / Templates

Rating scales are organization-owned, with no hardcoded scale values anywhere in the codebase — every configured level is user-defined (value, label, description, sort order). Once any review uses a scale, its level set is structurally locked (edits blocked, `409`); archiving and creating a new scale is the only path forward, preventing any retroactive change to historical meaning. Templates carry `goalsWeight`/`competenciesWeight` (must sum with their own internal competency weights to exactly 100 within each section) and a competency composition editable freely until the template is archived (templates carry no usage lock, since reviews snapshot their competencies at creation rather than referencing the template live). Both scales and templates are strictly same-organization-referenced — no cross-tenant reference is possible anywhere in the create/update paths.

### Cycles / Assignment

Cycle lifecycle: `draft → open → closed → archived`. Eligible-employee resolution supports `all_active` (every active employee), `department`, `position`, and `manual` (explicit `employeeIds`) scopes. The reviewer is always derived from the employee's own `reportingManagerId` at generation time — never client-supplied. `generate-reviews` is a single atomic transaction: it flips the cycle `draft → open` and inserts one review row per eligible employee (enforced by a unique `(cycleId, employeeId)` index — never more than one review per employee per cycle), each review starting directly in `self_assessment`. No goals are auto-generated by cycle assignment — goals arrive only through the employee-proposal or manager-authoring paths (W76).

### Internal Workspace

**W80 — `/performance-reviews`:** a paginated, filterable internal HR-wide review list — `cycleId`/`status`/`departmentId`/`positionId`/`reviewerId`/`employeeId` filters, each filtering the review's own historical snapshot columns (never live employee data); shows snapshotted department/position, reviewer, status, manager score, HR override, effective score, and revision number; reuses the existing finalize/reopen actions rather than duplicating them. **This did not widen or replace W78's own manager-scoped `/performance-team` list** — the two remain structurally distinct routes with distinct visibility tiers, exactly as built.

### Dashboard

**W81 — `/performance` dashboard, `GET .../performance/dashboard`.** Metrics actually shipped: `activeCycleCount`, `employeesAssignedCount`, a zero-filled six-status breakdown (`draft`/`self_assessment`/`manager_review`/`hr_review`/`finalized`/`acknowledged`), self-assessment pending/submitted counts, manager-review pending/submitted counts, and `proposedGoalsAwaitingDecisionCount`. **No completion-percentage tile, no average-score tile, and no rating-distribution tile exist** — all three were deliberately not built, per the frozen plan's own "no invented rate/KPI" constraint; this was re-confirmed, not merely re-asserted, in both W83 and this report.

### Reporting

Implemented report keys: `performance_review_status`, `performance_scores`, `performance_goal_results` — registered in the shared Reporting Foundation registry for catalog discoverability, executed through a dedicated, visibility-scoped route (`GET .../performance/reports/:reportKey`), never the generic runner. **Deferred:** `performance_rating_distribution` — no frozen band/bin definition exists anywhere in the source document; presenting it as implemented would be inventing scope, so it remains correctly unregistered (confirmed via a live `404` in both W83 and W83A's own QA runs). Own/reviewer/organization-wide visibility mirrors the dashboard exactly. CSV export (`?format=csv`) reuses the platform's established convention; export scope is always identical to the already-authorized JSON scope, with organizationId resolved from the URL/membership, never the query string — a cross-tenant export is structurally impossible.

### CSV Security Gap

Spreadsheet formula-injection escaping remains absent from CSV export across the platform — this predates Performance entirely and equally affects Attendance's and Recruitment's own dedicated report routes plus the generic `lib/reporting.ts` `toCsv` helper. It was **not fixed during Phase 3C**, and is classified as a **platform-wide security/hardening follow-up**, not a Phase 3C blocker — consistent with how it was classified when first identified during Attendance and re-confirmed unchanged in every Performance workstream that touched CSV export.

### Evidence / Attachments

**W82.** Storage reuses the existing `employee_documents`/`fileStorage` architecture verbatim — no second storage provider, no new upload/download infrastructure. `performance_review_evidence` is a lightweight join table pointing into `employee_documents`. Accepted file types: PDF, JPEG, PNG, DOCX, XLSX; maximum 10MB; validated by extension, MIME type, and file signature (reusing Phase 2A's `documentValidation.ts`), not filename alone. Storage keys/paths are always server-generated, never client-influenced. Download is authenticated only — no public URL exists anywhere for evidence. Tenant-scoped and IDOR-protected, live-verified (cross-org download denied, arbitrary evidence IDs denied). Actors/stages as implemented: employee (own review, `self_assessment` only), manager (reviewer of record, `manager_review` only), HR (`performance.manage`, `hr_review` only) — each may upload only during their own active stage; evidence remains viewable/downloadable after finalization and through acknowledgement, since it is part of the review's durable historical record. **No delete route exists for evidence — by design**, matching the durable-record principle. **No malware scanning exists** — this is not claimed anywhere in this report. A transactional failure during upload (DB insert failing after a file write, or vice versa) triggers compensating cleanup (the written file is deleted, or the DB row is never committed) — the combined create+attach action runs inside a single `db.transaction`.

### Audit

Meaningful Performance mutations are all audited: cycle create/open/close/archive; review assignment (`performance_review.assigned`, one event per generated review); goal proposal/accept/reject; self-assessment submission; manager-review submission; finalization (+ a distinct `score_overridden` event when an override is supplied); reopen (with full `beforeState`/`afterState`); and, as of W83A, **acknowledgement** (`performance_review.acknowledged`, safe metadata only — organization, review, employee, actor, transition, timestamp; the free-text `employeeFinalComment` is deliberately excluded, matching the platform's own established precedent of never putting free-text override/reopen reasons into audit metadata either). Reads generate zero audit noise — confirmed by direct test assertion on every read-only route (dashboard, reports, review detail GET, evidence list) throughout W73–W83A.

All surfaces: module-gated, standard loading/error/empty/`403`/`409` states, zero client-side scoring anywhere (only server-computed values are ever read for display), zero direct Supabase client usage anywhere in `artifacts/hrms/src`.

**Browser QA limitation, stated plainly and consistently across every one of W73–W83A:** interactive browser automation (`chromium-cli`/Playwright) was never available on this Windows host, at any point in Phase 3C. ### Multi-Organization Compatibility

Performance follows the platform's established one-codebase, one-module-framework, multiple-isolated-organizations model exactly — no WWM-specific or company-only Performance branch exists anywhere. Every organization type this platform supports (businesses, churches, NGOs, educational institutions, healthcare, hospitality, manufacturing, professional firms, government/public-sector, membership-based organizations) uses the identical Performance module; differences come entirely from module enablement, organization-owned rating scales/templates/cycles/competencies, `organization_settings`, seeded permissions, and tenant-owned review data — never from separate code paths.

Nothing in Phase 3C introduces provider-specific logic — Performance is compatible with shared hosting, dedicated/customer VPS, and evaluation/trial deployment modes identically. ### Features Delivered

**Capture:** an employee clocks themselves in/out through ESS (server-authoritative timestamp, server-derived identity — a client-supplied `employeeId` is always ignored); HR can enter/correct attendance directly for any organization employee via the same underlying mechanism, auto-approved immediately.

**Computed status:** every day's attendance status (`present`/`late`/`partial`/`absent`/`on_leave`/`holiday`/`non_working_day`/`null`) is computed live on every read from raw events, approved adjustments, approved Leave, and Public Holidays — never stored, never a second calculation engine, always timezone-correct via the organization's own configured IANA timezone.

**Correction workflow:** an employee can request a correction to their own attendance (always `pending`, never self-approving); HR/org-admin (`attendance.adjustment.approve`) decides it, atomically, with terminal-state protection against double-decision.

**Self-service surface:** an ESS "My Attendance" tab — clock controls, a 7-day recent summary, recent raw events, and a correction-request form — independently module-gated exactly like My Leave and Internal Vacancies.

**Internal management surfaces:** an Attendance Register (paginated, filterable, own/team/organization-wide scoped), an Attendance Dashboard (a same-day, zero-filled status tile breakdown), and four CSV-exportable Attendance Reports (`attendance_daily_register`, `attendance_monthly_summary`, `attendance_late_arrivals`, `attendance_absenteeism`) — all pure read-side aggregation over the identical W66 read-model, all sharing the identical own/team/organization-wide visibility tiers.

### Frozen-Plan Reconciliation

Interpretations and reconciliations made during implementation, each already individually documented in this file's own W64–W70 header paragraphs, consolidated here:

- **Repeated clock-ins are permitted, not rejected** — Open Decision 1's own recommended default; a second clock-in with no intervening clock-out returns `201`, not `400`. Accidental rapid double-taps are treated as a client UX concern, not a server-integrity concern.
- **First-in/last-out summary math** — no multi-segment (e.g. lunch-break) net-duration calculation; the schema supports it without change if ever needed later, but W64–W70 never required it.
- **An incomplete clock pair reads as `partial`** — §3.3 lists `partial` in the status enum with no definition; this is the interpretation used throughout, live-verified end to end in W71 (clock-in alone → `partial`, clock-out completes it → `present`/`late`).
- **`excuse_absence` maps to `on_leave`** — no literal 8th status exists among the 7 frozen values; the closest existing authorized-absence status was reused rather than inventing a new one.
- **A missing organization timezone is a hard `409`, never a silent UTC fallback** — Open Decision 2's own recommended default, to avoid systematically wrong "late" calculations for any non-UTC organization.
- **HR direct entry is a `attendance_adjustments` row (auto-approved), not a raw `attendance_events` row with `source: "hr_manual"`** — W65's own concrete "Backend/API impact" line assigns this the concrete route it actually got; `source: "hr_manual"` remains schema-valid but structurally unreached through any built route, same as `biometric`/`import`.
- **Correction-request approval is organization-wide only, no manager/delegated tier** — Open Decision 3's own recommended default for W67; a manager-tier extension was never built or approved.
- **No employee correction-request history/list UI or endpoint** — the frozen plan's own W67 "Backend/API impact" line is an exhaustive three-route list that never included a GET/list route; a submitted request is confirmed via its own create response, not a persisted-and-rendered history.
- **No Attendance-rate or lateness-rate metric anywhere (dashboard or reports)** — the frozen W70 scope line defines only a raw-count tile breakdown with no denominator or exclusion rule specified anywhere in the frozen document; inventing one would have violated the "do not invent executive KPIs" discipline this session was held to. If ever wanted, it needs its own frozen definition first.
- **No new charting library** — Recruitment's own dashboard precedent (plain Card/Badge/Table) was reused; nothing in W70 genuinely required a chart.
- **`/attendance/dashboard` + `/attendance-reports` as dedicated routes**, not folded into the existing `GET /dashboard/summary` widget — Open Decision 4's own recommended default, given Attendance's comparable operational scope to Recruitment's own W61 precedent.
- **The four W70 report keys** (`attendance_daily_register`, `attendance_monthly_summary`, `attendance_late_arrivals`, `attendance_absenteeism`) were selected from §7's own explicitly non-binding candidate list, at W70's own start, per that section's own "this plan's W70's own decision to make" framing.
- **W69's status filter applies after employee-level pagination** — status is a computed field, not a stored column; `total` reflects the pre-status-filter employee-scope count. Documented as a deliberate, transparent tradeoff for a first register cut, not silently glossed over, and never silently changed by W70's own reporting work (which computes its own, separately correct, full-range totals for each report instead).
- **No biometric device implementation** — `attendance_events.source` includes `biometric` as a schema-valid, reserved-only value (§3.6's own "boundary-only" framing, Open Decision 5's own recommended default); no device protocol exists to implement against yet.
- **No payroll integration, overtime pay, shift scheduling/rostering, GPS/geofencing, mobile app, offline sync, advanced timesheets, project time tracking, or performance-penalty logic** — all explicitly listed in §9's own "Explicit Exclusions (this phase does not build)," never attempted.

- **No persisted reporting/analytics table** — same discipline, extended to W70; `getAttendanceRegisterForEmployees` is the single shared computation both the Register and every Dashboard/Report figure route through.
- **Cross-midnight/overnight shifts remain explicitly out of scope for W64–W70**, per §2's own framing — a clock-out is always paired with clock-in events sharing its own civil date; night-shift support is a later, separately-scoped extension if ever approved.

None of the above are presented as defects — every one is either the frozen plan's own explicit exclusion, an Open Decision's own recommended default actually taken, or a reconciliation between the frozen document's general prose and its own more specific, controlling statement (per the "the frozen plan's most specific statement controls" discipline established from W65 onward).

### APIs

**9 endpoints across 5 route files**, all registered exactly once, no duplicates (verified by direct route-file inspection in W71):

| Route | Method | Permission |
|---|---|---|
| `.../attendance-events` | POST | `attendance.clock.own` |
| `.../attendance-events` | GET | `attendance.read.own` |
| `.../attendance-adjustments` | POST | `attendance.read.own` (branches internally on `attendance.manage`) |
| `.../attendance-adjustments/:id/approve` | POST | `attendance.adjustment.approve` |
| `.../attendance-adjustments/:id/reject` | POST | `attendance.adjustment.approve` |
| `.../employees/:employeeId/attendance/summary` | GET | `attendance.read.own` |
| `.../attendance` (Register) | GET | `attendance.read.own` |
| `.../attendance/dashboard` | GET | `attendance.read.own` |
| `.../attendance/reports/:reportKey` | GET | `attendance.read.own` |

Every one of the 9 handlers composes the identical `requireAuth` → `requireMembership("organizationId")` → `requireModuleEnabled("attendance")` → `requirePermission(...)` chain — confirmed by direct grep across all 5 route files in W71, not assumed. **OpenAPI:** 9 matching paths under the `attendance-events`/`attendance-adjustments`/`attendance-daily-summary`/`attendance-register`/`attendance-reporting` tags. **Generated client:** 9 matching hooks (`useRecordAttendanceEvent`, `useListAttendanceEvents`, `useRecordAttendanceAdjustment`, `useApproveAttendanceAdjustment`, `useRejectAttendanceAdjustment`, `useGetAttendanceDailySummary`, `useListAttendanceRegister`, `useGetAttendanceDashboard`, `useRunAttendanceReport`) — confirmed present, zero missing, zero extra. `orval codegen` produces byte-identical output across two consecutive runs, and is identical to the already-checked-in generated files (zero drift from `openapi.yaml`, re-confirmed in W71).

### Permissions

Four permissions, seeded exactly per the frozen plan's own §4 matrix, unchanged since W64 — **no permission was ever added by W65–W70**:

- **`attendance.clock.own`** — self clock-in/out. Seeded to `org_admin`/`hr_manager`/`employee` (every role).
- **`attendance.read.own`** — the coarse route-level gate for every read surface (own/team-scoped register, dashboard, reports, summary) and the shared adjustments-creation route. Seeded to `org_admin`/`hr_manager`/`employee` (every role).
- **`attendance.manage`** — organization-wide reach signal: HR direct-entry, organization-wide register/dashboard/reports. Seeded to `org_admin`/`hr_manager` only.
- **`attendance.adjustment.approve`** — decide a pending correction request. Seeded to `org_admin`/`hr_manager` only.

**No `attendance.read.team` or any manager-tier permission exists** — the "team" visibility tier (direct reports) is resolved entirely in the service layer via `employees.reportingManagerId`, the same mechanism `leaveCalendar.ts` already established for Leave — never a permission grant, exactly per §4's own explicit design.

### Module Gating

`attendance` — seeded in the Foundation's Module Registry as `status: "hidden"` until W64 flipped it to `active`; no organization is enabled by module availability alone (WWM and Acme both confirmed disabled at every checkpoint throughout W64–W71 except during each workstream's own bracketed, restored-afterward live QA window). Every one of the 9 routes composes `requireModuleEnabled("attendance")`, always paired with a specific `requirePermission` call — module gating is never a substitute for authorization, confirmed by direct inspection. Every frontend route wraps in `<ModuleGate moduleKey="attendance">`; ESS's "My Attendance" tab checks `attendance` accessibility independently within the ESS page (gated only by `employee_self_service` itself), degrading to a controlled message rather than a broken page — the identical pattern My Leave (W39) and Internal Vacancies (W60) already established.

### Authorization Matrix

- **Employee:** own clock-in/out, own summary read, own correction request. Cannot approve anything; cannot reach the organization-wide Register/Dashboard/Reports (own/team scope only, resolved server-side); cannot target another employee (server-derived identity on every write).
- **Manager** (a plain `employee`-role holder who happens to be someone's `reportingManagerId`): own + direct-report visibility on the Register/Dashboard/Reports — no organization-wide fallback, live-verified repeatedly including a zero-direct-reports case (valid empty scope, never a fallback to organization-wide); filters can only narrow this scope, never broaden it (live-verified with an out-of-scope `employeeId` filter); cannot use any `attendance.manage`-gated functionality (HR direct entry, organization-wide register) unless independently granted that permission; cannot approve/reject unless independently granted `attendance.adjustment.approve`.
- **HR Manager / Org Admin:** organization-wide read/manage per the seeded matrix above — HR direct entry, adjustment approval, organization-wide Register/Dashboard/Reports, all live-verified.
- **Super Admin:** inherits `org_admin`-equivalent Attendance reach via the same seeded permission matrix; the platform's own established hostname-binding behavior (from the tenant-domain work preceding Phase 3B) is untouched by anything in W64–W70 — no Attendance route implements custom hostname logic of its own, so super_admin is neither granted nor denied anything beyond what the shared `requireMembership` tenant-consistency guard already enforces platform-wide.
- **Module disabled:** denied independently of role or permission — confirmed live (a valid HR/org-admin token against a module-disabled organization still gets `403`).
- **No membership:** denied — confirmed live repeatedly (WWM↔Acme cross-org tokens, unauthenticated requests).

### Attendance Rules (final, as implemented)

- **Clock timestamps are always server-authoritative** — `occurredAt` is the server's own clock, never a client-supplied value, on every self-service clock event.
- **Civil dates are always derived server-side** from the organization's configured `general.timezone` via Node's `Intl.DateTimeFormat` (real IANA conversion, inherently DST-correct) — never client/browser-local, confirmed specifically with a non-UTC timezone (Asia/Tokyo) during W66's own live QA.
- **A missing organization timezone is a hard `409`** on every data-bearing Attendance route (summary, register, dashboard, reports) — never a silent UTC fallback.
- **Repeated clock-ins are permitted** — no sequencing rejection.
- **First-clock-in/last-clock-out** is the summary's own worked-time math; no multi-segment net-duration calculation exists.
- **An incomplete clock pair → `partial`**; a complete pair → `present` (on time) or `late` (past `workStartTime` + `gracePeriodMinutes`); no events at all on a configured work day → `absent`, unless the employee's *current* `employmentStatus` is `on_leave`/`suspended`, in which case it's suppressed to `null` instead.
- **Approved Leave → `on_leave`**, beating an otherwise-`absent` day; a merely-*pending* Leave request has zero effect.
- **A Public Holiday → `holiday`**; a non-configured work day (per §38's own `workDays` setting) → `non_working_day`; both beat event-derived statuses.
- **An approved whole-day adjustment** (`mark_present`/`mark_absent`/`excuse_absence`) overrides the event-derived status for that date; a *pending* or *rejected* adjustment has zero effect, live-re-verified in W71.
- **An approved `manual_clock_in`/`manual_clock_out` adjustment** overrides only the matching raw event's contribution to the pair, not the whole day.
- **Pre-`hireDate` or on/after-`separationDate` → `null`** (no summary generated at all), per §3.7's own literal wording.
- **No client ever computes a status, a rate, or a precedence decision** — every one of the 4 frontend surfaces (ESS, Register, Dashboard, Reports) renders server-computed DTOs only; confirmed by a repo-wide grep for any client-side date/status-computation logic in W71 (only the W38 Attendance Settings config-editing page references these field names at all, and only to edit the configuration values themselves, never to compute a status).

### Reporting

Four report keys (`attendance_daily_register`, `attendance_monthly_summary`, `attendance_late_arrivals`, `attendance_absenteeism`), registered in the shared Reporting Foundation registry (W17/ADR-016, `category: "attendance"`) for catalog discoverability via the existing `GET /reports`, but executed through a **dedicated, visibility-scoped route** (`GET .../attendance/reports/:reportKey`), never the generic `GET .../reports/:reportKey/run` — that route's own RUNNERS map has no entries for these keys and safely 404s, exactly mirroring how Recruitment's own 9 report keys (W61) are isolated from the generic runner. Own/team/organization-wide visibility is identical to the Register/Dashboard. Date ranges are always organization-local (never browser-local), reusing the Register's own 100-day-max/no-inverted-range validation, defaulting to organization-local "today" on both ends when omitted. CSV export reuses the exact `?format=csv` convention Recruitment's own reports already established — export scope is always identical to the JSON response's own already-authorized scope, with no separate export permission or code path; a cross-tenant export is structurally impossible (organizationId is resolved from the URL/membership, never the query string). No separate analytics store or second report registry was created anywhere.

### Frontend Surfaces

- **My Attendance (ESS tab)** — clock controls, 7-day recent summary, recent raw events, a correction-request form. Independent module-degradation (My Leave/Internal Vacancies precedent).
- **Attendance Register** (`/attendance-register`) — paginated, filterable internal list, HR-capable-role-gated nav entry, own/team tier still reachable directly by URL.
- **Attendance Dashboard** (`/attendance-dashboard`) — status tiles for a single organization-local date; the date input always displays the backend's own resolved date, never a browser-computed guess.
- **Attendance Reports** (`/attendance-reports`) — report selector, date-range inputs, CSV download; mirrors `recruitment-reports.tsx`'s own established structure exactly.

All four: `<ModuleGate moduleKey="attendance">` (or independent in-page checks for the ESS tab), standard loading/error/empty/`403`/`409` states, existing responsive table/card patterns (no HRMS shell redesign), no new charting dependency, zero direct Supabase client access anywhere in `artifacts/hrms/src` (repo-wide grep, zero matches).

**Browser QA limitation, stated plainly and consistently across every one of W64–W71:** interactive browser automation (`chromium-cli`/Playwright) was never available on this Windows host, at any point in Phase 3B. Frontend correctness was verified via the passing React Testing Library component suite (real rendering, real user-event interaction, mocked network) plus live HTTP/API QA against the real development database confirming the exact endpoints/payloads each surface actually depends on, plus all three production builds succeeding. This is stated here explicitly, not glossed over — no interactive browser walkthrough is claimed for any Phase 3B workstream.

## Phase 3A Progress

Authoritative, frozen plan: see `docs/PHASE_3A_RECRUITMENT_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` (21 dependency-ordered workstreams, W43–W63).

- **W61 — Recruitment Dashboard & Reporting — Complete.** Read-only metrics computed live over W43–W60's existing tables — no cache table, no stored aggregate, no recruitment-state mutation anywhere in this workstream (verified directly: `lib/recruitmentReporting.ts` contains zero `insert`/`update`/`delete` calls). **Dashboard** (`GET .../organizations/:organizationId/recruitment/dashboard`): six real-time tiles — `openRequisitionsCount` (status = `approved`, the only status this codebase's pipeline ever actually reaches for an actively-recruiting requisition — `partially_filled`/`filled` are schema-valid but no route anywhere sets them, a pre-existing gap this workstream doesn't fix, so "filled" metrics are honestly empty rather than fabricated), `openVacanciesCount` (status = `published`), `totalApplicantsCount`, `candidatesByStage` (a stage-category breakdown, a never-triaged application reading as "Applied (unstaged)" per `applicationPipeline.ts`'s own display-only convention), `recruiterWorkload`/`hiringManagerWorkload` (open-requisition counts grouped by `recruiterEmployeeId`/`hiringManagerEmployeeId`, resolved to staff names). **Reports** (`GET .../organizations/:organizationId/recruitment/reports/:reportKey`): nine keys registered as ordinary rows in W17's existing `reports` registry (category `"recruitment"`, so they appear in the existing `GET /reports` catalog) but executed only through this workstream's own dedicated, visibility-scoped route — the generic `GET .../reports/:reportKey/run` (lib/reporting.ts) has no runner entries for these keys and safely 404s "Unknown report" if ever hit directly, since it has no concept of the assigned-vs-organization-wide tier these reports require. The nine: `recruitment_applicants_by_vacancy`, `recruitment_applicants_by_source`, `recruitment_time_to_fill` (requisition-approval `decidedAt` → `updatedAt` on a `filled`-status requisition — honestly empty today, same pipeline gap as above), `recruitment_time_to_hire` (`applications.submittedAt` → the latest `application_stage_history` row moving into a hired-category stage, averaged per vacancy), `recruitment_age_in_stage` (now − the application's most recent stage-history entry, or `submittedAt` if never moved, averaged per non-terminal stage), `recruitment_conversion_funnel` (applied→screening→interview→assessment→offer→hired sequential reach counts plus separate rejected/withdrawn outcome counts), `recruitment_interview_to_offer_ratio`, `recruitment_offer_acceptance_rate` (`offer_versions.status` `accepted`/`declined` — schema-valid values no route in this codebase ever sets per W57's own documented scope boundary, so this is honestly null, not zero, until that flow exists), `recruitment_rejection_reasons`. **Null-vs-zero discipline enforced throughout:** every ratio/average returns `null` (never a fabricated `0`) when its denominator is zero or no rows exist to average — verified directly for the interview-to-offer ratio in both the zero-data and real-data cases. **Explicitly excluded:** §18's "vacancy performance (views/applicants)" — the views half requires a new view-count column on `vacancies` (a schema change), which contradicts W61's own frozen `Database impact: none` line; the applicants half is already covered by `recruitment_applicants_by_vacancy`. This is the same "frozen schema wins over speculative prose" discipline W44/W47/W58 already established, not an oversight. **Permissions — the single frozen key, nothing else:** `recruitment.reports.read`, seeded to org_admin, hr_manager, **and** employee — the same broad-rollout-plus-service-layer-narrowing shape every other Recruitment *read* permission this phase already uses (`requisition.read`, `vacancy.read`, `application.read`, `candidate.read`, `interview.read`, `offer.read`), since any employee could be the assigned recruiter/hiring manager on some requisition. **Visibility, resolved in `lib/recruitmentReporting.ts`, never by the permission grant alone:** organization-wide reach is signaled by holding `requisition.update` — reused, not a new permission, the exact same org_admin/hr_manager-only signal `jobRequisitions.ts` already established for this purpose; everyone else is scoped to `job_requisitions` rows where `recruiterEmployeeId` or `hiringManagerEmployeeId` matches their own linked employee id, then vacancies/applications/history/interviews/offers are all resolved through that requisition scope — verified directly that an assigned recruiter with no `requisition.update` sees only their own workload and never another recruiter's, and that a caller with `recruitment.reports.read` but no linked employee and no organization-wide reach gets a real empty scope, never an error or another caller's data. **Privacy:** no candidate name, email, phone, national identifier, referee contact, background-check result, recruiter note, interview/scorecard comment, or document storage key is read or returned anywhere in this workstream — every metric aggregates to vacancy/requisition/stage/reason-code granularity; the only names ever returned are recruiting *staff* (via `employeesTable`, for workload attribution), never a candidate. **A real, non-obvious frontend bug found and fixed during this session's own verification, before commit:** the Recruitment Reports page's original "auto-select the first report" logic compared the freshly-`.filter()`-ed `reports` array against a `useState`-held "previous" copy by reference to detect when to pick a default — but since `.filter()` returns a new array every render, and the initial "previous" value was captured from that very same first render, the two were reference-different-yet-conceptually-identical, and the comparison could never detect the very first arrival of real data when it happened to be available synchronously (exactly what the test harness surfaced, and a case a real cached/pre-populated React Query response could hit too). Fixed by deriving the effective `reportKey` during render (`reports.some(...) ? selectedReportKey : reports[0]?.key ?? ''`) instead of syncing state from an effect — also resolved a `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` lint error an earlier effect-based fix attempt introduced. **API/OpenAPI:** new `recruitment-reporting` tag; `RecruitmentDashboard`/`RecruitmentStageBreakdownItem`/`RecruitmentWorkloadItem` schemas; the report-run response reuses W17's existing `ReportRunResult`/`ReportColumn` schemas unchanged (same `{key, label, description, generatedAt, columns, rows}` shape, `?format=csv` convention, and `text/csv` content-type) — codegen verified zero-diff across two consecutive runs. **Frontend:** `/recruitment` (dashboard: tiles, stage-breakdown badges, two workload tables) and `/recruitment-reports` (catalog dropdown reused from the existing `reports` registry filtered to `category === "recruitment"`, result table, CSV download) — both `<ModuleGate moduleKey="recruitment">`-wrapped per §8; nav entries gated `isHrCapable`-only, the same precedent every other Recruitment nav entry (`/offers`, `/interviews`, ...) already established — an assigned recruiter/hiring manager without an HR-capable role can still reach both pages directly by URL. Both pages render a distinct "Access denied" state for a `403` (duck-typed via the thrown `ApiError`'s `status` field, since `ApiError` itself isn't part of the generated client's public exports) separately from a generic error state, plus loading and empty states — real zeros/an explicit "no data yet" message, never a crash, for an organization with the module enabled but nothing to report yet. **Audit/notifications:** none — a pure read path, nothing here changes state or is itself an event worth recording, and neither is named anywhere in W61's frozen scope. **Database impact: none** — confirmed via `drizzle-kit generate` reporting "No schema changes, nothing to migrate"; no migration file exists for this workstream. Backend: 17 new tests (`recruitmentReporting.test.ts`) covering unauthenticated/permission-denied/module-disabled statuses, organization-wide vs. assigned-vs.-empty visibility on the dashboard, stage-breakdown bucketing of a never-triaged application, cross-registry isolation (a non-recruitment report key 404s through this route), null-vs-real-percentage for the interview-to-offer ratio, the honestly-empty time-to-fill report, CSV content-type, and assigned-recruiter cross-recruiter isolation on a report (not just the dashboard). Frontend: 13 new tests (7 `recruitment-dashboard.test.tsx`, 6 `recruitment-reports.test.tsx`) covering loading/denied/error/empty/populated dashboard states and catalog-filtering/denied/error/empty/populated-with-a-null-cell/CSV-button-enabled report states. Full suite: 706 backend + 234 frontend tests pass, typecheck and lint clean, OpenAPI codegen zero-diff, zero migration drift, production builds (`api-server`, `hrms`, `mockup-sandbox`) all succeed. No live browser walkthrough was performed — this environment has no provisioned dev database, the same limitation every prior Recruitment workstream in this session has had; verification relied on the automated test suites, typecheck, lint, `drizzle-kit generate`, codegen, and production builds only. Does not implement vacancy view tracking, a diversity/EEO breakdown, PDF export, scheduled/emailed reports, or any change to existing recruitment records — all remain out of this workstream's frozen scope or explicitly excluded by §21/§25.

- **W60 — Employee Self-Service Internal Applications — Complete.** Lets an authenticated employee view internal vacancies and apply to them from inside ESS — `GET /me/internal-vacancies`, `POST /me/internal-vacancies/:publicId/apply`, `GET /me/applications` (§10's own exact three lines; no vacancy-detail or withdraw route exists in the frozen API — see scope notes below). **Database impact is genuinely zero**, exactly as the frozen plan's own scope line states — reuses `candidates`/`applications`/`vacancies`/`employee_user_links` unchanged, no migration generated. **Identity is always derived server-side**, the same `resolveOwnEmployeeId` (W14/W33) chain every other ESS/Recruitment-assigned-tier resolver in this codebase already reuses — no route accepts a client-supplied employeeId/candidateId. **A reused, not duplicated, employee-creation-service-style extraction:** `findOrCreateCandidate` (private in `candidateApplications.ts`, W49) was exported unchanged for reuse here — the exact same "extract rather than reimplement" discipline W59 already established for `createEmployee`. **Candidate resolution/linkage — the one genuinely new piece of logic this workstream adds:** an applying employee's `candidates` row is resolved in priority order — (1) an existing row already linked via `candidates.linkedInternalEmployeeId` (e.g. this employee was originally hired through external recruitment and their original candidate record survives, per ADR "never hard-delete"); else (2) `findOrCreateCandidate` resolved by the employee's own email (`workEmail ?? personalEmail`; a missing email on both is a clear 400, not an invented placeholder), then permanently linked by setting `linkedInternalEmployeeId` — but only if it isn't already set on some *other* employee (a defensive no-op that never overwrites another employee's provenance or any other field on an existing candidate row). **W59's conversion is never invoked** — an internal application does not change the employee record or create a second one; verified by a dedicated test. **Vacancy eligibility** mirrors `publicCareers.ts`'s own `isVacancyPubliclyEligible` predicate exactly, with the visibility condition inverted (`external`-only excluded instead of `internal`-only) — published status, openDate/closeDate window, per W47's frozen model; only an `active` employee may browse or apply (the literal, narrowest reading of "the employee is active" — no frozen rule distinguishes probation/on_leave/suspended, so that reading was chosen and documented as a judgment call). **Two read endpoints return a controlled `{linked, active, items}` 200-OK state** for an unlinked or non-active caller — mirroring `GET /me/employee`'s own established `linked: false` precedent exactly, per this workstream's own explicit instruction — never a 403/error for a passive view; the one write action (`apply`) still 403s for the same conditions, since a blocked write is conventionally an error, not a 200-with-flag response. **Submission** reuses the `applications` table's own `(candidateId, vacancyId)` unique constraint for duplicate/idempotent handling (mirrors `submitPublicApplication`'s "return the existing row, no second write" rule exactly) — enters W51's existing pipeline unchanged, `source` marked `"internal_ess"` (the table's own free-text column, same convention as `candidate_documents.categoryCode`) so recruiters can distinguish it, but no second pipeline exists. Screening answers reuse W52's existing optional `application_answers` capture unchanged (a vacancy's questions apply uniformly regardless of applicant source); no resume upload is required and no `candidate_consents` row is written — neither is named anywhere in W60's frozen scope, and an employee already has an existing employment relationship distinct from an anonymous external applicant's need for explicit consent capture. **Permissions — none added or changed:** every route is gated purely by `employee_self_service` AND `recruitment` module enablement (checked independently, §8 — a disabled `recruitment` module degrades only the two new ESS tab sections, never blocks the rest of the page) plus self-scoped identity resolution; no `requirePermission` call exists on any of the three routes, mirroring `GET /me/employee`'s own permission-key-independent design exactly. Ordinary employees receive no new or broadened recruitment permission — `seed-roles-permissions.ts` was not touched by this workstream at all. **Scope boundaries — deliberately not built, since §10's frozen API line names only three routes:** no `GET /me/internal-vacancies/:publicId` detail route (the list response already carries every field a detail view needs — job description, responsibilities, requirements, screening questions — so "detail" is a client-side selection from the already-fetched list, never a second fetch) and no withdraw route for internal applications (no such route is named anywhere in §10, and the existing internal `POST .../applications/:id/withdraw` from W51 is gated behind assigned-recruiter/hiring-manager/org-wide permissions an ordinary applicant could never hold). **API:** new `InternalVacancySummary`/`InternalVacancyQuestion`/`InternalVacanciesResponse`/`SubmitInternalApplicationInput`/`MyInternalApplicationSubmitResult`/`MyInternalApplicationSummary`/`MyInternalApplicationsResponse` OpenAPI schemas under the existing `self-service` tag (reused, not a new tag), codegen verified zero-diff across two consecutive runs. **Frontend:** two new tabs on the existing `/self-service` page — "Internal Vacancies" (card grid, a detail-and-apply dialog with inline screening-question inputs where a vacancy has any) and "My Applications" (status-badged list) — reusing the exact same independent-module-degradation pattern (`isModuleAccessible(modules, 'recruitment')`) W39's own "My Leave" tab already established for the `leave` module; the existing My Profile/My Leave/My Documents tabs are untouched and remain fully functional. **Audit:** `internal_application.submitted` only (on a genuinely new submission, never on an idempotent repeat) — no per-vacancy-view audit event exists, since none is required by the frozen plan. **No notifications** — none are explicitly assigned to W60. **Database impact:** none — no migration file, no schema change, confirmed via a clean `pnpm run typecheck`/build with zero drizzle-kit drift. Backend: 25 new tests (`meInternalApplications.test.ts`) covering unauthenticated/module-disabled 401/403s, the unlinked and non-active controlled states on both read endpoints, internal-vacancy eligibility (published/visibility/open-close-window, including an explicit external-only-exclusion test and a "both" visibility inclusion test), the full candidate-resolution-and-link flow (including reusing a pre-existing `linkedInternalEmployeeId`-linked candidate), idempotent repeat submission, optional screening-answer capture with an out-of-vacancy answer silently ignored, the no-employee-record-mutation/no-conversion-invoked proof, cross-employee application-list isolation, and restricted-DTO-field assertions. Frontend: 8 new tests added to `employee-self-service.test.tsx` covering the two new tabs' rendering, the disabled-recruitment-module degrade, the not-eligible controlled state, empty states, the list-to-apply-dialog flow with a no-recruiter-controls assertion, application submission, and My Applications rendering — all pre-existing ESS tests continue to pass unchanged. Full suite: 689 backend + 221 frontend tests pass. No live browser walkthrough was performed — this environment has no provisioned dev database, the same limitation every prior Recruitment workstream in this session has had; verification relied on the automated test suites, typecheck, lint, and production build only. Does not implement an internal-vacancy detail route, internal-application withdrawal, resume/document upload for internal applications, consent capture, notifications, or any change to the existing anonymous public careers flow (verified untouched) — all remain out of this workstream's frozen scope or later workstreams' concern entirely.

- **W59 — Employee Conversion — Complete.** The controlled hand-off from Recruitment to HR: a new `candidate_employee_links` provenance table plus a `convert-to-employee` transaction. **Core principle enforced structurally, not just by convention:** Recruitment selects a candidate; this workstream creates an employee — those stayed two different responsibilities in two different files, and there remains exactly ONE authoritative employee-creation pathway in the system. **A real gap found before this workstream could even begin:** the frozen plan's own §13 text assumes a reusable `createEmployee` **service** exists ("reuses the existing `createEmployee` service... same service `POST /organizations/:id/employees` already uses"), but the actual codebase had that exact logic (reference validation, employee-number generation, the insert itself) written *inline* inside `routes/employees.ts`'s POST handler, not extracted anywhere reusable. Building convert-to-employee without first fixing this would have meant either duplicating that logic (explicitly forbidden by this workstream's own instructions) or reaching into a route handler from a lib file (an architectural inversion no other workstream this phase does). Resolved by extracting the exact existing logic, unchanged, into a new `createEmployee(client, params)` export in `lib/employees.ts` — accepting a `QueryClient` (the same `db`-or-`tx` pattern `leaveBalances.ts`/`offers.ts` already established) so it can run inside convert-to-employee's own transaction — then updating `routes/employees.ts`'s POST handler to call it instead of inlining the insert. Confirmed behavior-preserving: all 30 pre-existing `employees.test.ts` tests pass unchanged against the refactored route. **Eligibility is exactly §13's own two-check formula, nothing more:** the application must be in a `hired`-category stage (§4.3, resolved via `recruitment_stages.category`, never an org-configurable stage *name*) AND every non-waived `pre_employment_requirements` row must be `satisfied` (reuses the identical `readyForConversion` computation W58 already established). **No offer-status check gates eligibility at all** — despite the task's own "typical examples" suggesting "offer accepted," §13's literal text names only the two checks above; an offer is used purely as an *optional data source* for the employee mapping, never a gate, since W57 built no candidate-facing acceptance flow. **Data mapping — only what's actually available, nothing invented:** name/contact/nationality from `candidates`, `residentialAddress` from `candidates.address` (§9 itself says the two mirror the same jsonb shape), department/branch/position from the linked requisition (the same application→vacancy→requisition three-hop chain every other Recruitment resource this phase reuses), employmentType/hireDate/workLocation from the current offer version if one exists. `candidates.nationalIdentifierType`/`Value` is deliberately NOT mapped to `employees.nationalId`/`passportNumber` — the candidate-side field is a generic type+value pair with no frozen rule for which employee column a given type resolves to; inventing that rule was out of scope. `emergencyContacts` is deliberately not mapped — no such field exists on `candidates` in this frozen model at all. **Duplicate/concurrent-conversion protection** is the same "no pre-check, just catch the DB race" discipline this phase already established (`offers.ts`'s `createOffer`, W58's `createPreEmploymentRequirement`) — `candidate_employee_links` carries BOTH a unique `(applicationId)` constraint (idempotent retry of the same application) AND a unique `(employeeId)` constraint ("one recruitment provenance per employee," §9), both translated to a single typed `AlreadyConvertedError` (mirrors `DuplicateLedgerEntryError`'s precedent, per §13's own text). **A real design gap found and closed during this workstream's own security review, before commit:** an internal candidate's `candidates.linkedInternalEmployeeId` needs to be *set* somewhere the first time a candidate converts, or the "does not create a second employee record" guarantee only holds for candidates who were already marked internal by some external means — a *second* application from a candidate who converted *through this very flow* would otherwise hit the "not yet linked" branch again and create a genuine duplicate employee. Fixed by setting `candidates.linkedInternalEmployeeId` to the newly created employee's id inside the same transaction, immediately after `createEmployee` succeeds. This surfaced a second, subtler consequence, caught by the workstream's own test suite rather than assumed: because `candidate_employee_links.employeeId` is *also* unique, a second application from an already-self-converted candidate correctly 409s as already-converted (inserting a second link row for the same employee is exactly what that constraint forbids) — the "reuse an existing employee" success path is therefore only ever reachable for a candidate whose `linkedInternalEmployeeId` was set by some means *other* than a prior conversion through this same function (e.g. a genuinely pre-existing employee who separately has a candidate record, with no `candidate_employee_links` row of their own yet) — a real, non-obvious interaction between two unique constraints, verified by a dedicated test for each branch. **Recruitment history is never touched:** no delete anywhere in this workstream — candidate, application, interview, scorecard, reference/background-check, offer, and pre-employment-requirement rows are all left exactly as they were; conversion only *adds* the provenance link, verified by a dedicated test. **Permissions:** §7's own row — `candidate.convert_to_employee`, no own/assigned tier, organization-wide only ("mirrors `employee.write`'s existing gate") — seeded to the exact same roles as `employee.write` (org_admin, hr_manager only, never `employee`). The route requires **both** `candidate.convert_to_employee` AND `employee.write` — neither alone is sufficient, verified by two separate 403 tests, satisfying this workstream's own explicit "neither permission alone should bypass the other" requirement. **API:** `POST .../applications/:id/convert-to-employee` (§10's own single line — no separate "conversion status"/"conversion detail" GET route exists in the frozen plan, so the frontend derives eligibility entirely from data it already fetches: `application.currentStageCategory` and the pre-employment-requirements summary's `readyForConversion`, both already wired into `/applications/:id` by W51/W58) — new OpenAPI schemas (`CandidateEmployeeLink`, `ConversionResult`) under a new `employee-conversion` tag, codegen verified zero-diff across two consecutive runs. **Frontend:** a "Convert to Employee" action on `/applications/:id` (§11's own frontend-impact line), shown only in a hired-category stage, disabled until every pre-employment requirement resolves, and replaced with a "View Employee" link to `/employees/:id` after a successful conversion. **Audit:** `employee_conversion.started`/`.completed`/`.failed` (targetType `application`) plus a distinct `employee_conversion.employee_linked` (targetType `employee`) — two perspectives on the same event (Recruitment's view vs. HR's view), not a duplicate. **Database impact:** migration `0034_bitter_microbe.sql` (one new table, purely additive) generated with a hand-authored `.down.sql`, not applied — confirmed zero further drift after generation. Backend: 15 new tests (`employeeConversion.test.ts`, covering both dual-permission 403s, tenant isolation, both eligibility checks' 400s, a from-scratch conversion with full field mapping including requisition placement and offer data, the `linkedInternalEmployeeId`-set-on-first-conversion behavior and its "second application now 409s" consequence, the pre-existing-internal-employee reuse path, idempotent-retry 409, and the no-history-lost proof) plus 30 pre-existing `employees.test.ts` tests confirmed unchanged after the `createEmployee` extraction. Frontend: 4 new tests added to `application-detail.test.tsx` covering the action's hidden/disabled/enabled states and the post-conversion "View Employee" link. Full suite: 664 backend + 213 frontend tests pass. No live browser walkthrough was performed — this environment has no provisioned dev database, the same limitation every prior Recruitment workstream in this session has had; verification relied on the automated test suites, typecheck, lint, and production build only. Does not implement onboarding, payroll/leave/attendance setup, asset assignment, orientation, training, user-account/email provisioning, offer generation/approval, or candidate accounts — all remain later workstreams' scope or explicitly out of the frozen plan entirely. This is the last workstream before Phase 3A's own numbering moves to Employee Self-Service integration (W60) and reporting (W61+) — Recruitment's core hire-to-employee pipeline (W43 through W59) is now feature-complete end to end.

- **W58 — Pre-Employment Requirements — Complete.** A checklist tracked against an application before employee conversion — `pre_employment_requirements`, one row per `(applicationId, requirementCode)`. **Completion of a requirement, or of every requirement, never creates an employee, activates payroll/leave/attendance/HR records, or creates an organization membership** — this workstream only tracks status; §13's own `convert-to-employee` (W59, not yet built) is the only thing that will ever read these rows to decide readiness, by re-querying them itself, not by calling anything this workstream exports. **The frozen §9 row is deliberately minimal, and this workstream builds nothing beyond it — the same "frozen schema wins over speculative prose" discipline W44/W47/W56/W57 already established:** columns are exactly `applicationId`/`requirementCode`/`status`/`satisfiedAt`/`notes`, nothing more. **Status model:** only three values — `pending`/`satisfied`/`waived` — not the richer submitted/verified/rejected/expired lifecycle a generic pre-employment-checklist feature might suggest; §9's own "status derivation" column reads "n/a" for this resource (unlike e.g. `reference_checks`, which cites §4.7's lifecycle diagram), meaning there is no frozen one-way transition model at all. Status is therefore freely settable between all three values — reverting a mistaken "satisfied" back to "pending" is allowed — a deliberate difference from reference/background checks' terminal-once-decided immutability. `satisfiedAt` reflects only the most recent transition into "satisfied" (set on entry, cleared on exit), never stale evidence of a since-reverted decision. **No document/storage handling at all:** the frozen §9 row has no storageKey column (unlike e.g. `background_checks.documentStorageKey`), and no internal candidate-document-upload route exists yet in this codebase (§10's `GET/POST/DELETE .../candidates/:id/documents` line belongs to a different workstream's own `Scope:`, not this one's, which names only `pre_employment_requirements`) — so this workstream builds no upload/storage mechanism whatsoever, a deliberate scope boundary. Any evidence a candidate already uploaded at application time (W49's `candidate_documents`) remains visible via the application detail's existing `documents` list (W51) without this resource owning or referencing any storage key. **Permissions — none new:** §7's matrix has no row for this resource at all (unlike `background_checks`, which gets its own dedicated org-wide-only pair) — reuses the existing `application.read`/`.manage` pair, the same precedent W56's `reference_checks` already established for an identical "org-scoped (via application)" RLS descriptor and comparably low sensitivity (this row's own sensitive-data column reads "none directly"). No `seed-roles-permissions.ts` change was needed — the first Recruitment workstream this phase that required zero permission-seeding changes. **Computed summary:** the list endpoint returns a `summary` object (`totalCount`/`pendingCount`/`satisfiedCount`/`waivedCount`/`readyForConversion`) computed on every read, never stored (the same discipline as W52's `scoreRollup`/W55's `panelSummary`) — `readyForConversion` mirrors §13's own convert-to-employee readiness rule exactly ("every non-waived row is satisfied"), vacuously true when no requirements are tracked at all; it is purely informational and does not itself gate or trigger anything. **API:** `GET`/`POST .../applications/:id/pre-employment-requirements`, `PATCH .../pre-employment-requirements/:id` — new OpenAPI schemas (`PreEmploymentRequirement`, `PreEmploymentRequirementSummary`, `PreEmploymentRequirementListResponse`, `CreatePreEmploymentRequirementInput`, `UpdatePreEmploymentRequirementStatusInput`) under a new `pre-employment-requirements` tag, codegen verified zero-diff across two consecutive runs. **Frontend:** a new "Pre-Employment Requirements" checklist section on `/applications/:id` (mirroring the Reference/Background Checks sections' subcomponent style) — add-requirement dialog (free-text `requirementCode`, matching `candidate_documents.categoryCode`'s own "Master Data, not FK-validated" convention; no hard-coded Ghana-specific or any other fixed list), a resolved-count summary line, and a per-row "Update Status" action always shown (never hidden once "terminal," since none exists here). **Audit:** `pre_employment_requirement.created`/`.status_changed` — not in §20's self-documenting exemption list (that list names only `application_stage_history`/`requisition_approvals`/`offer_approvals`/finalized `interview_scorecards`), so every creation and status change gets its own `recordAuditEvent` call, per §9's own "on status change" audit-trigger note. **Database impact:** migration `0033_fat_dorian_gray.sql` (one new table + one new enum, purely additive) generated with a hand-authored `.down.sql`, not applied — confirmed zero further drift after generation. Backend: 15 new tests (`preEmploymentRequirements.test.ts`) covering permission gating, tenant isolation, assigned/org-wide application visibility, duplicate-requirementCode 400 (a real DB unique-constraint race, mirroring `offers.ts`'s own catch-the-race discipline rather than a service-layer pre-check), the freely-bidirectional status transitions (including reverting satisfied back to pending and confirming `satisfiedAt` is set/cleared correctly), and all three `summary.readyForConversion` cases (all-resolved true, any-pending false, zero-rows vacuously true). Frontend: 4 new tests added to `application-detail.test.tsx` covering the new section's empty state, a pending row's Update Status action, a satisfied row still showing Update Status (no terminal hiding), and the resolved-count summary line. Full suite: 649 backend + 209 frontend tests pass. No live browser walkthrough was performed — this environment has no provisioned dev database, the same limitation every prior Recruitment workstream in this session has had; verification relied on the automated test suites, typecheck, lint, and production build only. Does not implement employee conversion, onboarding, user account creation, payroll/leave/attendance setup, contract execution, asset assignment, training, probation, orientation, candidate accounts, document upload/storage for requirements, or notifications (none explicitly assigned to this workstream in the frozen plan) — all remain later workstreams' scope or explicitly out of the frozen plan entirely.

- **W57 — Offers — Complete.** A versioned offer envelope per application (`offers` + `offer_versions`), taken through a single-step approval chain (`offer_approvals`, mirroring W47's `requisition_approvals` shape exactly, per §9's own "mirrors" instruction) before being issued — the final Recruitment stage this phase reaches. **The key architectural finding this workstream made — the first deliberate exception to "every Recruitment write stays admin-only" this phase:** §7's matrix marks `offer.manage`'s Assigned column "✔ manage draft" — real write capability, not just narrower visibility, unlike every prior write permission this phase (`application.pipeline.move`/`.manage`, `candidate.manage`, `interview.manage`, ...), which stayed org_admin/hr_manager-only regardless of the matrix's own assigned-tier markings, since no delegated recruiter/hiring-manager role exists in this codebase's actual three-role model (org_admin/hr_manager/employee). For offers there is genuinely no other mechanism through which an assigned recruiter or hiring manager (a plain "employee" role holder, identified only via the linked requisition's `recruiterEmployeeId`/`hiringManagerEmployeeId`) could ever exercise it, so `offer.read`/`offer.manage` are seeded broadly to every role — the first genuine precedent-break. Because `offer.manage` is now held by every employee, it can no longer serve as the org-wide-reach signal (unlike every prior resource, where the write permission itself implied admin-ness) — org-wide reach is instead signaled by holding any of the three narrow admin-only actions (`offer.approve`/`.issue`/`.withdraw`, none seeded to employee). Every `offer.manage`-gated write function independently re-verifies the caller is actually the assigned recruiter/hiring manager (via the existing `application → vacancy → requisition` three-hop resolution, applicationPipeline.ts's own established pattern) or org-wide — holding the permission key alone never lets an unrelated employee write an unrelated offer. **Versioning (§14):** editing a `draft` version updates that row in place (`PATCH .../offers/:id`); editing an `approved`/`issued` version instead creates a brand-new draft version and marks the prior one `superseded` in the same transaction (`POST .../offers/:id/versions`, a dedicated endpoint per §10's own naming, not a single dynamically-branching PATCH). §14 is silent on editing while `pending_approval` — this workstream treats that as not editable at all until a decision lands, mirroring W55 scorecards' "submitted = frozen" precedent. **No "reject" action exists** — §10 names only submit-for-approval/approve/issue/withdraw. `withdraw` is therefore the single general abort action, reachable from `pending_approval`, `approved`, or `issued` alike, doing double duty as both "pull back an issued offer" and "reject a pending one." `offer_approvals.decision` still carries the same three-value `pending`/`approved`/`rejected` enum as `requisition_approvals` (§9's own "mirrors" instruction), so `rejected` is a structurally valid but currently API-unreachable value — reserved, not invented from nothing. A withdrawn version's outstanding `offer_approvals` row (if any) is deliberately left `pending`, un-cleaned-up — the same precedent `cancelJobRequisition` already established for a requisition cancelled mid `pending_approval`. **Single-offer-per-application:** §9 marks `offers.applicationId` unique "where policy disallows multiple active offers," conditioned on an org policy flag (§17's `multipleActiveOffersAllowed`) that does not exist in this codebase's actual `recruitment_settings` table (already diverged from §9's prose before this workstream, per W44/W47's own documented gaps) — rather than inventing a new settings column, this workstream enforces the frozen default unconditionally: a plain, non-partial unique index, always one offer per application. Approval is similarly unconditionally required (no `offerApprovalRequired` toggle exists either) — a single, fixed required step, exactly mirroring `requisitionApprovals.ts`'s own no-config-gate precedent. **Reserved, not consumed:** `letterTemplateId`/`generatedDocumentStorageKey` are nullable columns per §9's own field list, with no offer-letter-template table and no document-generation logic built in this three-table frozen scope (§15: "offer letters are generated as stored HTML/text documents... no e-signature integration" — but no template-rendering mechanism is named to build it with). `generatedDocumentStorageKey` is stripped from every API response via a `PublicOfferVersion` DTO (the same discipline as W55's `externalInterviewerToken` and W56's `documentStorageKey`, applied proactively even though this workstream's own routes never populate it) — verified by a dedicated regression test; `letterTemplateId` stays (a harmless, always-null FK-shaped integer). Terminal states `accepted`/`declined`/`expired` are schema-valid but have no routes here — no candidate-facing acceptance/decline flow and no expiry scheduler exist anywhere in this codebase — a deliberate scope boundary. `compensationSummary` is an unvalidated, caller-supplied jsonb object (recruitment-scoped fields only — base salary, currency, bonus, benefits summary — never a full payroll structure, per CLAUDE.md's no-payroll-dependency principle), mirroring `candidates.experienceSummary`'s own precedent; never embedded in audit metadata. **Permissions:** `offer.read`/`.manage` seeded org_admin/hr_manager/employee (broad, per the finding above); `offer.approve`/`.issue`/`.withdraw` org_admin/hr_manager only, organization-wide only, no assigned tier at all — the same admin-only rollout every other Recruitment approval/finalization action this phase uses. **API:** `GET`/`POST .../applications/:id/offers`, `GET`/`PATCH .../offers/:id`, `POST .../offers/:id/versions`, `POST .../offers/versions/:id/submit-for-approval`, `GET .../offers/versions/:id/approvals`, `POST .../offers/versions/:id/approve`, `POST .../offers/versions/:id/issue`, `POST .../offers/versions/:id/withdraw` — new OpenAPI schemas (`Offer`, `OfferVersion`, `OfferDetail`, `OfferListItem`, `OfferListResponse`, `OfferApproval`, `CreateOfferInput`, `UpdateOfferVersionInput`, `ApproveOfferVersionInput`, `WithdrawOfferVersionInput`) under a new `offers` tag, codegen verified zero-diff across two consecutive runs (one nullable-object-via-`allOf` schema for `OfferListItem.currentVersion` hit the same broken orval pattern W55 already documented — fixed the same way, with a plain inlined `type: ["object", "null"]` shape). **Frontend:** `/offers` (list, org-wide + assigned visibility) and `/offers/:id` (full lifecycle: edit draft, create new version, submit, approve, issue, withdraw, version history, approval history) per §11's own frontend-impact line, plus a new "Offer" section on `/applications/:id` (create/view, mirroring the Reference/Background Checks sections' subcomponent style) and an "Offers" nav link (gated the same `isHrCapable`-only way every other Recruitment nav entry already is — an assigned employee still reaches their own offer via the application-detail deep link, the same UX precedent `/interviews` already established). **Audit:** `offer.created`, `offer_version.updated`/`.superseded`/`.submitted`/`.approved`/`.issued`/`.withdrawn` — the individual `offer_approvals` chain-row append is self-documenting (§20's own exemption list explicitly names `offer_approvals` alongside `application_stage_history`/`requisition_approvals`/finalized `interview_scorecards`), but the resulting
