offer-version status transition still gets its own `recordAuditEvent` call, mirroring `requisitionApprovals.ts`'s exact precedent. **Database impact:** migration `0032_burly_molecule_man.sql` (three new tables + three new enums, purely additive) generated with a hand-authored `.down.sql`, not applied — confirmed zero further drift after generation. Backend: 34 new tests (`offers.test.ts`, covering the application→vacancy→requisition visibility chain, the assigned-recruiter real-write exception, duplicate-offer 409, draft-edit-in-place vs. new-version-on-approved/issued, submit/approve/issue/withdraw transitions and their invalid-state 400/409s, approval-history visibility, and the generatedDocumentStorageKey-never-leaks regression on two separate response shapes). Frontend: 19 new tests (6 `offers.test.tsx`, 10 `offer-detail.test.tsx` covering per-status action visibility across every non-terminal state plus the terminal no-actions case, 3 added to `application-detail.test.tsx` for the new Offer section's empty/populated/403-silent states). Full suite: 634 backend + 205 frontend tests pass. No live browser walkthrough was performed — this environment has no provisioned dev database, the same limitation every prior Recruitment workstream in this session has had; verification relied on the automated test suites, typecheck, lint, and production build only. Does not implement offer letter generation/e-signature, candidate-facing offer acceptance/decline, automated expiry, multi-step/delegated approval chains, or employee conversion — all remain later workstreams' scope or explicitly out of the frozen plan entirely.

- **W56 — Reference & Background Checks — Complete.** Status-tracked checks, no vendor integration — informs recruitment decisions, never makes them: never automatically rejects an application, moves the pipeline, creates an offer, or hires/converts a candidate. Two deliberately distinct business processes, kept in two separate tables and two separate lib/route files rather than merged just because both track a status. **Scope boundary — the biggest reconciliation this workstream made:** §7's permission matrix has **no dedicated `reference_check.*` permission at all** — only "Background checks" gets its own row. Reference checks therefore reuse the existing `application.read`/`.manage` pair (the same tier as viewing/scoring the application itself, W52's own precedent for `application.manage` gating an assessment action), directly importing `applicationPipeline.ts`'s `resolveApplicationVisibilityContext`/`getVisibleApplicationById` rather than re-deriving the candidate→vacancy→requisition chain a second time. Background checks are the opposite extreme — §7 marks that row org-wide only with **no assigned tier at all** ("the narrowest permission in the matrix," §23's own verification line): holding `application.read`/`.manage` (or even `candidate.read`) never implies background-check access, verified by a dedicated 403 test. **Status model (§4.7, shared by both tables):** `requested → in_progress → (completed | flagged | unable_to_complete)` — no "cancelled"/"expired" state exists in the frozen model; a check that can't be completed is recorded as `unable_to_complete`. Terminal once completed/flagged/unable_to_complete — no further status change, no result changes after finalization, enforced by re-checking the existing row's status before every update (400 otherwise). **Reference checks:** column list is exactly §9's row — `applicationId`, `refereeName`/`Contact`/`Relationship`, `status`, `notes`, `completedAt` — no separate "verification actor" or "supporting document" column exists in the frozen model, so neither was built. Duplicate-active-check prevention is a service-layer check (no unique constraint exists on the table), keyed on `(applicationId, refereeContact)`. **Background checks:** column list is exactly §9's row — `applicationId`, `checkType` (free text — no Master Data domain exists in this frozen scope, so criteria/types are never hard-coded, e.g. no Ghana-specific provider list), `status`, `vendorReference` (a plain manually-entered string — "an integration boundary," never a real vendor API call), `resultSummary`, `documentStorageKey`. Duplicate-active-check prevention is keyed on `(applicationId, checkType)`. **A real DTO leak caught and fixed during this workstream's own security review, before commit (the same class of issue W55 caught for its reserved token columns):** `documentStorageKey` was being spread straight from the raw DB row into every API response; fixed with a `PublicBackgroundCheck` shape that omits it entirely in favor of a computed `hasEvidence` boolean, so the frontend can show a download link without the server ever handing back an internal storage reference — verified by a dedicated regression test. **Consent:** deliberately not gated — no `consentReference`/consent-linkage column exists anywhere in the frozen `background_checks` row, so no check-specific consent verification was implemented; W49's existing `candidate_consents` (captured once, at application submission) is not silently reinterpreted as blanket permission for every future check, but no second, W56-specific consent record was invented either, since the frozen plan doesn't call for one — a documented limitation, not an oversight. **Documents:** evidence reuses `documentValidation.ts`'s existing signature-verified upload (same PDF/JPEG/PNG/DOCX/XLSX/10MB policy as every other upload in this codebase) and `fileStorage.ts`'s private, org-scoped `"background-checks"` subdirectory — never a public URL, never the candidate's own `candidate_documents` row. A second upload replaces the first (deleting the old file), and any upload is rejected once the check is terminal. Evidence download streams the file through an authenticated, `background_check.read`-gated route (`res.set("Content-Type", "application/octet-stream")` + `Content-Disposition: attachment`), mirroring `employees.ts`'s existing profile-picture-download precedent — never a static/guessable path. **Permissions:** `background_check.read`/`.manage` seeded org_admin/hr_manager only, no employee-role grant at all (same org-wide-only rollout as `talent_pool.read`/`.manage`) — reference checks need no new permission keys. **API:** `GET`/`POST .../applications/:id/reference-checks`, `PATCH .../reference-checks/:id`; `GET`/`POST .../applications/:id/background-checks`, `PATCH .../background-checks/:id`, `POST`/`GET .../background-checks/:id/evidence` — new OpenAPI schemas (`ReferenceCheck`, `CreateReferenceCheckInput`, `UpdateReferenceCheckStatusInput`, `BackgroundCheck`, `CreateBackgroundCheckInput`, `UpdateBackgroundCheckStatusInput`, `ReferenceBackgroundCheckStatus`) under new `reference-checks`/`background-checks` tags, codegen verified zero-diff across two consecutive runs. **Frontend:** two new sections on `/applications/:id` (§11's own frontend-impact line) — Reference Checks (list, request dialog, Record Outcome dialog, hidden once terminal) and Background Checks (list, request dialog, Record Result dialog, evidence attach/replace/download, all write actions hidden once terminal) — the Background Checks section silently renders nothing on a 403 rather than showing a scary error card, since lacking `background_check.read` is an expected, permission-appropriate state, not a failure. **Audit:** `reference_check.created`/`.status_changed`, `background_check.created`/`.status_changed`/`.evidence_attached` — metadata deliberately excludes refereeContact, notes, resultSummary, vendorReference, and documentStorageKey; only status/checkType/applicationId are recorded. **Database impact:** migration `0031_premium_wolfsbane.sql` (two new tables + one new shared enum, purely additive) generated with a hand-authored `.down.sql`, not applied — confirmed zero further drift after generation. Backend: 24 new tests (`referenceChecks.test.ts` — 10, reusing the full W51 application-visibility mock chain; `backgroundChecks.test.ts` — 14, a much smaller flat-permission harness) covering permission gating (including the general-permissions-never-bypass-background_check-access proof), tenant isolation, assigned/org-wide application visibility for reference checks, duplicate-check prevention for both resources, status transitions, terminal immutability, evidence upload/download/signature-validation, and a no-pipeline-side-effect proof. Frontend: 7 new tests added to `application-detail.test.tsx` covering both sections' empty/populated/terminal states and the silent-403 behavior for background checks. Full suite: 600 backend + 186 frontend tests pass. No live browser walkthrough was performed — this environment has no provisioned dev database, the same limitation every prior Recruitment workstream in this session has had; verification relied on the automated test suites, typecheck, lint, and production build only. Does not implement external background-check provider/government-database integrations, automated identity/criminal-record verification, a referee public portal, candidate accounts, offers, hiring decisions, employee conversion, or AI risk scoring — all remain later workstreams' scope or explicitly out of the frozen plan entirely.
- **W55 — Interview Scorecards — Complete.** Independent, lockable evaluations — one per panel member per interview — never redesigns W54 (interviews/panel membership are read-only inputs here, never written to) and never mixes with W52's `application_scores` (a distinct business process: screening vs. interview evaluation, never combined into one rollup). A scorecard informs later decisions; it never moves the W51 application stage or triggers any offer/hiring action itself. **Scope boundary — the single biggest reconciliation this workstream made:** the frozen §9 table plan defines exactly two tables (`interview_scorecards`, `interview_scorecard_responses`) with no template/criteria table, no `weight` column, and no rating scale anywhere in the model — so, despite the session prompt's own extensive "scorecard template," "criteria weighting," and "template builder UI" language (all explicitly hedged as "expected concepts may include"), none of that was built. `criterion` is plain free text supplied per submission (not organization-configured), and `rating` is an unconstrained integer, mirroring `application_scores.score`'s own unconstrained-numeric precedent — a documented limitation, not an oversight. **Lifecycle (§9's own "draft until submittedAt, immutable after"):** draft (`submittedAt` null) → submitted (`submittedAt` set, immutable from the owning interviewer's side) → finalized (`finalizedAt` set, an HR/recruiter-only lock, §7 — no "own" tier exists for finalize at all, so an interviewer can never lock their own scorecard). §10 lists no separate submit/reschedule-style route, so the one `POST .../interviews/:id/scorecards` upserts the caller's own draft and, given `submit: true`, transitions it to submitted in the same call; any further call once submitted is rejected outright (400) — "a submitted scorecard cannot be silently replaced." **Visibility — a direct, explicit rule from §7's own integrity note, not a rollout judgment call this time:** `scorecard.submit` never implies `scorecard.read_all` — an interviewer must never see a colleague's scorecard, submitted or not, through this API; only a `scorecard.read_all` holder (org_admin/hr_manager) sees every panel member's scorecard plus a computed (never stored) panel-completion summary (submitted/pending counts, recommendation tally — same discipline as W52's `scoreRollup`). Panel membership is re-verified fresh against `interview_panel_members` on every single write, never cached, so a since-removed panel member is rejected going forward without any special-case code. `conflictDeclared` (W54) carries no automated restriction in this workstream — informational only, no rule anywhere in the frozen plan attaches behavior to it. **A real leak caught and fixed during this workstream's own security review, before commit:** the reserved, not-yet-consumed `externalInterviewerToken`/`externalInterviewerTokenExpiresAt` columns (present in §9's schema for a later workstream to wire up external-panel evaluation — §10 names no such route here, so it is explicitly deferred, mirroring `vacancies.publicId`'s own "reserved, not consumed" precedent) were being spread straight from the raw DB row into every API response; fixed by explicitly omitting both fields before any scorecard ever reaches a DTO, with a dedicated regression test asserting neither field is ever present even when the underlying row has a token set. **Permissions:** `scorecard.submit` seeded to every role (any employee could be an assigned panel interviewer, same broad rollout as `interview.read`); `scorecard.read_all` and `scorecard.finalize` are org_admin/hr_manager-only with no assigned tier at all — directly stated in §7's matrix itself for these two keys, not an inferred rollout choice. The GET route's own permission gate is manual (not the standard single-key middleware), since either `scorecard.submit` or `scorecard.read_all` alone should grant entry — a bug caught by this workstream's own cross-org test failing during development, fixed before commit. **Audit — deliberately none:** §20's Audit Plan explicitly names finalized `interview_scorecards` among the tables that are "routine, already-self-documenting movements" not duplicated into `audit_events` (alongside `application_stage_history`/`requisition_approvals`/`offer_approvals`) — the row's own `interviewerMembershipId`/`submittedAt`/`finalizedAt` columns already record who and when. **API:** `GET .../interviews/:id/scorecards`, `POST .../interviews/:id/scorecards`, `POST .../scorecards/:id/finalize` — new OpenAPI schemas (`InterviewScorecard`, `InterviewScorecardResponse`, `ResponseInput`, `SaveInterviewScorecardInput`, `InterviewScorecardListResponse`, `RecommendationCounts`) under a new `interview-scorecards` tag, codegen verified zero-diff across two consecutive runs (one nullable-object-via-`allOf` schema pattern was tried first, produced a broken `(unknown | null) & X` TypeScript type via orval, and was replaced with a plain inlined `type: ["object", "null"]` shape instead). **Frontend:** a dedicated `/interviews/:id/scorecard` route (per §11's own frontend-impact line) — a draft/submit evaluation form (recommendation select, overall comment, dynamic criterion/rating/comment rows) for panel members, a submit-confirmation dialog warning about immutability, a read-only view once submitted, and — for `scorecard.read_all` holders — a panel-completion-summary card plus every evaluator's scorecard with a per-row Finalize action; a minimal "Scorecard" link was added to `interview-detail.tsx` (W54) without otherwise touching that page. Draft-form state is lazily initialized from props in a dedicated `MyEvaluationCard` subcomponent (not a `useEffect`-driven sync), avoiding this codebase's `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` lint rule entirely. **Database impact:** migration `0030_wide_doctor_octopus.sql` (two new tables + one new enum, purely additive) generated with a hand-authored `.down.sql`, not applied — confirmed zero further drift after generation. Backend: 15 new tests (`interviewScorecards.test.ts`) covering permission gating, tenant isolation, not-a-panel-member rejection, cancelled-interview rejection, draft upsert, submit-then-immutable, post-removal rejection, read_all-vs-own-only visibility (including a submitted colleague's scorecard staying invisible to a submit-only caller), panel-summary computation, finalize/double-finalize/finalize-a-draft rejection, and the externalInterviewerToken-never-leaks regression. Frontend: 8 new tests (`interview-scorecard.test.tsx`) covering loading/error/cancelled states, blank-draft rendering, the submit-confirmation warning, read-only rendering of a submitted scorecard, and the panel-summary/finalize-button visibility (including hiding Finalize once already finalized). Full suite: 576 backend + 179 frontend tests pass. No live browser walkthrough was performed — this environment has no provisioned dev database, the same limitation every prior Recruitment workstream in this session has had; verification relied on the automated test suites, typecheck, lint, and production build only. Does not implement scorecard templates/criteria configuration, weighted scoring, external-panel-member evaluation submission (deferred — reserved columns only), recommendations beyond the frozen four values, hiring decisions, offer generation, calendar/video integrations, or notifications — all remain later workstreams' scope or explicitly out of the frozen plan entirely.
- **W54 — Interviews & Scheduling — Complete.** Scheduling and panel composition only — this workstream never evaluates an interview (scores/recommendations/hiring decisions are W55's `interview_scorecards`, a wholly separate table this workstream never touches). Built on top of W51's existing `applications` records, never redesigning them. **Status model (§4.5):** `scheduled -> completed | cancelled | no_show`. "Rescheduled" is not a stored status — realized entirely through the one PATCH route (§10 lists no separate reschedule/complete/no-show endpoint): supplying `scheduledAt` cancels the existing row and creates a brand new one (never mutating a scheduled interview's date in place, the same "never edit history in place" discipline as `application_stage_history`); omitting `scheduledAt` performs an ordinary in-place update, including a status transition to completed/no_show or a full panel replace. **Visibility — a genuine departure from every prior Recruitment resource's pattern:** §7's Interviews row marks the assigned tier "own scheduled interviews as interviewer," not the recruiter/hiring-manager-on-linked-requisition chain every other resource (candidates, vacancies, applications) uses — an interview carries no such column at all. Resolved instead by a direct check of whether the caller's own membership appears as an `interviewerMembershipId` on that specific interview's panel; org-wide reach is still signaled by holding `interview.manage`, the same pattern as everywhere else. **Permissions:** §7's Interviews row is a single `interview.read`/`.manage` pair (unlike every prior resource's two-key read/write split) with the assigned marker against that one pair — kept consistent with this codebase's established rollout rather than treated as a new exception: `interview.read` is seeded to every role (any employee could be an assigned panel interviewer); `interview.manage` (schedule/update/reschedule/cancel/panel changes — no dedicated panel-management permission, per §7's own "avoid permission explosion" note) stays org_admin/hr_manager-only, the same admin-only rollout every other Recruitment write action uses regardless of a resource's read-side assigned tier. **Panel:** new `interview_panel_members` table — `interviewerMembershipId` nullable for an external interviewer, captured by name/email only (§17 decision 13 — no external-interviewer portal, no login); a partial unique index on `(interviewId, interviewerMembershipId)` where not null lets several external interviewers coexist freely on one interview while preventing the same internal interviewer being added twice; `conflictDeclared` is a plain self-declared flag with no automated behavior attached in this workstream. Panel composition is fully replaced (delete + reinsert) on every update that supplies a `panelMembers` array, mirroring `vacancies.ts`'s locations/questions embedded-array convention, rather than incremental add/remove endpoints. **Reconciliation — two top-level routes beyond §10's literal nested text:** `GET .../interviews` and `GET .../interviews/:id` were added at the organization root, not nested under one application, to back the frozen §11 frontend route `/interviews` ("calendar/list of scheduled interviews for the caller") and its detail page — the same top-level-list precedent W51 already established for `/organizations/:organizationId/applications` despite every application belonging to one vacancy. Scheduling/updating remain nested under `.../applications/:id/interviews[/:id]` and cancel stays a top-level `.../interviews/:id/cancel`, exactly matching §10's literal text. **Database:** two new tables — `interviews` (`applicationId`, `interviewType` enum `phone`/`virtual`/`in_person`, `scheduledAt` `timestamptz`, `durationMinutes`, `location`/`meetingLink`, `status`, `outcome` — column list is exactly §9's row; no `notes`/`timezone`/separate-end-time field exists there, so none were added — `scheduledAt` is inherently timezone-aware, an end time is derived from `scheduledAt + durationMinutes`, never stored) and `interview_panel_members`. **API:** `GET`/`GET .../interviews/:id`, `POST .../interviews/:id/cancel` (top-level); `GET`/`POST .../applications/:id/interviews`, `PATCH .../applications/:id/interviews/:id` (nested) — new OpenAPI schemas (`Interview`, `InterviewPanelMember`, `PanelMemberInput`, `InterviewListResponse`, `ScheduleInterviewInput`, `UpdateInterviewInput`) under a new `interviews` tag, codegen verified zero-diff across two consecutive runs. **Frontend:** `/interviews` (calendar/list, status filter), `/interviews/:id` (detail: type/schedule/location/meeting-link/outcome, panel list resolving internal panelists' names via the existing organization-members endpoint, reschedule/mark-completed/mark-no-show/cancel actions, a panel-edit dialog with internal-member-select and external name/email capture) — both gated by `<ModuleGate moduleKey="recruitment">`, a new "Interviews" nav link shown to `org_admin`/`hr_manager`. Additive tie-in: `application-detail.tsx` (W51) gains an Interviews card (§11 names interviews as part of `/applications/:id`) listing that application's interviews with a Schedule Interview dialog, linking each row to `/interviews/:id`. **Audit:** `interview.scheduled`/`.rescheduled`/`.cancelled`/`.panel_updated`/`.status_changed` recorded on every mutation — per §20's own audit plan, `interviews`/`interview_panel_members` are notably *not* among the tables explicitly exempted from `audit_events` duplication (unlike finalized `interview_scorecards`), so this workstream audits directly rather than relying on the rows' own columns alone. **Database impact:** migration `0029_flawless_captain_midlands.sql` (two new tables + three new enums, purely additive) generated with a hand-authored `.down.sql`, not applied — confirmed zero further drift after generation. Backend: 19 new tests (`interviews.test.ts`) covering schedule/permission gating, cross-org 404s, the own-panel-membership-vs-org-wide visibility split (including proof that org-wide `candidate.manage` does *not* grant interview access), reschedule-as-new-row (old row cancelled, new row a genuinely different id, panel carried over), status transitions to completed/no_show, full panel replace, double-cancel 400, and panel-member validation (internal-and-external-both rejected, cross-org membership rejected). Frontend: 13 new tests (`interviews.test.tsx`, `interview-detail.test.tsx`) covering loading/error/empty states, status badge rendering, action-visibility gating by status (scheduled vs. completed), and panel-member name resolution (internal vs. external, conflict-declared flag) — plus the existing `application-detail.test.tsx` mock was extended for the two new hooks it now calls, with all 13 of its prior assertions still passing unchanged. Full suite: 561 backend + 171 frontend tests pass. No live browser walkthrough was performed — this environment has no provisioned dev database, the same limitation every prior Recruitment workstream in this session has had; verification relied on the automated test suites, typecheck, lint, and production build only. Does not implement interview scorecards, scoring, recommendations, hiring decisions, offer generation, candidate accounts, calendar integrations (Google/Microsoft 365/Zoom/Teams/Meet), or email reminders beyond this workstream's own audit trail — all remain W55's or later workstreams' scope.
- **W53 — Candidate Notes, Tags, and Talent Pools — Complete.** Collaboration and passive-sourcing features on top of W49's existing `candidates`/`applications` records — never redesigns the candidate record itself (no `PATCH /candidates/:id` was built, despite appearing in the consolidated §10 API Plan: this workstream's own compact §23 scope line names exactly four new tables and nothing else, the same precedent every prior workstream has followed of treating §23 as the scope boundary and §7/§9/§10/§11 as field/permission detail only). Notes, tags, and talent pools are three deliberately independent abstractions — no shared "collaboration" table or merged model. **Candidates (internal read, new this workstream):** new `lib/candidates.ts` — `GET .../candidates` (paginated, name/email search) and `GET .../candidates/:id`, visibility-resolved via the same three-hop batched traversal pattern as every other Recruitment resource (candidate → its applications → their vacancies → linked requisitions), org-wide for `candidate.manage` holders or assigned via a matching `recruiterEmployeeId`/`hiringManagerEmployeeId` on any reachable requisition; a non-visible candidate 404s identically to a nonexistent one. **Notes:** new `candidate_notes` table (`candidateId`, nullable `applicationId` distinguishing a candidate-level note from an application-scoped one, `authorMembershipId`, `note`) — create-only, no update/delete path, mirroring `candidate_consents`'/`application_scores`' append-only precedent; a supplied `applicationId` is validated server-side to actually belong to the candidate (400 otherwise). Never exposed to an applicant — no candidate-session read path exists anywhere in this codebase (W50 still deferred). **Tags:** new `candidate_tags` table, plain free-text `tag` column (deliberately never an enum or Master Data domain, per instruction that tag values are never hard-coded), unique on `(candidateId, tag)`; add/remove only, duplicate-insert races translated via the existing `isUniqueViolation` helper. **Talent pools:** new `talent_pools` (org-scoped, unique name per org, active/archived, mirrors `recruitment_workflows.ts`'s exact archive/reactivate shape) and `talent_pool_members` (unique on `(talentPoolId, candidateId)`) tables — a pool is never tied to a single vacancy or requisition, so candidates remain reusable across future campaigns. **Permissions — a deliberate split discovered while reconciling this workstream's own permission matrix row against established precedent:** `candidate.read` and `candidate.notes.read` are both seeded to every role (same reasoning as `vacancy.read`/`application.read` — any employee could turn out to be the assigned recruiter/hiring manager, resolved per-record in the service layer); `candidate.manage` and `candidate.notes.write` are org_admin/hr_manager-only, since every Recruitment *write* action in this codebase stays administrative-only regardless of a resource's read-side assigned tier (mirrors `application.manage`/`application.pipeline.move` over `application.read`'s exact precedent) — `candidate.manage` also gates tag add/remove, avoiding a dedicated tags permission. `talent_pool.read`/`.manage` are org-wide only, org_admin/hr_manager-only with no assigned tier at all (§7 — a pool isn't reachable through any one requisition's recruiter/hiring-manager), mirroring `leave_type.manage`'s rollout; verified by a test asserting an assigned recruiter without `talent_pool.manage` still gets 403. **API:** `GET .../candidates`, `GET .../candidates/:id`, `GET`/`POST .../candidates/:id/notes`, `GET`/`POST .../candidates/:id/tags`, `DELETE .../candidates/:id/tags/:tagId`, `GET`/`POST .../talent-pools`, `GET`/`PATCH .../talent-pools/:id`, `POST .../talent-pools/:id/archive`, `POST .../talent-pools/:id/reactivate`, `GET`/`POST .../talent-pools/:id/members`, `DELETE .../talent-pools/:id/members/:candidateId` — new OpenAPI schemas (`Candidate`, `CandidateListResponse`, `CandidateNote`, `CreateCandidateNoteInput`, `CandidateTag`, `AddCandidateTagInput`, `TalentPool`, `CreateTalentPoolInput`, `UpdateTalentPoolInput`, `TalentPoolMember`, `AddTalentPoolMemberInput`) under new `candidates`/`talent-pools` tags, codegen verified zero-diff across two consecutive runs. **Frontend:** `/candidates/:id` (candidate info, tags with inline add/remove, notes list with an add-note form, distinguishing application-scoped notes) and `/talent-pools` (pool list, create dialog, archive/reactivate, a members-management dialog with candidate search-to-add) — both gated by `<ModuleGate moduleKey="recruitment">`, a new "Talent Pools" nav link shown to `org_admin`/`hr_manager`. Deliberately no standalone `/candidates` directory page (only `/candidates/:id` and `/talent-pools`, per this workstream's own frontend-impact line, even though the consolidated §11 plan separately lists a directory page) — a minimal additive tie-in links `application-detail.tsx`'s (W51) candidate name to its new `/candidates/:candidateId` profile. **Audit:** `candidate_note.created`, `candidate_tag.added`/`.removed`, `talent_pool.created`/`.updated`/`.archived`/`.reactivated`/`.member_added`/`.member_removed` recorded on every mutation. **Database impact:** migration `0028_simple_onslaught.sql` (four new tables, purely additive) generated with a hand-authored `.down.sql`, not applied — confirmed zero further drift after generation. Backend: 22 new tests (`candidatesTalentPools.test.ts`) covering candidate visibility (org-wide/assigned/cross-org-isolation), notes gating (`.read` alone insufficient to write) and applicationId-ownership validation, tag add/list/remove, and talent-pool CRUD/archive/reactivate/membership including the no-assigned-tier permission proof. Frontend: 16 new tests (`candidate-detail.test.tsx`, `talent-pools.test.tsx`) covering loading/error/empty states, tag and note rendering, and the members-management dialog. Full suite: 542 backend + 158 frontend tests pass. Does not implement interviews, offer management, employee conversion, candidate accounts/login, email campaigns, AI ranking, resume parsing, or external recruitment integrations — all remain later workstreams' or W50's scope.
- **W52 — Screening Questions & Scoring — Complete.** Answer capture (into W49's existing apply endpoint) plus internal scoring, on top of W47's `vacancy_questions` and W51's application pipeline — neither W49 nor W51 was redesigned, both were extended. **Reconciliation (per the handoff's own instruction to check the compact §23 entry against the fuller spec before building):** §23's terse W52 entry ("Answer capture, knockout evaluation, scoring rollup") omits two load-bearing rules that only exist in §12 (Screening, Scoring, and Pipeline Notes) — (1) knockout evaluation happens **at submission time**, server-side, and a failed knockout only **flags** the answer row for recruiter review, it **never auto-rejects** the application; (2) `applications.score` (defined since W49, always null) "is a computed, non-authoritative rollup ... recomputed from `application_scores` on read, not trusted as stored state" — mirroring `leave_balance_entries`' ledger precedent — so this workstream never writes to that column, only computes an equivalent rollup at read time. Missing either rule would have produced a materially wrong implementation (auto-rejecting candidates on a miskeyed expected answer; persisting a stale score). **Answer capture:** `submitPublicApplication` (W49, `lib/candidateApplications.ts`) now accepts an optional `answers: {vacancyQuestionId, answerText}[]`, sent as a JSON-encoded string field alongside the resume file in the same multipart apply request (multipart/form-data has no native array-of-objects support) — a `vacancyQuestionId` not belonging to the vacancy is silently ignored, never an error, since answers are optional and a mismatched id carries no security implication. Knockout evaluation (`computeKnockoutFailed`) applies only to `yes_no`/`multiple_choice` questions with a non-null `expectedAnswer` (§12 — free-text/numeric have no single canonical comparison); a normalized (trim+lowercase) mismatch sets `knockoutFailed = true` on the new `application_answers` row and nothing else. The public vacancy detail DTO (`lib/publicCareers.ts`) now also returns a `questions: PublicVacancyQuestion[]` array — deliberately excluding `isKnockout`/`expectedAnswer`, since a candidate must never learn which questions are knockout-screened or what answer is "correct." **Scoring:** new `lib/applicationScoring.ts`, append-only — `submitApplicationScore` inserts a new `application_scores` row every time (never an edit), gated by a new `application.manage` permission (already named, unused, in the frozen §7 matrix) rather than W51's `application.pipeline.move`, since scoring evaluates an application without ever changing its stage. `computeScoreRollup` (a pure function over the score list, never persisted): an explicit `overall`-type entry wins outright if one exists; otherwise the average of whichever of `screening`/`interview` have a latest entry; `null` when no scores exist. Deliberately never imports from `applicationPipeline.ts` (which imports this module's rollup helpers for the detail DTO) — a new, distinct `ApplicationScoreTargetNotFoundError` is defined here instead, mirroring `requisitionApprovals.ts`'s established precedent for keeping a mutual two-file dependency one-directional rather than circular. **A visibility gap found and fixed during this workstream:** the org-wide visibility check for applications (`resolveApplicationVisibilityContext`, W51) originally keyed only off `application.pipeline.move`, so a caller holding only the new `application.manage` (in principle, a scoring-only role) could submit a score but then get a null response back, since they couldn't see the application they'd just legitimately acted on. Fixed to treat either administrative permission as org-wide — caught by this workstream's own tests before it shipped, not discovered later. **Database:** two new tables — `application_answers` (`applicationId`, `vacancyQuestionId`, `answerText`, `knockoutFailed`, unique on `(applicationId, vacancyQuestionId)`, write-once) and `application_scores` (`applicationId`, `scoredByMembershipId`, `scoreType` enum `screening`/`interview`/`overall`, `score` `numeric(5,2)`, `notes`, no unique constraint — multiple entries per type are expected as independent reviewers score separately) — both append-only, no update/delete path anywhere. **API:** the existing `POST /careers/:orgSlug/jobs/:vacancyPublicId/apply` gains the `answers` field (no new public route); new `POST /organizations/:organizationId/applications/:id/scores` (`application.manage`-gated, returns the refreshed `ApplicationDetail`); `GET .../applications/:id` (W51) now also returns `answers[]` (with each question's text resolved for display), `scores[]` (newest first), and the computed `scoreRollup` — new OpenAPI schemas (`ApplicationAnswerSummary`, `ApplicationScoreEntry`, `SubmitApplicationScoreInput`, `PublicVacancyQuestion`), codegen verified zero-diff across two consecutive runs. **Frontend:** `careers-apply.tsx` (W49) now renders the vacancy's screening questions (a `Select` for `yes_no`, a typed `Input` for the rest) and JSON-encodes answered questions into the submission; `application-detail.tsx` (W51) gains a Screening Answers card (rendered only when answers exist, flags a failed knockout) and a Scoring card (score list, a rollup badge, an inline submit-score form shown only while the application is non-terminal). No Kanban/scorecard UI beyond this — interview scorecards remain a later workstream's scope. **Audit:** `application.scored` recorded on every score submission, mirroring the existing `application.*` event naming from W51. **Database impact:** migration `0027_violet_ozymandias.sql` (two new tables + one new enum, purely additive) generated with a hand-authored `.down.sql`, not applied — confirmed zero further drift after generation. Backend: 9 new tests (3 in `publicCareers.test.ts` covering answer capture, the non-rejecting knockout flag, and cross-vacancy question filtering; 6 in `applicationPipeline.test.ts` covering score submission, the `application.manage` permission gate, the visibility-gap fix, the overall-wins/average rollup rules, and cross-org 404). Frontend: 8 new tests (3 in `careers-apply.test.tsx` covering question rendering and the JSON-encoded answers payload; 5 in `application-detail.test.tsx` covering answer/knockout rendering, score rendering with the rollup badge, and the score form's terminal-vs-non-terminal visibility). Does not implement interview scheduling/scorecards, assessments beyond this scoring primitive, offers, hiring decisions, employee conversion, talent pools, background checks, recruiter messaging, or reporting dashboards. Does not touch W50 (still deferred) or close the outstanding W39 ESS scope, which remains open.
- **W51 — Application Pipeline & Stage Movement — Complete.** The start of the ATS: internal review of applications already created by W49's public apply flow, and controlled movement through the organization's own configured recruitment workflow. Never redesigns W49 — reuses its `candidates`/`applications`/`candidate_documents` records unchanged, and W44's existing `recruitment_stages` unchanged as the stage model. **Stage model:** stages are W44's own org-configurable `recruitment_stages`, not a new hardcoded enum — every stage maps to one of the frozen plan's eight fixed categories (`applied`/`screening`/`interview`/`assessment`/`offer`/`hired`/`rejected`/`withdrawn`, §4.3); system logic keys off category, never an organization's own stage label. `hired`/`rejected`/`withdrawn` are terminal — no further movement except the dedicated `reopen` action. Every W49-submitted application starts with `currentStageId = null` (stage assignment was explicitly deferred to this workstream); the first movement's history row has `fromStageId = null`, which the schema anticipated. A never-triaged application (`currentStageId` null) is treated as the `applied` category for display purposes only — never written to the row. **Database:** one new table, `application_stage_history` (`applicationId`, `fromStageId` nullable, `toStageId` not-null, `movedByMembershipId`, `reason` — the optional comment, `movedAt`) — append-only, mirrors `requisition_approvals`'/`candidate_consents`' immutability discipline; no separate comments table (the frozen plan's own scope/database-impact lines name exactly one new table). **Transitions:** `moveApplicationStage` validates the target stage server-side against the application's own vacancy's workflow stage list — never a client-supplied "next stage" trusted as-is (§10) — rejecting a target outside that workflow, a target whose category is itself terminal (terminal categories are reachable only through their own dedicated actions below), or any movement while the application is already in a terminal stage. `rejectApplication`/`withdrawApplication` resolve the workflow's own `rejected`/`withdrawn`-category stage (lowest `displayOrder` if more than one is configured) and set `applications.rejectionReasonCode`/`withdrawalReasonCode` (both already existed, unused, since W49) — 400 if the org hasn't configured a matching-category stage, or the application is already terminal. `reopenApplication` moves a terminal application back to the workflow's `applied`-category stage, clearing both reason codes — 400 if the application isn't currently terminal, or no `applied`-category stage exists. Every transition is one `db.transaction` (history insert + `applications.currentStageId` update), so history and the current-stage pointer can never diverge. **Deliberately not enforced:** `reapplicationWaitingDays`/`duplicateCandidatePolicy` (W44) still have no terminal-state-triggered behavior to act on in this workstream — rejection/withdrawal exist now, but re-application after one is a distinct future capability, not built here. **Visibility:** same two-tier model as W47's vacancies — organization-wide (via holding `application.pipeline.move`) or assigned (via the application's vacancy's linked requisition's `recruiterEmployeeId`/`hiringManagerEmployeeId`, two hops out, batched not N+1); no candidate-session ("own") tier — anonymous applicants never reach these routes, consistent with W50's deferral. A not-visible application returns 404, identical to nonexistent, on both list-exclusion and direct `GET .../:id`. **Permissions:** `application.read` (seeded to every role, mirrors `vacancy.read`/`requisition.read`'s reasoning), `application.pipeline.move` (gates move-stage/reject/withdraw/reopen — org_admin/hr_manager/super_admin only, mirrors `vacancy.publish`/`.close`'s exact rollout; the permission matrix's "Assigned" column is realized as a visibility tier only, not a broader role grant, consistent with every prior Recruitment workstream's precedent). **API:** `GET .../applications`, `GET .../applications/:id` (embeds `documents[]` and immutable `history[]` directly — no separate `/history` route, mirroring W47's vacancy-embeds-locations/questions convention; the frozen API list names no such route either), `POST .../applications/:id/move-stage`, `.../reject`, `.../withdraw`, `.../reopen` — new OpenAPI paths/schemas (`ApplicationSummary`, `ApplicationDetail`, `ApplicationListResponse`, `ApplicationDocumentSummary`, `ApplicationStageHistoryEntry`, `MoveApplicationStageInput`, `RejectApplicationInput`, `WithdrawApplicationInput`, `ReopenApplicationInput`) under a new `applications` tag, codegen verified zero-diff across two consecutive runs. Internal DTOs freely expose internal ids (unlike W49's public DTOs) — this route requires authentication and `application.read`; candidate documents are surfaced as metadata only (filename/category/mime/size) — this workstream does not add a file-download/streaming endpoint. **Frontend:** `/applications` (list, candidate/stage filters, search, empty/error/loading states), `/applications/:id` (candidate info, current stage, move-stage control, reject/withdraw dialogs with optional reason code + comment, reopen action when terminal, document list, immutable history timeline), `/pipeline` (board view per selected vacancy — per the frozen plan's own frontend-impact line for this workstream — columns are the vacancy's own workflow stages via W44's existing `GET .../recruitment-workflows/:id/stages`, click-based card movement calling the same `move-stage` endpoint, not drag-and-drop: the frozen plan's own text explicitly allows "drag-or-click ... either way," and click avoids a new drag-and-drop dependency for one page). All three gated by `<ModuleGate moduleKey="recruitment">`, nav links ("Applications," "Pipeline Board") shown to `org_admin`/`hr_manager`. **Audit:** `application.stage_changed`/`.rejected`/`.withdrawn`/`.reopened` events recorded on every transition, mirroring the existing `job_requisition.*`/`vacancy.*` naming convention. **Database impact:** migration `0026_previous_adam_destine.sql` (one new table, purely additive) generated with a hand-authored `.down.sql`, not applied — confirmed zero further drift after generation. Backend: 22 new tests (`applicationPipeline.test.ts`) covering assigned/org-wide visibility tiers, tenant isolation, every transition (first-movement-from-null, regression, terminal-block, cross-workflow-stage rejection, missing-category-stage config errors, double-terminal 400s, reopen clearing reason codes), and permission/module gating. Frontend: 15 new tests (`applications.test.tsx`, `application-detail.test.tsx`) covering loading/error/empty states, candidate/stage rendering, status-conditional action visibility (non-terminal vs. terminal), and history/document rendering. Does not implement interview scheduling/scorecards, assessments, offers, hiring decisions, employee conversion, talent pools, background checks, recruiter messaging, or reporting dashboards — all remain later workstreams' scope. Does not touch W50 (still deferred) or close the outstanding W39 ESS scope, which remains open.
- **W50 — Candidate Accounts & Verification — Deferred, not completed (approved product decision, 2026-07-30).** Documentation-only reconciliation, no source changes — see `docs/PHASE_3A_RECRUITMENT_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`'s own W50 section for the full reasoning and the preserved original scope, marked there as `STATUS: DEFERRED — NOT IMPLEMENTED`. **Reason:** W49 (below) already delivers the minimum useful public recruitment product — public listing/detail, anonymous application submission, candidate persistence, consent capture, CV upload, and signed-token status checking. Candidate accounts (password auth, verification tokens, candidate sessions, password recovery, account-support obligations, anonymous-application linking) are not required to continue internal candidate/application processing, and would add meaningful authentication surface and support burden without a demonstrated need yet. **Existing candidate experience (unchanged, remains active):** every application is anonymous; there is no candidate account, password, login, or session anywhere in this codebase; a candidate checks their own application status only via the signed, time-limited `statusCheckToken` link emailed at submission (W49) — never a bare email lookup. **Deferred scope (preserved, not built):** `candidate_accounts` table, candidate-session middleware, a verification token flow, `/careers/:orgSlug/login`/`register`, `/candidate/*`. **Dependency reconciliation:** inspected the next workstream in the frozen plan's own ordering, W51 ("Application Pipeline & Stage Movement") — its `Dependencies` line already names **W49**, not W50, so it operates directly on W49's `candidates`/`applications`/`candidate_consents`/`candidate_documents` records and needs no candidate-account concept; no dependency language anywhere in the frozen plan required correction. W50 is not cancelled — it may be resumed later as its own workstream, triggered by demonstrated demand for reusable candidate profiles, authenticated dashboards, multi-application management from one account, self-service, saved jobs, or account-based communication preferences. **Architecture decision:** not separately recorded — this repository has no established ADR log or architecture-decision-record convention to append to (only informal, uncatalogued "ADR-NNN" citations appear inline within the phase-plan documents themselves, with no canonical source); the decision and its consequences are captured here and in the frozen plan's W50 section instead, per instruction not to invent a new documentation framework for one decision. **Next active workstream:** W51 — Application Pipeline & Stage Movement (frozen plan §23), unstarted.
- **W49 — Public Careers Portal (Read + Apply Shell) — Complete (full frozen scope; see scope note).** Unauthenticated public listing/detail plus a real, anonymous (no-account) application-submission pipeline. **Scope note — a deliberate escalation over this session's own initial instruction, confirmed with you first:** this session's own prompt initially described a narrower "shell" (no persistence, no file upload, no candidate data) and separately said "the frozen plan controls" on conflict. The frozen plan's actual W49 Objective/Scope (§23) is unambiguous — "the apply-submission pipeline," four new tables (`candidates`, `candidate_consents`, `candidate_documents`, `applications`), and §6's full security model (rate limiting, honeypot, real file upload through `documentValidation.ts`, consent capture, signed status-check tokens) — a real submission pipeline, not a shell. Asked directly which to build, you chose the full frozen scope; this entry reflects that. **Numbering:** per this session's explicit instruction, labeled "W49" to match the frozen document directly — see the Current Phase note above for why there is no session "W48." **Public tenant resolution:** `resolvePublicOrganization(slug)` (new `lib/publicCareers.ts`) resolves an organization by its own `organizations.slug` only — never a numeric ID — and collapses "doesn't exist," "suspended," and "careers not enabled" into the identical null/404 outcome, so no public request can distinguish which applied (§6's cross-tenant-disclosure rule extended to org existence itself). "Careers enabled" reuses W44's existing `recruitment_settings.enabled` + `externalRecruitmentEnabled` (read via the existing `getRecruitmentSettings`, unchanged) rather than the platform Module Registry's `organization_modules` — per the frozen plan's own §8 instruction that public routes check the former, not `requireModuleEnabled`. No `careersSlug` field exists on `recruitment_settings` (W44 never built one — the org's own `slug` already serves that purpose per §6's literal text), so none was added. **Vacancy eligibility** (`isVacancyPubliclyEligible`, applied identically to both the list and detail reads): `status = "published"`, `visibility != "internal"`, `openDate` not in the future, and `closeDate` not in the past — evaluated fresh on every read, never by mutating the stored vacancy (no background scheduler exists to flip status on close, W47's documented limitation, so a stale-but-still-`published` row past its own `closeDate` must still be filtered out live). The `openDate` check is a deliberate defense-in-depth addition beyond what internal `status` alone guarantees: W47's manual-flip publish action lets a staff operator deliberately go live internally before `openDate`; the public boundary enforces its own independent gate regardless, so that override affects internal/staff visibility only, never public. Public DTOs (`PublicVacancySummary`/`PublicVacancyDetail`) are hand-built, field-by-field projections — never the internal `Vacancy` type reused — structurally excluding the internal serial id, `requisitionId`, and salary (vacancies carry no salary field at all, and `job_requisitions.salaryRangeMin/Max/Currency` is explicitly documented "org-internal only, never public"); `departmentName`/`employmentType`/`workplaceType` are resolved through a batched (not N+1) lookup of the linked requisition and department, never exposing the requisition's own id or any other of its fields. **Public identifiers:** every public reference is `vacancies.publicId` (W47) or a new `applications.publicId` — both random tokens via the existing `generateToken()` convention (`auth.ts`), never the row's serial PK; `applications` also carries a *separate* `statusCheckToken`/`statusCheckTokenExpiresAt` (90-day TTL) — an ephemeral, re-emailable secret for the anonymous status-check link, deliberately distinct from the permanent `publicId`. **Apply pipeline** (new `lib/candidateApplications.ts`, `submitPublicApplication`): finds-or-creates a `candidates` row deduped by `(organizationId, lower(email))` (a functional unique index), then atomically (one `db.transaction`) inserts `applications` (unique on `(candidateId, vacancyId)` — a repeat submission from the same email to the same vacancy is idempotent, returning the existing row with no second write, exactly per §6), `candidate_consents` (privacy-notice-version + a text snapshot, immutable/append-only, never reinterpreted against a later version), and `candidate_documents` for the uploaded resume (`fileStorage.ts`'s existing `writeOrgFile` under a new `"candidate-documents"` org-scoped subdirectory, validated first by the same `documentValidation.ts` signature/size/type check every other upload in this codebase uses — PDF/JPEG/PNG/DOCX/XLSX, 10MB). `applicationLimitPerCandidate` (W44) is enforced by a scoped-`WHERE`-then-`.length` count in application code, not a SQL `count()` aggregate — mirrors this codebase's established "scoped WHERE, filter/reduce in JS" convention (the same reasoning W40's dashboard metrics already documented) over introducing a new query pattern. On a genuinely new submission, a status-check email is sent via the existing Resend `EmailProvider` (reused unchanged from the forgot-password flow, W19); delivery failure is logged, never surfaced to the caller (mirrors `requestPasswordReset`'s exact discipline). **Deliberately not enforced in this workstream:** `reapplicationWaitingDays` and `duplicateCandidatePolicy` (both W44 settings) are read and stored but have no terminal application state to act on yet — nothing in this workstream can mark an application rejected/withdrawn (that begins with W51, Application Pipeline & Stage Movement) — so both are wired through for a later workstream to start honoring, not silently dropped. `applications.currentStageId` is likewise defined now (matching the frozen table's full shape) but always `null` — resolving an initial workflow stage is pipeline logic, not submission logic; every application in this workstream reports a simple "submitted" status, not a stage-category-derived one. **Security:** the apply endpoint is rate-limited (5/15min per IP, stricter than `/auth/login`'s 10/15min) given the larger file-upload payload; a hidden honeypot field ("website") returns the identical success response with nothing persisted when filled, never revealing detection to an automated submitter; the anonymous status-check endpoint is separately rate-limited (20/15min) against token brute-forcing and is strictly scoped to the organization resolved from the URL's own slug — a token belonging to a different organization is indistinguishable from an unknown one (closed as a real gap found and fixed during this workstream, before any test was written against it). No public route ever accepts or returns a numeric organization/vacancy/application ID. **Database:** migration `0025_dashing_wolverine.sql` (`candidates`, `candidate_consents`, `candidate_documents`, `applications` — four new tables, purely additive) generated with a hand-authored `.down.sql`, not applied — confirmed zero further drift after generation. **API:** `GET /careers/:orgSlug`, `GET /careers/:orgSlug/vacancies` (search/department/location/employmentType/workplaceType filters, bounded `pageSize` ≤ 50), `GET /careers/:orgSlug/jobs/:vacancyPublicId`, `POST /careers/:orgSlug/jobs/:vacancyPublicId/apply` (multipart/form-data), `GET /careers/:orgSlug/application-status/:token` — none composes `requireAuth`/`requireMembership`/`requireModuleEnabled` (the first routes in this codebase that don't); new OpenAPI paths/schemas (`PublicOrganization`, `PublicVacancySummary`/`PublicVacancyDetail`, `PublicVacancyListResponse`, `ApplicationSubmittedResponse`, `ApplicationStatusResponse`) under a new `public-careers` tag, codegen verified zero-diff across two consecutive runs. **Frontend:** new standalone pages (no `<AppShell>`, never wrapped in `SecureRoute`, mirroring `reset-password.tsx`/`invite-accept.tsx`'s existing precedent) — `/careers/:orgSlug` (branding header, search/filters, vacancy cards, pagination, empty/error/loading states), `/careers/:orgSlug/jobs/:vacancyPublicId` (public-safe detail, Apply CTA), `/careers/:orgSlug/jobs/:vacancyPublicId/apply` (the form: name/email/phone/resume upload/consent checkbox/hidden honeypot, re-resolves the vacancy server-side, shows a real, non-misleading confirmation only after the API confirms persistence — this is not a no-op shell), `/careers/:orgSlug/status/:token` (anonymous status lookup). Also fixed a genuine pre-existing test-infrastructure gap while building these: added a `ResizeObserver` stub to the shared frontend test setup (`src/test/setup.ts`), alongside the existing Pointer Events stubs — no prior test had mounted a Radix `Checkbox` outside a closed dialog, so nothing had exercised the gap before this page. **Audit/Notifications:** no audit events for anonymous page views (none required by the frozen scope); the status-check email is the only outbound message, reusing existing infrastructure exactly as the frozen plan specifies, not a new notification system. Backend: 33 new tests (`publicCareers.test.ts`) covering org resolution (unknown/suspended/careers-disabled, all collapsing to the same 404), every vacancy-hidden case (draft/scheduled/paused/closed/archived/internal-only/future-open-date/past-close-date), cross-tenant isolation on both the vacancy list and the status-check token, public DTO field exclusion, the honeypot no-op, resume signature validation, the idempotent-duplicate-submission path, `applicationLimitPerCandidate` enforcement, and rate-limiter wiring. - **W47 — Vacancy Management Foundation — Complete (scope note below).** The postable unit produced from an approved job requisition — internal CRUD and lifecycle only, no public careers exposure, candidate, or application logic exists yet, per the frozen plan's exclusion list for this workstream. **Scope note:** per this session's explicit numbering, this "W47" corresponds to the frozen document's own §23 W48 ("Vacancies") — the numbering shift recorded in the four prior sessions' notes (W43/W44/W45/W46) continues consistently; the next workstream (session "W48") corresponds to the frozen document's own W49 ("Public Careers Portal (Read + Apply Shell)"). **Status model — deliberate, transparent simplification:** the frozen plan's §4.2 vacancy status model is `draft -> pending_approval (if the org requires vacancy-level approval, otherwise skipped) -> scheduled -> published -> paused <-> published -> closed -> archived`, plus `cancelled` as a terminal exit from any pre-closed state. The frozen `recruitment_settings` field list (§9) has no `vacancyApprovalRequired` toggle — only `requisitionApprovalRequired`/`offerApprovalRequired` exist — mirroring the same kind of gap W46 already documented for its own delegated-approver tier, so `pending_approval` is omitted entirely here. The frozen compact workstream entry and its own API list expose only publish/pause/close/archive, no separate cancel action, so `cancelled` is folded into `closed` — the single terminal exit from any pre-closed state (draft/scheduled/published/paused), reached via the one `close` action the API plan defines. **Publish semantics:** the initial publish from `draft` weighs `openDate` — goes straight to `published` when unset or not in the future, otherwise becomes `scheduled` (no background scheduler exists in this phase, per the frozen plan's own note). Calling publish again on an already-`scheduled` vacancy always flips it live immediately (the manual operator flip), and the same action resumes a `paused` vacancy straight back to `published` — reusing one action for both directions since the frozen API plan defines no separate resume action. **Database:** new `vacancies` table (`requisitionId` restrict-FK to `job_requisitions`, `workflowId` nullable FK to `recruitment_workflows`, `publicId` — a unique token via the existing `generateToken()` convention from auth.ts, reserved for a later public careers workstream and not consumed here — `title`, `visibility` enum internal/external/both, `status` enum per above, `openingsCount`, `filledCount` always 0 and never client-settable, `openDate`/`closeDate` as `timestamptz`, `jobDescription`/`responsibilities`/`requirements`/`preferredQualifications`, `seoTitle`/`seoDescription`, `featured`), `vacancy_locations` (`vacancyId` cascade, nullable `branchId` for an existing branch or free-text `label` for e.g. "Remote"), `vacancy_questions` (`vacancyId` cascade, `questionText`, `questionType` enum text/yes_no/multiple_choice/numeric, `isKnockout`, nullable `expectedAnswer`, `displayOrder`, active/archived) — `organizationId` denormalized on both child tables, mirroring `recruitment_stages.ts`'s established convention for tables scoped only via a parent FK. **Locations/questions are nested fields on the vacancy payload, not separate CRUD endpoints** — a deliberate scope narrowing: the frozen plan's §10 API Plan lists only `GET/POST/PATCH .../vacancies[/:id]` plus the four lifecycle actions, no `.../locations` or `.../questions` sub-routes, and the frontend plan describes one editor page ("description, questions, locations, publish controls"), not separate sub-resource screens — create/update replaces the full location/question set transactionally when provided. **Creation gating:** a vacancy can only be created from a requisition whose `status = "approved"` — every other status (draft/pending_approval/rejected/cancelled/closed/partially_filled/filled) is rejected with 400; the requisition's organization ownership is independently re-verified via `assertBelongsToOrganization` (never trusted from the request body alone), matching Architecture Principle 5. **Visibility:** the frozen plan's §7 permission matrix marks only "Assigned" and "Org-wide" for Vacancies (no "Own" tier, unlike Requisitions) — a vacancy carries no `recruiterId`/`hiringManagerId` of its own, so the assigned tier is resolved through the linked requisition's `recruiterEmployeeId`/`hiringManagerEmployeeId` (a batch lookup, not N+1); a vacancy invisible to the caller returns 404 for both list-exclusion and direct `GET .../:id`, identical to Requisitions' non-probeable-403-vs-404 discipline. **Permissions:** `vacancy.read` (seeded to every role, mirrors `requisition.read`'s reasoning — any employee could be the assigned recruiter/hiring manager on the linked requisition), `vacancy.manage` (create/update), `vacancy.publish` (publish/pause), `vacancy.close` (close/archive) — the latter three org_admin/hr_manager/super_admin only, mirroring `requisition.create`/`.update`/`.cancel`'s exact rollout. **API:** `GET/POST .../vacancies`, `GET/PATCH .../vacancies/:id` (PATCH only while `status = draft`, mirroring `job_requisitions`' exact PATCH-only-draft convention — `status`/`filledCount`/`publicId`/audit fields structurally absent from the request schema), `POST .../vacancies/:id/publish`, `.../pause`, `.../close`, `.../archive` — all 404/400-on-invalid-transition, new OpenAPI paths/schemas (`Vacancy`, `VacancyListResponse`, `CreateVacancyInput`, `UpdateVacancyInput`, `VacancyLocation(Input)`, `VacancyQuestion(Input)`), codegen verified zero-diff after generation. **Frontend:** new `/vacancies` (list, filters, create-from-approved-requisition dialog) and `/vacancies/:id/edit` (single editor + detail page: read-only details/locations/questions cards, a draft-only edit dialog covering description/openings/featured/locations/questions, and status-conditional publish/pause/close/archive actions) pages, `<ModuleGate moduleKey="recruitment">`, nav link ("Vacancies") shown to `org_admin`/`hr_manager`. **Audit:** `vacancy.created`/`.updated`/`.published`/`.paused`/`.closed`/`.archived` events recorded on every write and lifecycle transition, mirroring the existing `job_requisition.*` event naming convention. **Database impact:** migration `0024_salty_wither.sql` (three new tables + three new enums, purely additive) generated with a hand-authored `.down.sql`, not applied — confirmed zero further drift after generation. Backend: 37 new tests (`vacancies.test.ts`) covering creation gating on every non-approved requisition status, cross-org requisition/workflow/branch reference validation, nested location/question creation, assigned/org-wide visibility tiers, tenant isolation, draft-only PATCH, every lifecycle transition (including the scheduled-vs-published openDate branching and the paused-resume direction), concurrent double-publish/double-close 400s, and permission/module gating. Frontend: 15 new tests (`vacancies.test.tsx`, `vacancy-editor.test.tsx`) covering the list's loading/error/empty states and detail linking, and the editor's status-conditional action visibility (draft/published/paused/closed/archived) and locations/questions rendering. - **W46 — Requisition Approval Workflow — Complete (scope note below).** Controls the transition of a submitted job requisition from `pending_approval` to `approved`/`rejected`. **Scope note:** per this session's explicit numbering, this "W46" corresponds to the frozen document's own §23 W47 ("Requisition Approval Workflow") — the numbering shift recorded in the three prior sessions' notes (W43/W44/W45) continues consistently; the next workstream (session "W47") corresponds to the frozen document's own W48 ("Vacancies"). **Approval model — deliberate, transparent simplification:** the frozen plan's §7 permission matrix names both an "assigned" tier (recruiter/hiring manager, "where explicitly delegated") and an organization-wide tier for `requisition.approve`. No delegated-approver assignment mechanism exists anywhere in Recruitment (W43–45 built none), so this workstream implements the organization-wide tier only — any `requisition.approve` holder (`org_admin`/`hr_manager`/`super_admin`) may decide any pending requisition in the organization; a future workstream can add a delegated tier without changing the table shape. A single required approval step per requisition (sequence 1) is used, mirroring W35's single-level transactional decision pattern exactly — not a generic multi-step workflow engine. **Database:** new `requisition_approvals` table (`requisitionId`, `sequence` — always 1 today, present for a future multi-step extension without a schema change — `approverMembershipId` resolved at decision time not pre-assigned, `decision` enum pending/approved/rejected, `decidedAt`, `comment`), `(requisitionId, sequence)` unique (structural duplicate-instance guard), indexed for pending-lookup. Rows are mutated in place from pending to a final decision and never touched again — immutable once decided, enforced structurally (the conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE decision = 'pending'` finds nothing once decided). **Submission integration:** `jobRequisitions.ts`'s `submitJobRequisition` now creates the single pending approval step inside the same `db.transaction` as the `draft → pending_approval` status update — a requisition can never be `pending_approval` without an active approval instance, and the existing conditional-update + unique-index pair together prevent a concurrent or repeated submit from ever creating two. **Decisions:** `approveJobRequisition`/`rejectJobRequisition` (new `lib/requisitionApprovals.ts`) each run a transactional conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE decision = 'pending'` on the approval row followed by a conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE status = 'pending_approval'` on the requisition row, both inside one transaction — a concurrent double-decision, or an approve/reject race, sees zero rows affected on the second attempt and fails as `RequisitionApprovalNotPendingError` (409), never double-processing; approval is immediately final since there is only one step. Rejection reason/comment is optional on both actions, mirroring W35's `rejectionReason` precedent exactly (not a frozen requirement to make it mandatory). No reopening/resubmission of a rejected requisition — out of this workstream's scope, per instruction. **Permissions:** one new key, `requisition.approve`, seeded to `org_admin`/`hr_manager`/`super_admin` — same rollout as `requisition.update` (mirrors the org-wide-only approver model above); approval history reuses the existing `requisition.read` permission plus the same visibility tiers `GET .../job-requisitions/:id` already established (own/assigned/department/branch/organization-wide) — a requisition invisible to the caller returns 404 for its approval history too, same non-probeable-403-vs-404 discipline. **API:** `GET .../job-requisitions/pending-approvals` (org-wide inbox, `requisition.approve`-gated, registered before the `/:id` route so Express doesn't swallow the literal segment as an `:id` param), `GET .../job-requisitions/:id/approvals` (immutable history, `requisition.read`-gated + same visibility), `POST .../job-requisitions/:id/approve`, `POST .../job-requisitions/:id/reject` (both `requisition.approve`-gated, optional `comment` body, 404/409 responses) — new OpenAPI paths/schemas (`RequisitionApproval`, `ApproveJobRequisitionInput`, `RejectJobRequisitionInput`), codegen verified zero-diff after generation. **Frontend:** new `/requisition-approvals` inbox page (list, approve, reject-with-optional-comment dialog, empty/loading/error states), nav-gated to `org_admin`/`hr_manager` (UX convenience; the server-side permission is the real gate); `/requisitions/:id` gains Approve/Reject actions (visible only while `pending_approval`) and an Approval History card (rendered only when history exists), both reusing the page's existing conflict-toast pattern for a 409. **Audit:** `job_requisition.approved`/`job_requisition.rejected` events recorded on decision (mirrors the existing `job_requisition.*` event naming already used for created/updated/submitted/cancelled/archived) — no separate "workflow created"/"completed" events, since a single-step chain's creation and completion are already implicit in the existing `job_requisition.submitted` event and the new approved/rejected events respectively. **Database impact:** migration `0023_rich_romulus.sql` (one new table + one new enum, purely additive) generated with a hand-authored `.down.sql`, not applied — confirmed zero further drift after generation. Backend: 18 new tests (`requisitionApprovals.test.ts`) covering pending-approvals inbox scoping/tenant-isolation, approval-history visibility/404 parity, approve/reject success, immutable-decision and duplicate/concurrent-decision 409s (including an approve/reject race), and permission/module gating; `jobRequisitions.test.ts` updated (submit now creates the pending approval step transactionally) with a `db.transaction` mock added, all 23 existing tests still passing. Frontend: 10 new tests (`requisition-approvals.test.tsx`, plus additions to `requisition-detail.test.tsx`) covering the inbox's loading/error/empty states, approve/reject actions, status-conditional action visibility, and approval-history rendering. Does not implement a delegated-approver tier, multi-step sequential chains, reopening/resubmission, vacancies, candidates, applications, or any later workstream's scope.
- **W45 — Job Requisition Foundation — Complete.** An organization-scoped request/authorization to recruit for one or more openings — the record and its lifecycle only; no approval execution, vacancy, candidate, or application logic exists yet, per the frozen plan's exclusion list for this workstream. **Scope note:** per this session's explicit numbering, this "W45" corresponds to the frozen document's original W46 ("Job Requisitions") — the numbering shift recorded in the prior two sessions' notes (W43/W44) continues consistently; the next workstream (session "W46") corresponds to the frozen document's original W47 ("Requisition Approval Workflow"). **Database:** new `job_requisitions` table (`title`, `requisitionType` — new_role/replacement/temporary/internship/volunteer/contract/ministry — `positionId`/`departmentId`/`branchId`/`hiringManagerEmployeeId`/`recruiterEmployeeId`, all nullable; `requestedHeadcount`, `filledCount` always 0 and never client-settable; `employmentType` reuses the existing `employees.employmentType` enum unchanged; a new `workplaceType` enum — onsite/remote/hybrid; `expectedStartDate`; recruitment-scoped `salaryRangeMin`/`Max`/`Currency`, never a payroll dependency; `replacementEmployeeId`; a full 8-value `status` enum defined now — draft/pending_approval/approved/rejected/partially_filled/filled/cancelled/closed — even though this workstream only ever writes draft/pending_approval/cancelled/closed, so a later ALTER TYPE is never needed once approval execution and fulfillment land; `cancellationReason`; `createdBy`/`updatedBy`, doubling as "requested by" — no separate column, same as `employees.createdBy` already does). **Lifecycle:** create (always `draft`) → submit (`draft → pending_approval`, a conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE status = 'draft'` mirroring W35's exact idempotency shape — a concurrent double-submit sees zero rows affected and fails, never double-processing) → cancel (`draft`/`pending_approval` → `cancelled`, with an optional reason) → archive (`draft`/`cancelled` → `closed`, this workstream's "Closure," per the frozen plan's §3.2 JOB REQUISITIONS field list). General `PATCH` is only permitted while `status = draft`; `filledCount`/`status`/audit fields are structurally impossible to set through it (absent from the request schema entirely, not merely ignored). **Validation:** every FK (`position`/`department`/`branch`/`hiringManager`/`recruiter`/`replacementEmployee`) independently re-verified to belong to the caller's organization via `assertBelongsToOrganization` (unchanged); `requestedHeadcount` must be positive; `filledCount` (always 0 today) validated to never exceed it, ready for when a later workstream starts incrementing it; salary min/max ordering and currency-required-with-range; `replacementEmployeeId` required if and only if `requisitionType = replacement`. **Authorization/visibility:** new `requisition.read` (seeded to every role, mirrors `leave_request.approve`'s precedent — any employee could be a requisition's assigned recruiter or hiring manager) plus `requisition.create`/`.update`/`.cancel` (org_admin/hr_manager only, mirrors `leave_type.manage`'s rollout). Read visibility is tiered in the service layer using W43's authorization primitives unchanged: organization-wide for `requisition.update` holders; otherwise scoped to requisitions the caller requested (`createdBy`), is the assigned recruiter or hiring manager on (`isAssignedRecruitmentActor`), or shares a department/branch with (`isSameDepartmentScope`/`isSameBranchScope`) — a requisition that exists but isn't visible returns 404, identical to one that doesn't exist, so visibility can never be probed via a 403-vs-404 difference. **API:** `GET/POST .../job-requisitions`, `GET/PATCH .../job-requisitions/:id`, `.../submit`, `.../cancel`, `.../archive` — list supports `status`/`requisitionType`/`department`/`branch`/`hiringManager`/`recruiter`/`search` filters plus `page`/`pageSize` (visibility-filtered in application code, then paginated, mirroring `leaveCalendar.ts`'s established "scoped WHERE, filter/reduce in JS" convention — no new query pattern). **Frontend:** new `/requisitions` (list, filters, create dialog) and `/requisitions/:id` (detail, edit-while-draft, submit/cancel/archive actions gated by current status) pages, `<ModuleGate moduleKey="recruitment">`, nav links shown to `org_admin`/`hr_manager`. **Database impact:** migration `0022_productive_talkback.sql` (one new table + three new enums, purely additive) generated with a hand-authored `.down.sql`, not applied — confirmed zero further drift after generation. Backend: 23 new tests (`jobRequisitions.test.ts`) covering module/permission gating, every validation rule, all four visibility tiers, tenant isolation, and every lifecycle transition including the concurrent-double-submit idempotency case. Frontend: 12 new tests (`requisitions.test.tsx`, `requisition-detail.test.tsx`) covering loading/error/empty states, list rendering and detail linking, and status-conditional action visibility. ## Phase 3A Completion Report (W63)

All 19 executed frozen workstreams (W43–W47, W49, W51–W62; W50 formally deferred, not executed) are complete, verified in W62, and closed out by this report. Checking against `docs/PHASE_3A_RECRUITMENT_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` §24's Phase Acceptance Criteria, item by item:

- **Every workstream (W43–W62) satisfies its own acceptance criteria.** Yes — each entry in the Phase 3A Progress section above states what was built and how it was verified; W62 re-confirmed all of it still holds together as a whole.
- **Documentation matches implementation.** Yes, as of this report — that is this workstream's (W63's) job.
- **The repository builds successfully and all tests pass.** Yes — W62: 706 backend + 234 frontend tests pass; `api-server`, `hrms`, and `mockup-sandbox` production builds all succeed.
- **No destructive migration risk remains; every migration generated, none applied without your explicit approval.** Yes — migrations `0021`–`0034` (thirty new tables total, detailed below) are purely additive, each with a hand-authored `.down.sql`; none have been applied to any database. W60 and W61 correctly generated no migration at all (pure read models / reuse of already-shipped tables).
- **OpenAPI and generated clients are synchronized.** Yes — W62: zero-diff `orval codegen` across two consecutive runs; all 63 Recruitment routes reconciled 1:1 against `openapi.yaml`, no route missing either direction.
- **Multi-tenant isolation, the permission matrix (§7), module gating (§8), and own-resource authorization are verified for every new entity and route.** Yes — W62's dedicated verification pass, detailed in the Security Verification section below.
- **Public careers routes are confirmed rate-limited, non-leaking on failure, and incapable of cross-tenant disclosure.** Yes — W62 re-read `publicCareers.ts` directly: every route independently resolves its organization by slug, every not-found/not-eligible case returns a generic 404 rather than distinguishing "doesn't exist" from "exists but not visible," and `applyRateLimiter`/`statusCheckRateLimiter` remain in place from W49.
- **The `recruitment` module is live-verified: an enabled org sees the feature, a disabled org gets the designed unavailable state, never a partial or broken page, and disabling the module never deletes or corrupts existing recruitment data.** Verified at the code level for every workstream (W62: `requireModuleEnabled("recruitment")` composed on every non-public internal route, `<ModuleGate moduleKey="recruitment">` on every internal frontend route, ESS's internal-vacancies/My Applications sections degrade independently per W60) — **no live browser walkthrough was performed**, since no provisioned development database or browser environment exists in this environment; this is a code-level, test-suite-backed confirmation, not a live-environment one.
- **The Phase 3A Completion Report (this report) declares zero remaining blockers, or lists them explicitly, and explicitly does not claim the outstanding W39 scope (§22) as resolved.** Declared below.

### Executive Summary

Phase 3A delivered a complete, configurable Recruitment & Hiring module end to end: requisition → approval → vacancy → public/internal application → screening/scoring → pipeline movement → interviews → scorecards → reference/background checks → offers → pre-employment requirements → employee conversion, plus talent pools, candidate notes/tags, an internal (ESS) application path, and read-only dashboard/reporting — on top of the completed Foundation (W1–W21), Phase 2A Core Employee Domain (W22–W31), and Phase 2B HR Operations (W32–W42). Nineteen workstreams (W43–W47, W49, W51–W61) each shipped independently reviewed and tested; W62 verified the phase as a whole; W63 (this report) closes it. W50 (Candidate Accounts & Verification) was a deliberate, approved product decision to defer, not a skip — the anonymous-applicant/signed-status-check experience W49 already delivers remains the fully supported path, and nothing built in W51–W61 needed anything from W50.

**Numbering note (preserved from the Phase 3A Progress section above):** sessions building W45–W47 used a numbering one behind the frozen document's own; a later session was explicitly instructed to align directly with the frozen document's numbering — "W49," not "W48" — so there is no session "W48": the frozen document's own W48 ("Vacancies") is exactly this phase's W47. From W49 onward, session numbering and the frozen document's numbering are identical.
